turns.en: Most people will miss the biggest opportunity of their lifetime because they're looking for certainty instead of taking action.
turns.zh: 大多数人都会错过一生中最大的机遇，因为他们追求确定性而非采取行动。

turns.en: There's never been a better time to be an inventor and a pioneer than right now because the world is on fire with new ideas, with AI and space opportunities. We're in the middle of multiple golden ages right now. What are you going to do? When are you going to start doing it?
turns.zh: 现在做一名发明家和先驱的时机从未如此之好——世界正因新想法而沸腾，AI 和太空机遇层出不穷。我们正身处多重黄金时代。你打算做什么？你什么时候开始？

turns.en: Only action matters.
turns.zh: 只有行动才重要。

turns.en: Every generation gets a new tool that changes the rules, and AI happens to be yours.
turns.zh: 每一代人都会得到改变规则的新工具，而 AI 恰好是你们的。

turns.en: Whether you want to start a company or be a programmer, the ability for one person to use these tools and have great ideas and implement them with what would have taken decades of experience or teams of people is really quite remarkable.
turns.zh: 无论你想创业还是做程序员，一个人利用这些工具，产生好点子并付诸实施——而这些原本需要数十年的经验或团队支持——这种能力真的非常了不起。

turns.en: The companies that will succeed in this transition period will be the ones that most effectively use AI. So,
turns.zh: 在这个过渡期，能成功的公司将是那些最有效利用 AI 的公司。所以，

turns.en: if you're doing something and making maximum use of AI and you're competing against someone who is not, you will win.
turns.zh: 如果你在做某件事时最大化使用 AI，而你的竞争对手没有，你就会赢。

turns.en: If you wait until everything feels safe, someone else will build the future that you could have created. So, in the next 3 hours you'll learn the principles the world's greatest entrepreneurs use to create wealth and how AI is opening even bigger opportunities for you today.
turns.zh: 如果你等到一切感觉安全，别人就会建造你本可以创造的未来。所以，在接下来的 3 个小时里，你将学到世界最伟大企业家创造财富的原则，以及 AI 如今如何为你打开更大的机遇。

turns.en: If you've been before, put a hashtag believe in the comments below so I can feature you here in a future video. And if you're new, welcome to Believe Nation, the only channel that helps you believe in yourself daily one video at a time. Believe.
turns.zh: 如果你之前来过，请在下方评论中加上 #believe，这样我就能在未来的视频中推荐你。如果你是新人，欢迎来到 Believe Nation，这是唯一一个每天通过一个视频帮助你相信自己的频道。相信。

turns.en: This is the first moment in history where one person and a laptop can out-earn an entire company.
turns.zh: 这是历史上第一次，一个人加一台笔记本电脑就能赚得比整个公司还多。

turns.en: We might have AI that is smarter than any human by the end of this year.
turns.zh: 我们可能在今年年底之前拥有比任何人类都聪明的 AI。

turns.en: This could be very significant productivity in the economy.
turns.zh: 这可能会带来经济上非常显著的生产力提升。

turns.en: AI is the biggest technical thing ever in my lifetime. I mean, it is so profound.
turns.zh: AI 是我这辈子遇到的最重大的技术变革。我的意思是，它如此深远。

turns.en: You've got the smartest business partner ever built ready to work all day for about 20 bucks a month and you haven't even opened it yet. People who actually use Claude are finishing complex college-level work around 12 times faster than the ones grinding through it all by themselves. And the people winning right now are starting with less than what you have today. The only thing that's in your way is the decision to begin. Let me tell you about a guy named Peter Levels. Back in 2014, he was in his late 20s, bouncing around the world with barely any money coming in, watching his savings shrink every single month. He didn't have a degree, he didn't have a rich uncle, he didn't have a safety net. He was just a scared guy who was running out of cash. So, he made a wild promise to himself. I love this. 12 startups in 12 months. One brand new product every month, whether he's ready or not. And most of them flopped completely. Then one hit. It was called Nomad List. It was a site for people who travel and work online. It grew to millions of visitors. Then he created Remote OK, and that became one of the biggest remote job boards on the planet. And then in February 2023, he built a little tool that was called Photo AI. And here you upload a few of your selfies and it creates professional photos of you using AI. Its first week it made about $5,000. 18 months later, it was pulling in more than $130,000 every single month. And the best part is this. Peter had no employees, he had no office, he had no investors, he had no team. It was him, a laptop, and AI doing most of the heavy lifting. One person, more than 40 products, over $200,000 a month. He started before he felt ready. He was broke and scared. And the work turned him into the guy who could win. Okay.
turns.zh: 你拥有了有史以来最聪明的商业伙伴，每天工作，每月只需 20 美元，而你甚至还没打开它。实际使用 Claude 的人完成复杂的大学级作业的速度，比独自苦干的人快约 12 倍。而现在赢的人，起点比你今天拥有的还少。唯一阻碍你的是开始的决心。让我给你讲一个叫 Peter Levels 的人。2014 年，他 20 多岁，在全球漂泊，收入微薄，看着积蓄逐月减少。他没有学历，没有富有的叔叔，没有安全网。他只是一个害怕、快没钱的家伙。于是，他对自己做了一个疯狂承诺——我喜欢这个——12 个月做 12 家初创公司。每个月一个全新产品，不管他准备好没有。其中大多数彻底失败。然后一个成功了，叫 Nomad List，一个为旅行和在线工作的人服务的网站，访问量达到数百万。接着他创建了 Remote OK，成为全球最大的远程工作板之一。然后在 2023 年 2 月，他做了一个小工具叫 Photo AI，你上传几张自拍，它就用 AI 为你生成专业照片。第一周就赚了约 5000 美元。18 个月后，每月收入超过 13 万美元。最棒的是：Peter 没有员工、没有办公室、没有投资者、没有团队。就他一个人、一台笔记本电脑，AI 完成大部分重活。一个人，40 多个产品，月入超过 20 万美元。他在感觉自己准备好之前就开始了。他身无分文、充满恐惧。而工作把他变成了能赢的人。好了。

turns.en: Now, you might be thinking, 'Okay, Evan, that's great for him, but he's a coder. I'm not technical. I don't even know where to start. And honestly, I'm worried that AI is going to replace me in my job or in my business before I even make a dollar from it.' And I understand. This year, Claude is the coder. The skill that matters most is actually spotting the problem and just pointing Claude at it. You find someone that is hurting enough to pay to make that problem go away, and Claude helps you handle the bill. What leaves people behind is just waiting to feel ready, and ready is not real. So, you don't need to wait for permission, you don't need to wait to feel ready, we just need to start. One tiny step. The opportunity in front of you is bigger than any skill gap you think you have, and I'm going to show you exactly how to grab it. Nobody wants AI, they want their problem gone. Okay, so here's the first thing that we want to burn into our brain. People do not pay for AI, they pay to make a painful, expensive problem disappear. A business owner that's bleeding customers at 11:00 p.m. when nobody's there to answer the phone or emails just wants that to stop. A realtor who's stuck writing listings for 3 hours wants those 3 hours back. So, your job is to find that kind of problem and then kill it with Claude. The best place to look is your own pain. I think your purpose comes from your pain. So, the stuff that frustrated you in your old job, the headaches in your own life, those are the exact problems that other people will pay you to take away for them. So, you already know where it hurts, so that's where you start. And let's talk about just giving yourself permission. It's okay to want the money. Your mission comes first, but if money is sitting at number 100 on your list, you'll always be doing part-time things nights and weekends forever. So, keep money in your top five, and then get specific. So, we're not helping small businesses, pick dentists, pick plumbers, pick real estate agents in one city. Find the single task they hate, the one that eats their week up, and then point Claude straight at it. So, I teach my team a simple filter, eliminate, automate, delegate. The job a busy owner would kill to get off their plate is the one that you get paid to take out. And when you reach out, never leave with the word AI, say, 'I'll handle your follow-up emails so you stop losing leads.' Or say, 'I'll give you back 10 hours of your week.' That's what a busy person, a busy entrepreneur, they pull out their credit card for. So, get this right, and five people with the same problem and a credit card is enough to start a real business. If you can solve a real problem, then you must go offer it. Somebody out there is stuck tonight on the exact thing that you could fix tomorrow with Claude sitting right next to you. Sell a service before you build a startup. Now for the fastest way to put money in your pocket this week, sell a service where Claude does the heavy lifting and you keep the money. The biggest, most boring gold mine right now is automating the busy work that drowns every small business.
turns.zh: 现在你可能会想：“好吧，Evan，对他来说很好，但他是个程序员。我不懂技术，甚至不知道从哪里开始。老实说，我担心在我从 AI 上赚到一分钱之前，AI 就会取代我的工作或生意。”我理解。今年，Claude 就是程序员。最重要的技能其实是发现问题，然后把 Claude 指向它。你找到那些痛苦到愿意付钱解决问题的人，Claude 帮你搞定。让人落后的就是等待“准备好”，而“准备好”并不真实。所以你不需要等待许可，不需要等待感觉准备好了，我们只需要开始。一小步。你面前的机遇比你自认为的任何技能差距都要大，我将向你展示如何抓住它。没人想要 AI，他们想要问题消失。好，这是我们要深深记住的第一件事：人们不为 AI 付费，他们付费是为了让痛苦且昂贵的麻烦消失。一个在晚上 11 点客户流失却无人接电话或回邮件的老板，只想让这种情况停止。一个花 3 小时写房源的房产中介，想要那 3 小时回来。所以你的工作就是找到那种问题，然后用 Claude 消灭它。最好的方法是看你自己的痛苦。我认为你的使命来自你的痛苦。所以，你在旧工作中感到沮丧的事情，你自己生活中的头痛问题，正是别人会付钱让你帮他们消除的。你已经知道哪里痛，就从那里开始。我们来谈谈给自己许可。想赚钱是可以的。使命第一，但如果钱在你清单上排第 100 位，你就永远只能晚上和周末做兼职。所以把钱放在前五，然后具体化。我们不帮所有小企业，选牙医、水管工、房产中介，选一个城市。找出他们讨厌的单一任务，那个占据他们一周的任务，然后把 Claude 直接对准它。我教我的团队一个简单的筛选：消除、自动化、委托。一个忙碌老板拼命想甩掉的工作，就是你赚钱去解决的事。当你联系时，永远别提 AI，说“我来处理你的跟进邮件，这样你就不会丢失线索”，或者“我给你每周省出 10 小时”。这就是忙碌的人、忙碌的企业家会掏信用卡的理由。所以做好这一点，五个有同样问题且有信用卡的人就足够开始一个真正的生意。如果你能解决一个真实问题，你就必须去提供它。今晚有人被困在某个事情上，明天你就能用 Claude 解决。在建立初创公司之前，先销售服务。现在最快本周把钱放进你口袋的方式是：销售一项服务，让 Claude 做重活，你拿钱。目前最大、最无聊的金矿就是自动化那些淹没每个小企业的琐碎工作。

turns.en: Think about what an owner does over and over again: chasing leads, answering the same customer questions, writing weekly reports and emails, newsletters, onboarding every new client by hand. It eats the hours they should be spending running the business. So you build a Claude-powered system that takes one of those jobs off their plate completely, then charge them to set it up plus a monthly fee to keep it running. And the demand is exploding. According to Fiverr's business trends data, searches from companies looking for freelancers who can build AI agents and automation jumped more than 18,000% in a single year. Businesses are hunting for someone to do exactly this, and most have no idea where to start. That someone can be you. And here's the beautiful part: you never touch the code. You sit with the owner for an hour, find the one task that wastes their week the most, map out exactly how it gets done step by step, understand their process, hand that to Claude, and it builds a system that runs it. You test it, fix what doesn't quite work, and hand them back hours of their life. To them, you're the person who gave them their time back, and that is worth real money to you. Being leads to doing. The moment you start showing up as the person who solved this, you start becoming that person, too.
turns.zh: 想想看，老板们日复一日地做什么？追线索、回答重复的客户问题、写周报和邮件、写通讯、手动迎接每一位新客户。这些事吞噬了他们本应用来经营公司的宝贵时间。所以，你打造一个 Claude 驱动的系统，把其中一项工作完全从他们肩上卸下，然后收取搭建费加月度维护费。需求正在爆发。根据 Fiverr 的商业趋势数据，企业寻找能构建 AI 智能体和自动化的自由职业者的搜索量，一年内暴涨超过 18,000%。企业正在疯狂寻找能做这件事的人，而大多数人根本不知道从何入手。那个人可以是你。最美好的是：你完全不用碰代码。你和老板坐下来聊一小时，找出最浪费他每周时间的一项任务，一步步描绘出完整的流程，了解他的工作方式，然后把它交给 Claude，它就能搭建一个系统来运行。你测试、修复不完美的地方，然后把他们生命中的时间还给他们。在他们眼里，你就是那个帮他们找回时间的人，而这对你来说就是真金白银。存在先于行动。当你开始以解决问题的人的身份出现，你也就真正成了那样的人。

turns.en: Okay, so how much can you make? A setup like this runs anywhere from a couple thousand dollars plus a monthly retainer to keep it humming, and one client can replace a whole paycheck. So, pick one painful, repetitive task that businesses in your niche all hate. Write one simple message and send it to 20 local businesses this week. Say, 'I'll answer your customers the second they reach out, day or night, so you never lose another sale.' That's a message a busy owner actually pays for. The tools are free or close to it—$20 a month. The only thing between you and your first client is a message that you have not sent yet. Build the thing in a weekend, not a year.
turns.zh: 好了，那么你能赚多少钱？这样一套系统通常收费几千美元，外加月费维持运行，一个客户就能抵得上整份薪水。所以，挑选一个你所在行业里所有企业都痛恨的重复性任务。写一条简单的消息，这周发给 20 家本地企业，说：‘我能在客户一联系你时就立即回复，不分昼夜，让你再也不错失任何销售机会。’ 这就是忙碌的老板愿意花钱买的消息。工具要么免费，要么接近免费——每月 20 美元。你和第一个客户之间，只差一条你还没发送的消息。用一周时间搭建，而不是一年。

turns.en: So once you have a little cash and you know what people need, then you start to really build. And this is where this year gets unfair in your favor. Building software used to take a team of engineers 6 months to 6 years to create. Now you describe what you want in plain English and Claude writes the code with you. They call it vibe coding, and it's how a lot of new software is getting built right now. Here's how you can do it without a computer science degree. Open Claude, describe the thing you want in plain English, plain words, like you're explaining it to a smart friend. Claude writes the actual code and hands you back a working version that you can click through and try out in a couple minutes, long before you put any real time or money into this thing. And when you're ready for the real thing—the version that runs a business—you can point Claude Code at your project and it builds, tests, and fixes the files for you. You test it, tell it what's broken, and it keeps patching and improving. You keep going until it works, then you connect simple services for sign-ups and payments. So you don't need an engineering team, you don't need a 6-month to 6-year timeline, just you and Claude. And it does not have to be the next big app. Most of the money is in the small, boring tools: a booking system for a local gym, a dashboard that pulls a contractor's numbers onto one screen, a little automation that saves a busy office an hour a day. Unglamorous problems that people will gladly pay to make disappear.
turns.zh: 一旦你有了点资金，知道了人们的需求，你就可以开始真正搭建了。这就是今年变得对你格外有利的地方。过去开发软件需要一个工程师团队花 6 个月到 6 年。现在，你用简单的英语描述需求，Claude 就和你一起写代码。这被称为‘氛围编码’，也是如今许多新软件的构建方式。没有计算机科学学位也能做到。打开 Claude，用简单英语描述你想要的，就像向一个聪明的朋友解释一样。Claude 会写出实际代码，并在几分钟内给你一个可点击试用的工作版本，远在你投入大量时间或金钱之前。当你准备好真正用于商业的版本时，你可以将 Claude Code 指向你的项目，它会为你构建、测试和修复文件。你测试，告诉它哪里有问题，它不断修补改进。你一直迭代直到它工作，然后连接简单的注册和支付服务。所以你不需要工程团队，不需要 6 个月到 6 年的时间线，只需要你和 Claude。而且它不一定要成为下一个大应用。大部分钱都在那些小而无聊的工具里：本地健身房的预订系统、将承包商数据汇集到一个屏幕上的仪表盘、为繁忙办公室每天节省一小时的自动化工具。那些不吸引人但人们愿意花钱解决的问题。

turns.en: Okay, now this is really important because this is where a lot of people are tempted to quit. Your first version is going to be pretty rough, pretty bad, right? Expect it to suck in the beginning—it's supposed to. Ship it anyway. Remember Peter? He shipped Photo AI rough and started charging in week one, then made it better while people were already paying. A boring tool making a little money beats your perfect app that lives in your head forever and never gets out into the world. The person who ships something ugly this weekend ends up miles ahead of the genius still planning their next step next year. A paper airplane isn't supposed to break the sound barrier either, right? But doing the impossible is exactly what you were here to do. So give yourself one weekend, pick the smallest version of your idea—the one thing it absolutely has to do—and build only that with Claude. Charge for it before it's pretty. You can always make it better once real people are paying you. Turn what you know into something that sells while you sleep.
turns.zh: 好了，这一点非常重要，因为很多人在这里会想放弃。你的第一个版本会相当粗糙、糟糕，对吧？接受它一开始很烂——它本来就该这样。不管怎样，先发布。还记得彼得吗？他发布了粗糙的 Photo AI 并在第一周就开始收费，然后在人们已经付费的同时把它做得更好。一个能赚点小钱的无聊工具，胜过你脑中永远存在却从未面世的完美应用。这个周末发布一个丑陋作品的人，会比那个明年还在计划下一步的天才领先一大截。纸飞机本来就不是用来突破音障的，对吧？但做到不可能的事正是你来到这里的意义。所以，给自己一个周末，选出你想法的最小版本——它绝对必须做的一件事——只用 Claude 构建它。在它变得漂亮之前就收费。一旦有真实用户付费，你随时可以改进它。把你所知道的变成你睡觉时也在卖的东西。

turns.en: Okay, so not everybody wants to run a service or build an app, and that's fine. Because there's a third door, and it might be the simplest one. You package what you know into small digital products and sell them over and over. Don't worry about the 200-page book that takes 40 hours and barely sells. What we're here to do is make tight, useful tools people can buy and apply in 5 minutes. A big one right now is called Prompt Packs. These are collections of proven instructions that get Claude to do a specific job really well, like writing sales emails for a dentist or planning a month of content for a coach. Makers sell these for around $17, and because it costs you nothing to make another copy, you keep 95% of every sale. You can go bigger too. A focused mini course that solves one specific problem sells for $47, and you can record it in an afternoon. Claude can even translate your product into other languages in minutes, so you can sell the same thing to people all over the world without learning a single new word. Put it up in a simple online store, and you're open for business. Prompt Packs are just a start. You can sell templates that do someone's boring setup for them, a planning system that runs their whole week, a swipe file of messages that actually get replies, a checklist that turns a 3-hour job into 20 minutes. Anything you had to figure out the hard way, you can hand to someone else for a small price. The magic is you build it once, then sell it thousands of times. It keeps selling while you sleep on a Saturday, on vacation, at 3:00 in the morning. You do the work once, and Claude helps you make it in an afternoon instead of a month. So think about what you already know that other people are struggling with right now. The things your friends always ask you for help with. The skill you might take for granted. That knowledge is worth real money, and now you finally have the tools to package it and sell it while you are sleeping. You're not too late, and you're not too small. You know what the best time to start was? Years ago. The second best time? Right now. Your first 10 customers are closer than you think. Now, the next worry creeps in.
turns.zh: 好了，不是每个人都想经营服务或构建应用，那也没关系。因为还有第三扇门，而且可能是最简单的一扇。把你所知道的东西打包成小型数字产品，反复销售。别担心那本花 40 小时却几乎卖不出去的 200 页书。我们要做的是紧凑实用的工具，人们可以在 5 分钟内购买并应用。现在一个大热门是提示包。这些都是经过验证的指令集，能让 Claude 出色地完成某项特定工作，比如为牙医写销售邮件，或为教练规划一个月的內容。制作者以大约 17 美元的价格出售，而且复制一份的成本为零，所以你能保留 95% 的销售额。你也可以做得更大。一个针对特定问题的迷你课程可以卖 47 美元，而且一个下午就能录好。Claude 甚至可以在几分钟内把你的产品翻译成其他语言，这样你无需学习一个新词就能向全世界销售同一产品。把它放在一个简单的在线商店里，你就可以开张了。提示包只是起点。你可以出售模板，帮别人完成繁琐的设置、规划整个星期的系统、一张能获得回复的消息模板集、将 3 小时工作变成 20 分钟的清单。任何你曾艰难摸索出来的东西，你都可以以低价交给别人。神奇之处在于，你只构建一次，然后可以销售上千次。它在你周六睡觉时、度假时、凌晨 3 点时持续销售。你只需一次工作，Claude 帮你一个下午就做好，而不是一个月。所以想想你现在已经知道的东西，别人正在苦苦挣扎的事情。你的朋友总是向你求助的那些事。你可能习以为常的技能。那知识值得真金白银，现在你终于有了工具把它打包并在睡觉时销售。你并不晚，也不太小。你知道最佳的开始时间是什么时候吗？几年前。那第二好的时间呢？就是现在。你的前 10 个客户比你想的更近。现在，下一个担忧悄然袭来。

turns.en: Okay, this sounds good, but how do I get customers when nobody knows who I am? The answer is smaller than you think. You need 10 people. Remember Peter? He had no audience when he started. He built in public, shared what he was making out loud, and every win and every flop, and people followed along and bought from him because they trusted the journey. You can do the same thing for free starting today. Pick one place where your people are already hanging out. A Facebook group for local business owners, LinkedIn, a forum about your topic. Show up, be useful. Answer questions, share what you learned building your thing. Post a before and after of a problem that you solved. Once a day, find someone asking about the exact problem you solved and give them a genuinely useful answer without a pitch connected to it. Spend 2 weeks doing that and stop being a stranger to this community. You start becoming the person that they think has all the answers.
turns.zh: 好，听起来不错，但没人知道我的时候怎么获取客户？答案比你想象的小。你需要 10 个人。还记得 Peter 吗？他起步时没有听众。他公开构建，大声分享他在做什么，每一次成功和每一次失败，人们都跟着他并从他那购买，因为他们信任这趟旅程。从今天开始你也可以免费做同样的事。选一个你的目标群体已经在的地方：本地企业主的 Facebook 群组、LinkedIn、关于你话题的论坛。出现，有用。回答问题，分享你构建东西时学到的东西。贴一个你解决问题的前后对比。每天一次，找到正在问你的确切问题的人，给他们一个真正有用的答案，不带推销。花两周这样做，不再对这个社区是陌生人。你开始成为他们眼中拥有所有答案的人。

turns.en: And here's a framework that I teach our Mover Makers clients. Make a Money 50 list. That's the 50 people who, if they knew you, liked you, trusted you, could send you real business this year. Don't ask them for coffee or pick their brain. Bring them real value first. Feature them. Share their story. Solve one small problem for them for free. You can open a simple spreadsheet, write down 50 names, and every week pick a few and actually do it. By the time they need what you sell, you're the obvious person that they want to call. You're building real relationships with 50 people who can change your whole year. So, go direct. Email 20 local businesses this week. Message 10 people you already know who run companies. One yes out of 20 and you've made more than a week at a job that you can't stand. So, stop waiting to be discovered. Discovery is not going to come banging on your door. You are going to go where the people are and you help them first. You let the relationship turn that into a customer. Your first 10 customers are in the room you're already standing in. You just haven't started the conversation yet. So, when are you going to start it? Today. The work that you put out is what gives people a reason to find you. So, put something out. Stack small wins into something nobody can ignore.
turns.zh: 这是我在 Mover Makers 课程中教给客户的框架：制作一个「金钱 50」名单。这 50 个人，如果他们认识你、喜欢你、信任你，今年就能给你带来真实的业务。不要请他们喝咖啡或挖空心思。先给他们带来真实的价值。推荐他们。分享他们的故事。免费帮他们解决一个小问题。你可以打开一个简单的电子表格，写下 50 个名字，每周挑几个真正去做。等到他们需要你的产品时，你自然而然就是他们想找的人。你在和 50 个可能改变你一整年的人建立真实的关系。所以，直接出击。这周给 20 家本地企业发邮件。给 10 个你已经认识的企业主发消息。20 个里有一个说好，你就赚到了比你在受不了的工作里一周还多的钱。所以，别再等着被发现。发现不会自己来敲你的门。你要去人们所在的地方，先帮助他们。让这段关系变成客户。你的前 10 个客户就在你已经在的房间里。你只是还没开始对话。那么，你打算什么时候开始？今天。你产出的工作让人们有理由找到你。所以，产出一些东西。把小胜利堆成无法忽略的东西。

turns.en: Okay, so here's the last piece and I think it's the one that separates the people who make a little money from the people who completely change their whole life and their whole family's life. Don't stop at one. One service, one product, one app, that's a great start, but it's just the first brick in your empire you're building. The people winning with AI right now are doing a lot of small things that each make a little and it all adds up. Remember Peter? More than 40 products. Most made nothing. A few changed everything. He didn't know in advance which were going to hit. So, he kept shipping. He kept trying. That's your real advantage. AI makes the cost of trying almost nothing. So, you can take more swings than anyone in history has ever been able to take. You turn the system that you used into a product. You turn what you learned into a course. Each one just feeds the next one. So, you take the money and you make it better. You put it back in. Better tools, more time, the next idea.
turns.zh: 好，这是最后一点，也是区分赚点小钱的人和彻底改变自己及全家生活的人的关键。不要止步于一个。一项服务、一个产品、一个应用，那是个好的开始，但只是你正在建造的帝国中的第一块砖。现在用 AI 获胜的人正在做很多小事情，每件赚一点，加总起来就很可观。还记得 Peter 吗？超过 40 个产品。大多数一无所获。少数几个改变了一切。他事先不知道哪个会爆。所以他不断发布，不断尝试。那是你真正的优势。AI 让尝试的成本几乎为零。所以你可以比历史上任何人都多挥几次棒。把你用过的系统变成一个产品。把你学到的东西变成一个课程。每一步都滋养下一步。你拿着钱，让它变得更好。你把它投回去：更好的工具、更多的时间、下一个想法。

ts.sec: The most important thing you build is yourself

turns.en: And the most important thing that you're building isn't just the money, it's who you become. The first time you make $100 from something that you created with your own hands and a little AI, I don't know, something changes in you forever. You stop seeing yourself as someone waiting for a break and start seeing yourself as someone who makes their own. And that belief is worth more than any paycheck. Because once you have it, nobody can ever take it from you. The whole reason I do this is simple. I want to solve the world's biggest problem. I think people do not believe in themselves enough. AI doesn't fix that. You do. By starting, by shipping, by proving to yourself that you're capable of so much more than you ever gave yourself credit for. Your first dollar is waiting on you. Okay, so here's where you are right now. You've got the most powerful tool in history ready to work for you for almost nothing and real proof that one person starting from scratch and scared can build a life that they're proud of. The only missing piece is you. Saying yes and starting today. So, take the first small step, send the first message, build the first thing, and let the work turn you into the person you already have it in you to be.
turns.zh: 你建造的最重要的东西不仅仅是钱，而是你成为什么样的人。第一次靠自己的双手和一点点 AI 赚到 100 美元时，我不知道，你身上有些东西永远地改变了。你不再把自己看作一个等待机会的人，而是开始把自己看作创造机会的人。那种信念比任何薪水都珍贵。因为一旦你拥有它，就没人能夺走。我做这件事的全部原因很简单：我想解决世界上最大的问题。我认为人们不够相信自己。AI 不能解决那个问题。你才能。通过开始、发布、向自己证明你远比之前以为的更有能力。你的第一块钱在等着你。好，现在你处于什么位置？你拥有了历史上最强大的工具，几乎免费为你工作，还有真实的证明：一个从零开始、害怕的人也能建立起自己自豪的生活。唯一缺失的是你。说「好」，今天就开始。所以，迈出第一步，发出第一条信息，建造第一个东西，让工作把你变成你骨子里已经是的那个样子。

ts.sec: Security in corporate jobs is disappearing

turns.en: Security in a corporate job doesn't exist anymore. The safe job is about to be unsafe. So far this year, companies have cut more than 800,000 jobs. That's the highest number we have seen since the pandemic. A major West Michigan company plans to cut hundreds of jobs. Tonight, Grand Rapids-based Acrisure is telling us that artificial intelligence is replacing actual employees. Over 80% of students feel they learn nothing about entrepreneurship in school, even though most want to start their own businesses. The only non-gamble in life is going on offense. And you've been taught that going on offense is the gamble because the school system was literally created to create factory workers. Our school systems teach us nothing about money. Nothing. It's pathetic. So, at 25, I recommitted to my education, but this time I started studying not things that were in books, but people that had actually created wealth. Sticking to a traditional career path limits your impact, keeps you miserable, and stops you from sharing your unique genius with the world. My sense is that even for the kids that get into the elite colleges at this point, it's like you've passed some Mandarin examination in China, but you're just so exhausted, you're never going to do anything more with the rest of your life. You're burned out at 18. You take a calculated risk to start a company realizing you may forego a couple of years of steady income in another job, and whatever else. That's a great risk to take. And if you don't take that risk, I think you have a very high chance that you end up regretting that. Where are you going to spend your time and your energy is one of the most important decisions you get to make in life. When I was 19, I had the hardest choice to make. I was in university and I had a job offer for a safe six-figure investment banking job. It was a job everybody wanted, but I also had a chance to own 30% of a biotech startup making only $300 a month. And I picked a startup. I chose to struggle, eat beans for lunch because the thought of sitting in a cubicle doing work I hated scared me more than being broke. I knew I had to take control of my own income. Think about Colonel Sanders. At 65 years old, he had a tiny $105 social security check. He didn't go looking for a greater job at a local store.
turns.zh: 企业工作的安全感已经不存在了。安全的工作即将变得不安全。今年到目前为止，公司已经裁掉了超过 80 万个岗位。这是自疫情以来我们看到的最高的数字。密歇根西部一家大公司计划裁员数百人。今晚，总部在大急流城的 Acrisure 告诉我们，人工智能正在取代实际员工。超过 80% 的学生觉得他们在学校学不到任何关于创业的知识，尽管大多数人想创业。生活中唯一不是赌博的事就是主动出击。而你被教导主动出击是赌博，因为学校系统本质上就是为培养工厂工人而创建的。我们的学校系统不教我们任何关于钱的东西。一点都没有。可悲。所以 25 岁时，我重新投入教育，但这次我开始学习的不是书本里的东西，而是那些真正创造财富的人。坚持传统的职业道路限制了你的影响力，让你痛苦，并阻止你与世界分享你独特的天赋。我的感觉是，即使是那些进了精英大学的孩子，也像通过了中国的普通话考试，但你已经筋疲力尽，余生不会再做什么了。18 岁就 burnout 了。你承担计算过的风险去创业，意识到你可能要放弃另一份工作几年的稳定收入，以及其他。那是一个很值得冒的风险。如果你不冒那个风险，我觉得你极有可能后悔。你打算在哪里花费时间和精力，是你一生中最重要的决定之一。我 19 岁时，做了最艰难的选择。我在上大学，有一份安全的六位数投资银行工作 offer，是每个人都想要的工作，但我也有机会持有生物科技创业公司 30% 的股份，每月只赚 300 美元。我选择了创业。我选择了奋斗，午餐吃豆子，因为坐在格子间里做我讨厌的工作比没钱更让我害怕。我知道我必须掌控自己的收入。想想桑德斯上校。65 岁时，他只有 105 美元的社会保障支票。他没有去当地商店找一份更好的工作。

turns.en: He took his chicken recipe, hit the road, and slept in his car. He faced a thousand and nine rejections before finally someone said yes to his franchise idea. He proved that you can create massive wealth at any age just by owning your own ideas instead of working for someone else. Brian Chesky and Joe Gebbia couldn't pay their rent in San Francisco. They didn't rush out to get safe normal jobs. Instead, they put three air mattresses on their floor and charged people to sleep there during a local design conference. That simple idea turned into Airbnb. They created a hundred million-dollar company because they looked for a creative way to solve a problem instead of looking for a safe corporate salary. And right now you might be thinking that you need thousands of dollars in the bank to start making your own money. You think you need rich parents or some giant loan to succeed, and that's not true. Colonel Sanders was broke at 65. Airbnb started with three cheap air mattresses. You don't need money to make money. You just need a problem to solve and the courage to take the first step.
turns.zh: 他带着自己的炸鸡配方上路，睡在车里。他遭遇了一千零九次拒绝，终于有人同意了他的特许经营想法。他证明了无论年龄多大，你都可以通过拥有自己的想法而非为别人打工来创造巨额财富。布莱恩·切斯基和乔·格比亚在旧金山付不起房租。他们没有急于去找安稳的正常工作。相反，他们在地板上放了三个气垫床，在本地设计会议期间收费让人来睡。这个简单的想法变成了 Airbnb。他们创建了一家价值上亿美元的公司，因为他们寻求创造性的问题解决方案，而不是追求安稳的企业薪水。现在你可能认为你需要银行里有数千美元才能开始自己赚钱。你以为你需要有钱的父母或一笔巨额贷款才能成功，但事实并非如此。桑德斯上校在 65 岁时身无分文。Airbnb 始于三个廉价气垫床。你不需要钱来赚钱。你只需要一个待解决的问题和迈出第一步的勇气。

turns.en: To make money without a job, you've got to realize where value actually comes from. You get paid for bringing value to other people. The absolute easiest way to bring value is to look directly at your own life. Your purpose comes from your pain. Whatever you struggle with the most is exactly what you want to help other people overcome. So, think about your past. If you had a hard time getting fit and you figured out a system that works, that system is your new business. If you struggled with anxiety and found a way to manage it, that method is your business. You don't need a fancy business degree to make this happen. You just need to be one step ahead of the person that you're trying to help. Over 62% of billionaires are totally self-made, meaning they've created their wealth by solving real problems, not by inheriting cash. People pay you to solve their problems because they desperately want to skip the pain that you have already gone through. You're selling speed and convenience. If you can help someone skip 5 years of painful trial and error, they pay you for that shortcut. So, don't think you need to invent the next big tech platform to be successful. Look at the local businesses in your town. They need help with their marketing, their accounting, their daily operations. They've got massive problems right now. You can step in and help fix those problems. When you focus entirely on serving others and solving their actual pain points, you stop acting like an employee begging for a simple paycheck and you start acting like a true entrepreneur commanding a premium price. You stop handing out weak resumes and start handing out powerful solutions for problems. This simple shift in your mindset changes everything. You go from hoping that a boss picks you to knowing that the market desperately needs you. So, you've got to stop looking for a company to hire you and start looking for a person to help. The money will always follow the value you provide. So, if you fix a $100 problem, you make a little bit of money. If you fix a $1,000 problem, you make a lot more money. It's simple. Your job right now is to identify the most expensive problem you know how to solve and then go find the exact people who are crying out for that exact solution.
turns.zh: 要想不靠工作赚钱，你必须意识到价值从何而来。你因给别人带来价值而获得报酬。带来价值最简单的方法就是直接审视自己的生活。你的使命源于你的痛苦。你最挣扎的事情正是你想帮助他人克服的事情。所以，回想你的过去。如果你在健身方面遇到过困难并找到了一套有效的系统，那套系统就是你的新生意。如果你曾与焦虑作斗争并找到了管理方法，那个方法就是你的生意。你不需要一个花哨的商科学位来实现这一点。你只需要比你试图帮助的人领先一步。超过 62% 的亿万富翁完全是白手起家，这意味着他们通过解决实际问题创造了财富，而不是继承现金。人们付钱给你解决他们的问题，因为他们迫切想要跳过你已经经历过的痛苦。你出售的是速度和便利。如果你能帮助某人跳过 5 年痛苦试错的过程，他们就会为这个捷径付费。所以，不要以为你需要发明下一个大型科技平台才能成功。看看你所在城镇的本地企业。他们在营销、会计、日常运营方面需要帮助。他们目前面临巨大的问题。你可以介入并帮助解决这些问题。当你完全专注于服务他人并解决他们实际痛点时，你就不再像一个乞讨薪水的员工，而是像一个真正定价的企业家。你不再递出弱小的简历，而是递出强大的问题解决方案。这种心态的转变改变了一切。你从希望老板选中你转变为知道市场迫切需要你。所以，你必须停止寻找公司雇佣你，开始寻找需要帮助的人。金钱总是追随你提供的价值。所以，如果你解决了一个 100 美元的问题，你赚一点钱。如果你解决了一个 1000 美元的问题，你会赚更多的钱。很简单。你现在的任务是找出你知道如何解决的最昂贵的问题，然后找到那些迫切渴望那个解决方案的人。

turns.en: But, finding a problem is only the first step because your surroundings might be secretly destroying your chances of success. Change your environment to change your mind. Your current environment is perfectly designed to keep you exactly where you are right now. So, if your friends all have traditional jobs, they'll constantly tell you to get a safe job. They aren't trying to hurt you, they just don't understand your big vision. Research shows that you're up to 61% more likely to adopt the exact habits and mindsets of the people closest to you. So, if you want to make your own money, you must change your daily environment. You've got to completely shut out the negativity. Limit your access to people who doubt you and fill that empty space with extreme positivity and the specific messages you actually want to hear. So, if you can't find supportive friends in your own town yet, go find them online. Read powerful books, listen to great podcasts, watch amazing YouTube videos from the exact people who are already doing what you want to do. I started my YouTube channel because I wanted to surround myself with some of the greatest minds in history. I wanted Steve Jobs and Warren Buffett in my ear every single morning. I wanted their intense ambition to rub off on me. You've got to be incredibly intentional with your daily morning routine. Don't wake up and immediately scroll through toxic social media or the depressing news. Start your day with content that makes you believe in yourself. When you consume greatness daily, it starts to feel completely normal. Soon, the idea of settling for a boring cubicle will feel totally insane to you. You'll begin to think bigger, act faster, expect so much more of yourself. You can literally rewire your entire brain for massive success just by changing what you look at and who you listen to every single day. So, treat it like a garden, right? Your mind is a garden. If you plant negative seeds, you'll grow a massive negative life. If you plant seeds of belief, you'll grow a massive awesome empire. You've got to ruthlessly protect your focus. So, stop giving your attention to things that make you feel small and start obsessing over the ideas that make you feel powerful. The moment you change your inputs, the outputs will transform forever.
turns.zh: 但是，发现问题只是第一步，因为你的周围环境可能正在暗中破坏你的成功机会。改变环境以改变心态。你当前的环境被完美设计来让你保持现状。所以，如果你的朋友都有传统工作，他们会不断告诉你找份安稳工作。他们不是想伤害你，只是不理解你的宏大愿景。研究表明，你采用最亲近之人的习惯和心态的可能性高达 61%。所以，如果你想自己赚钱，你必须改变你的日常环境。你必须完全屏蔽负能量。限制你接触那些怀疑你的人，并用极度的积极和你真正想听的信息来填补空白。如果你在自己的城镇还找不到支持你的朋友，那就去网上找。阅读有力量的书，听优秀的播客，观看那些已经做着你所向往之事的出色人士的 YouTube 视频。我创办我的 YouTube 频道是因为我想让自己身边围绕着历史上一些最伟大的头脑。我希望每天早上都能听到史蒂夫·乔布斯和沃伦·巴菲特在我耳边。我希望他们强烈的雄心能感染我。你必须对你的晨间例行活动极度用心。不要醒来就立刻浏览有毒的社交媒体或令人沮丧的新闻。用让你相信自己的内容开始新的一天。当你每天接触伟大，它就会开始变得完全正常。很快，安于一个无聊隔间的想法会让你感到完全疯狂。你会开始想得更远大，行动更快，对自己期望更高。仅仅通过改变你每天看什么、听什么，你就能真正重新连接你的整个大脑，取得巨大成功。所以，把它当成花园，对吧？你的头脑就是一座花园。如果你播下负面的种子，你就会长出一个巨大的负面人生。如果你播下信念的种子，你就会长出一个巨大的帝国。你必须无情地保护你的注意力。所以，停止把注意力放在让你感到渺小的事情上，开始痴迷于让你感到强大的想法。当你改变输入的那一刻，输出将永远改变。

turns.en: But, once you fix your surroundings, you need a system to actually get you moving, which brings us to the simple 2% trick. Use the 2% rule to build massive momentum. The biggest thing you're missing right now is just momentum. You're sitting on a truly great idea, but you haven't taken any real action. You're constantly overthinking it. You want everything to be 100% perfect before you finally launch. You want the perfect logo, the perfect website, the perfect business plan. Stop doing that. Perfectionism is just you being afraid. Studies reveal that perfectionism actually decreases your productivity and increases severe mental burnout. You don't need a perfect plan. You just need to execute the first 2%. If your goal is to write a book, a best-selling book, the first 2% is writing just one single page. If your goal is to start a massive YouTube channel, awesome. The first 2% is pulling out your phone and recording your first really messy video. Don't worry about step 100, just focus completely on step number one. Take the absolute smallest, easiest action right now. Once you take that first step, your brain gets a quick win.
turns.zh: 但是，一旦你改善了周围环境，你需要一个系统来真正让自己行动起来，这就引出了简单的 2% 技巧。利用 2% 法则来建立巨大动力。你现在缺少的最大东西就是动力。你拥有一个真正伟大的想法，但你没有采取任何实际行动。你一直在过度思考。你希望在最终推出之前一切都能 100% 完美。你想要完美的标志、完美的网站、完美的商业计划。别再这样做了。完美主义只是你在害怕。研究表明，完美主义实际上降低了你的生产力，并增加了严重的精神倦怠。你不需要一个完美的计划。你只需要执行前 2%。如果你的目标是写一本书，一本畅销书，前 2% 就是只写一页。如果你的目标是创建一个大型 YouTube 频道，太好了。前 2% 就是拿出手机录制你的第一个非常凌乱的视频。不要担心第 100 步，完全集中于第一步。现在立即采取最小、最容易的行动。一旦你迈出第一步，你的大脑就会获得一个快速胜利。

turns.en: And that quick win builds confidence and that confidence creates momentum. So, when I wrote my book about momentum, I didn't plan it out for long months. I just started typing furiously. The physical action itself creates the energy you need to keep going. So, waiting around for the perfect moment, what does it do? It guarantees that you'll wait forever. Action cures fear every single time. When you're moving forward, you simply don't have the time to sit there and doubt yourself. So, don't let your greatest ideas die just silently here in your head. Put them out into the real world. Start messy. Start small. But, you've absolutely got to start when? Today. It doesn't matter if your first attempt looks crazy, ridiculous. The only thing that matters is that you aren't just standing still anymore. You're finally in the game. Every massive company started as some tiny, flawed, little experiment. You are no different. So, push through the hesitation, click publish, make the call, and watch how quickly your life begins to change.
turns.zh: 快速的胜利能建立信心，而信心能创造动能。所以，当我写关于动能的书时，我没有策划好几个月。我只是疯狂地开始打字。身体动作本身就会产生你需要的能量，让你坚持下去。所以，等待完美时刻会怎样？它保证你会永远等下去。行动每次都能治愈恐惧。当你向前迈进时，你根本没有时间坐在那里怀疑自己。所以，不要让你最伟大的想法在脑海中默默消亡。把它们放到现实世界中去。混乱地开始，从小处开始。但你绝对要什么时候开始？今天。你的第一次尝试看起来疯狂、荒谬都没关系。唯一重要的是你不再原地踏步。你终于上场了。每个大公司都是从微小、有缺陷的小实验开始的。你也不例外。所以，克服犹豫，点击发布，打个电话，看看你的生活如何迅速开始改变。

turns.en: Now that you're moving though, you've got to prepare yourself for the hardest phase of all. And this is where almost everyone quits. Expect to be terrible at first. So, now you got to accept a really harsh reality. Your first attempt at anything new is going to be absolutely terrible. Your first product will have tons of flaws. Your first uh video will be incredibly embarrassing. Your first major sales call will feel completely awkward. And that is completely normal. Everyone starts out at the bottom. You just don't see the messy, hidden starts. Data shows that it takes roughly 10,000 hours of deliberate practice to truly master any complex skill. You just can't skip the struggle. When I first started on YouTube, I was completely terrified. I was shy, quiet, introverted. I did not like being on camera. It took me 350 videos before I wasn't completely embarrassed to watch myself back and 700 public videos before I actually felt inspired by one piece of content that I made. And I made absolutely hundreds of terrible videos. You can go back and watch them. But, I kept going anyway. Most people just quit because they tried five times and they expected to be world-class immediately. They let their ego stop you from making actual progress. So, the fact that you're willing to try and be terrible becomes an actual secret advantage. So, embrace the highly awkward phase. Look at your early failures as data and that's going to be part of your story as you climb. Every single time you fail, you learn exactly what not to do the next time. You'll be an inspiration to others. If you can handle looking foolish for a little while, you'll eventually become completely unstoppable. The only real failure in life is quitting before you get good. So, you've got to give yourself permission to be a total beginner. Stop comparing your chapter one to somebody else's chapter 20, right? Your journey is your journey, and that is okay. So, put in the boring reps, do the unglamorous work. The mastery that you want is waiting on the other side of a thousand terrible attempts.
turns.zh: 不过，既然你已经行动了，就得为最艰难的阶段做好准备。这也是几乎所有人放弃的地方。预期一开始会很糟糕。所以，你得接受一个残酷的现实：你对任何新事物的第一次尝试都会极其糟糕。你的第一个产品会有很多缺陷。你的第一个视频会非常尴尬。你的第一次重要销售电话会感觉很别扭。这完全正常。每个人都是从底层开始的。你只是看不到那些混乱、隐藏的起点。数据显示，真正掌握任何复杂技能需要大约一万小时的刻意练习。你无法跳过挣扎。我刚开始做 YouTube 时，完全吓坏了。我害羞、安静、内向，不喜欢上镜。我花了 350 个视频才不再完全尴尬地回看自己，花了 700 个公开视频才终于对自己制作的某个内容感到受启发。我做了几百个糟糕的视频，你可以回去看看。但我还是坚持了下来。大多数人因为尝试了五次、期望立刻成为世界级就放弃了。他们让自尊心阻止了自己取得实际进步。所以，你愿意尝试并表现糟糕反而成了秘密优势。拥抱非常尴尬的阶段。把早期的失败看作数据，它们将是你攀登过程中的故事。每次失败，你都确切学到了下次不该做什么。你会成为他人的启发。如果你能忍受一段时间看起来愚蠢，最终你会变得势不可挡。生活中唯一的真正失败是在变好之前放弃。所以，你得允许自己做一个彻头彻尾的初学者。停止把你的第一章和别人第二十章比较，对吧？你的旅程就是你的旅程，这没关系。投入那些枯燥的重复，做不光彩的工作。你想要的精通在无数次糟糕尝试的另一边等着。

turns.en: And once you survive that awkward phase, you can speed up your results by borrowing the exact blueprints of people who've already won. Model the massive success of others. You don't need to figure out all of this on your own. That was one of the biggest mistakes I made early on. You don't have to reinvent the wheel to make a massive fortune. The smartest entrepreneurs study the exact people who've already won and simply model their success. So, if you want to build a $100,000 consulting business, find someone who already did exactly that. Study their public website, look at their specific pricing, see exactly how they talk to their premium clients, then thoughtfully apply those same proven principles to your own unique style. According to the Small Business Administration, businesses that receive direct mentoring and strictly model proven strategies are two times more likely to survive their first five difficult years. When my first business was struggling, I felt completely lost. I had no real idea how to turn things around. Then I decided to intensely study a highly successful software company, Microsoft, cuz I had a software company. I looked at how they operated, looked at how they got their first clients, not how they make an extra million now. I didn't steal or copy them, but I learned directly from Bill Gates' powerful framework. And that single focus decision saved my entire company. Success always leaves clues. There's a roadmap out there for you to do whatever you want and achieve whatever you want. You just have to be humble and curious enough to actively go and follow it. So, read the biographies of great leaders. Watch the long-form interviews of the performers that you look up to and respect. Find the hidden patterns in their daily behaviors and then creatively adapt them to your situation. Why would you spend 10 years making deeply painful mistakes when you can learn from someone else's expensive experience in just 10 days or 10 hours? So, being aggressive student of greatness and your path to financial independence will be so much faster. You don't lack the ability. You just lack the right model. So, find your ideal model, study them relentlessly, build your own blueprint for your special flavor.
turns.zh: 一旦你熬过了那个尴尬阶段，就可以通过借鉴成功者的确切蓝图来加快成果。模仿他人的巨大成功。你不需要自己摸索一切。这是我早期犯的最大错误之一。你不需要重新发明轮子来赚大钱。最聪明的创业者会研究那些已经成功的人，并直接模仿他们的成功方式。所以，如果你想建立一个十万美元的咨询业务，找一个已经做到的人。研究他们的公开网站，查看他们的具体定价，看他们如何与高端客户交谈，然后深思熟虑地将这些经过验证的原则应用到你自己独特的风格中。根据小企业管理局的数据，接受直接指导并严格模仿被证明有效策略的企业，在头五年生存下来的可能性是其他企业的两倍。当我的第一个生意陷入困境时，我感到完全迷茫，不知道如何扭转局面。于是我决定深入研究一家非常成功的软件公司——微软，因为我当时也有一家软件公司。我观察他们如何运营，如何获取第一批客户，而不是现在如何多赚一百万。我没有抄袭他们，而是直接从比尔·盖茨的强大框架中学习。那一个专注的决策拯救了我的整个公司。成功总会留下线索。那里有一张路线图，让你可以做任何你想做的事，实现任何目标。你只需要足够谦虚和好奇，主动去跟随它。所以，阅读伟大人物的传记，观看你仰慕和尊敬的表演者的长篇访谈。找到他们日常行为中隐藏的模式，然后创造性地将它们应用到你的情况中。为什么要花十年时间犯痛苦的大错，而你可以在十天或十小时内从别人的昂贵经验中学习？所以，做一个伟大的学生，你通往财务独立的道路会快得多。你不是缺乏能力，只是缺乏正确的模型。找到你理想的模型，不懈地研究它，为你自己特殊的风味构建蓝图。

turns.en: And then when you've got the right model, you need the right people. And there's a specific way to get the most powerful CEOs to take your call. Build real relationships instead of fake followers. So, most people think that making money online means you definitely need millions of random followers, right? You think that you need to go incredibly viral to succeed. And that's a massive and actually dangerous distraction. You don't need a million casual subscribers to make a million dollars. You just need deep, highly meaningful relationships. Don't worry about the vanity metrics. They will constantly waste your time. Instead, focus on direct business development through high-value connections. One of my favorite strategies that we teach inside our Movement Makers program is a business development show. It's a dedicated interview show. Don't constantly cold call potential clients. Warmly invite them onto your show to share their story. People love talking about themselves. When you feature them prominently, they feel valued and you build a relationship. Statistics clearly show that 84% of B2B sales start exactly with a warm referral or a strong existing relationship. When you interview someone, you spend real focused time with them. You build authentic trust with them. That genuine trust turns into lucrative partnerships, massive referrals, highly paying clients. It literally doesn't matter if your new channel only has 200 total subscribers. We're going after people who have high demand but low media demand. You're coming in as media right now.
turns.zh: 然后，当你有了正确的模型，你需要正确的人。有一种特定的方式可以让最有影响力的CEO接你的电话。建立真实的关系，而不是虚假的粉丝。所以，大多数人认为在线赚钱意味着你肯定需要数百万随机的粉丝，对吧？你认为你需要疯传才能成功。那是一个巨大且危险的干扰。你不需要一百万个随意订阅者来赚一百万美元。你只需要深度、非常有意义的关系。不要担心虚荣指标，它们会不断浪费你的时间。相反，通过高价值的联系专注于直接的业务发展。我们在「Movement Makers」项目中教授的一个我最喜欢的策略是商业发展节目。这是一个专门的访谈节目。不要一直打冷电话给潜在客户。热情地邀请他们上你的节目分享他们的故事。人们喜欢谈论自己。当你突出介绍他们时，他们会感到被重视，你就能建立关系。统计数据清楚地表明，84% 的B2B销售恰恰始于温暖的推荐或强大的现有关系。当你采访某人时，你会与他们共度真正的专注时间，建立真实的信任。这种真诚的信任会转化为利润丰厚的合作伙伴关系、大量的推荐和高付费客户。你的新频道只有200个订阅者完全没关系。我们要追求的是那些高需求但低媒体需求的人。你现在就是以媒体的身份进入。

turns.en: You can get top industry leaders who built multi-million dollar networks. So don't worry about random clicks and start aggressively chasing real conversations. Add massive value to the exact people you desperately want to work with. Feature their deep expertise. Ask them incredibly great questions. Do your research before you have them on. Give them a beautiful platform to share their story. When you actively become a super connector and a supporter, the big money naturally follows you everywhere you go. Your network is truly your net worth. So start building it deliberately and strategically today.
turns.zh: 你能结识那些建立了价值数百万美元人脉的顶尖行业领袖。所以别担心那些随机的点击，开始积极地追求真正的对话。为你迫切想要合作的那些人创造巨大的价值，突出他们的深厚专长，向他们提出极其精彩的问题，在上线前做好研究，给他们一个漂亮的平台来分享他们的故事。当你主动成为一个超级连接者和支持者时，大钱自然会跟着你走。你的人脉就是你真正的净资产。所以从今天开始有策略地、有意识地构建它。

turns.en: Stop worrying about the algorithm and start obsessing over the actual human beings you want to serve. Building that network takes extreme focus, which means you've got to completely change how you manage your 24 hours. Make every single day truly count. Your limited time is your absolute most precious asset. If you want to permanently escape the endless job cycle and build your own incredible life, you've got to maximize your specific daily actions. So you wake up every morning with a clear intention. Make today truly count. Before you hit your head on the pillow tonight, do one specific thing that moves you significantly closer to your dream. Make one beautiful piece of art. Send one highly important email. Record one incredibly helpful video. Create something today that you desperately want your future grandkids to see. Research strongly indicates that completing just one highly meaningful task a day significantly boosts your overall life satisfaction and guarantees long-term success. To make real time for that meaningful work, you've got to ruthlessly manage your busy schedule. You must eliminate, automate, or delegate absolutely everything else. If a specific task doesn't directly serve your core mission, stop doing it. If a basic computer program or AI can do it, automate it immediately. If someone else can do it significantly cheaper, hire them right away. Don't waste your unique genius on boring busy work. Focus only on the high-level tasks that actually move the big needle forward.
turns.zh: 别再担心算法了，开始痴迷于那些你真正想要服务的人。建立这样的人脉需要极度的专注，这意味着你必须彻底改变你管理 24 小时的方式。让每一天都真正有意义。你有限的时间是你最宝贵的资产。如果你想永久地逃离无止境的工作循环，建立自己精彩的人生，就必须最大化你的日常行动。所以你每天早上醒来都要有清晰的意图。让今天真正有意义。在你今晚头靠枕头之前，做一件能让你离梦想更近一步的事。创作一件美丽的艺术品，发送一封非常重要的邮件，录制一个极有帮助的视频。今天创造一些你未来孙子孙女渴望看到的东西。研究强烈表明，每天完成一项非常有意义的任务能显著提升你的整体生活满意度，并保证长期成功。为了给那些有意义的工作腾出时间，你必须无情地管理你的繁忙日程。你必须消除、自动化或委派其他所有事情。如果某件任务不能直接服务于你的核心使命，就停止做它。如果一个基本的计算机程序或 AI 能做，立即自动化。如果别人能做得更便宜，马上雇佣他们。不要把你独特的天赋浪费在无聊的琐事上。只专注于那些真正能推动大局的高层次任务。

turns.en: When you finally take control of your daily time, you instantly take total control of your personal income. You stop hopelessly trading hours for a flat, boring salary and start aggressively trading massive value for huge financial returns. You already have absolutely everything it takes to build a beautiful life of total freedom. You just have to firmly decide that you're ready to step up and claim it. And this brings us to the absolute most important truth of all, and it's something that I hope that you remember every single morning when you wake up. Your belief is your ultimate superpower. You are entirely capable of building a massive life on your own terms. So trust your vision. Take the messy action and never let fear make your decisions for you.
turns.zh: 当你最终掌控了自己的日常时间，你就立刻完全掌控了自己的个人收入。你不再绝望地用时间换取一份平淡无奇的固定薪水，而是开始积极地用巨大的价值换取丰厚的财务回报。你已经完全具备了建立自由美好生活所需的一切。你只需要坚定地决定自己准备好了，去站出来并抓住它。这就引出了最重要的事实，我希望你每天早上醒来都能记住：你的信念是你终极的超能力。你完全有能力按照自己的方式建立庞大的生活。所以相信你的愿景，采取杂乱的行动，永远不要让恐惧替你决定。

turns.en: Your intelligence is the reason you're not successful. Being smart might actually be holding you back. Every day I see brilliant people with sky-high IQs lose to others with half their talent. Why? Because intelligence alone doesn't automatically translate to results. If you keep letting your smarts run the show, you'll watch those average people, the ones who show up consistently and push through, leapfrog right over you. And the worst part? The world misses out on your genius. The woman who should have cured cancer might be stuck in a dead-end job because she didn't believe in herself or take action. Think of the tortoise and the hare. The fast, cocky hare, the smart one, took a nap thinking he had the race won. The slow but steady tortoise kept going and crossed the finish line first. In real life, too many smart people act like the hare. So confident in their brain power that they get complacent or overcomplicate everything while the less assuming tortoises quietly grind out the win. Being the hare might feel good at first, but it doesn't win races. I learned that the hard way. In my early 20s, I had a shot at a life-changing deal selling my first company for millions of dollars. I was trying to be the smart kid with a detailed plan, and I over-planned everything. I spent months crafting the perfect business plan instead of actually doing something. And guess what happened? A big company came looking to buy businesses like mine, but we weren't ready to move. It came down to my company and our biggest competitor, and we lost. And that competitor of ours got bought for $40 million while I was still polishing my plan. $40 million? That stung. I could have sold my business for $40 million, but I missed my shot because I was being too perfect. That failure woke me up. I realized my smart plan was really just fear in disguise. Fear of making a mistake, fear of it not being perfect. Perfectionism is really just fear. We call it diligence, but really you're just scared. I decided to become a recovering perfectionist after that. Now when I get a great idea, I force myself to act on it immediately before my brain can come up with 20 reasons to wait. I learned that a half-assed plan that you actually execute is better than a perfect plan that stays in your head. Now at this point you might be thinking, "Evan, are you saying I should stop being smart? Am I supposed to dumb it down to succeed?" No, I'm not saying abandon your brain or act recklessly. I'm saying you have to change how you use your intelligence. Right now your smarts are running the show and running you into a wall. You probably pride yourself on being the smartest person in the room, but is that working out for you? If you're so smart, why aren't you where you want to be? The truth is raw intelligence without execution gets you nowhere. You have to get out of your head and into action. Being smart is a gift, but if you don't pair that gift with courage, with discipline, with hustle, it will absolutely hold you back. Don't let your ego or fear of not looking smart keep you from growing. The only thing worse than being seen as not smart is being full of potential and never actually achieving anything. So yes, keep your intelligence, but put it to work for you, not against you.
turns.zh: 你的智力正是你不成功的原因。聪明可能实际上在拖你的后腿。每天我都看到智商极高的人才输给只有他们一半天赋的人。为什么？因为智力本身并不会自动转化为结果。如果你继续让聪明才智主导一切，你会看到那些普通人——那些持续出现、奋力前行的人——直接跳到你前面。最糟糕的是？世界错过了你的天才。那个本应治愈癌症的女性可能被困在一份没有前途的工作中，因为她不相信自己或不采取行动。想想龟兔赛跑。那只快速、自负的兔子（聪明的那位）打了盹，以为已经赢了比赛。而缓慢但稳健的乌龟继续前进，率先冲过终点线。在现实生活中，太多聪明人表现得像兔子。他们对大脑能力如此自信，以至于变得自满或过度复杂化一切，而那些不那么引人注目的乌龟则默默赢得了胜利。当兔子一开始感觉不错，但它赢不了比赛。我通过痛苦的方式学到了这一点。在我 20 岁出头时，我有一个改变一生的机会，可以将我的第一家公司以数百万美元出售。我试图做一个有详细计划的聪明孩子，结果过度计划了一切。我花了几个月时间构思完美的商业计划，而不是实际做点什么。猜猜发生了什么？一家大公司来收购像我这样的企业，但我们还没准备好行动。最后是我的公司和最大的竞争对手之间抉择，我们输了。那个竞争对手被以 4000 万美元收购，而我还在打磨计划。4000 万美元？那很痛。我本可以以 4000 万美元卖掉公司，但因为太追求完美而错过了机会。那次失败唤醒了我。我意识到我聪明的计划实际上是恐惧的伪装——害怕犯错，害怕不够完美。完美主义其实就是恐惧。我们称之为勤奋，但其实你只是害怕。之后我决定成为一个正在康复的完美主义者。现在当我有个好主意时，我强迫自己在脑子想出 20 个等待理由之前立即行动。我学到了一个执行得马马虎虎的计划，比一个停留在脑子里的完美计划要好。现在你可能会想：“Evan，你是说我应该停止聪明吗？难道我要为了成功而变笨吗？”不，我不是说放弃你的大脑或鲁莽行事。我是说你必须改变使用智力的方式。现在你的聪明才智在主导一切，却把你逼进了死胡同。你可能为自己是房间里最聪明的人而自豪，但这对你有用吗？如果你这么聪明，为什么还没达到你想要的位置？事实是，没有执行的原始智力让你一事无成。你必须走出自己的头脑，进入行动。聪明是天赋，但如果你不用勇气、纪律和努力去配它，它绝对会拖你后腿。不要让你的自我或害怕看起来不聪明阻止你成长。唯一比被认为不聪明更糟糕的事，就是充满潜力却从未取得任何成就。所以是的，保留你的智力，但要让它为你工作，而不是与你作对。

turns.en: So let's talk about how to fix this. Let's turn your intelligence into an asset instead of a liability. Here we go. Why smart people struggle with success and how to turn it around. Number one, you overthink everything. Smart people can get stuck in analysis paralysis. Your brain sees 20 angles to every problem. You can imagine every possible outcome and all that analysis leaves you spinning in circles. Sound familiar? You plan and you plan and you plan and nothing actually happens. Meanwhile, someone with half your brainpower just picks a direction and goes. They get results while you're still in your head. Here's the deal. Thinking about doing something and actually doing it are completely different things.
turns.zh: 那么我们来谈谈如何解决这个问题。把你的智力变成资产而不是负债。开始吧。为什么聪明人难以成功以及如何扭转局面。第一，你过度思考一切。聪明人容易陷入分析瘫痪。你的大脑看到每个问题的 20 个角度。你能想象所有可能的结果，所有这些分析让你原地打转。听起来熟悉吗？你计划、计划、再计划，而实际上什么都没发生。与此同时，一个只有你一半脑力的人只是选了一个方向就出发了。他们得到了结果，而你还在脑子里打转。关键在于：想做什么和实际做什么是完全不同的两件事。

turns.en: No matter how brilliant your idea is, you must act on it. Studies in cognitive psychology even show that excessive deliberation can lead to worse decisions because you start second-guessing yourself and overcomplicating simple choices. So, what's the solution? Decide and go. Give yourself a deadline to make a decision and then execute. Trust your intuition and start moving. You can adjust course as you go. Remember, real progress happens in the real world, not in your head. Don't let overthinking murder your momentum.
turns.zh: 无论你的想法多么出色，都必须付诸行动。认知心理学研究甚至表明，过度思考会导致更糟的决策，因为你开始自我怀疑，把简单问题复杂化。那解决方案是什么？做决定，然后行动。给自己设定决策期限，然后执行。相信直觉，开始行动。你可以在过程中调整方向。记住，真正的进步发生在现实世界，而不是你的头脑里。别让过度思考扼杀你的动力。

turns.en: Number two, you're chasing perfect and it's slowing you down. This was my curse. In school, you might have been the kid who got A's, who set super high standards. In life and business, those high standards can actually hold you back. You rewrite the opening chapter seven times and never publish the book. You tinker with your product endlessly because it's not good enough yet to launch. Guess what? Perfect is the enemy of progress. Successful people execute and then iterate. Unsuccessful smart people keep polishing a draft that never sees the light of day. Here's how one entrepreneur put it, you can't refine what doesn't exist. You can't improve a product that never launched. Average performers often beat perfectionists because they're willing to put out good enough and then improve later. My own $40 million mistake was due to perfectionism. I waited and wanted the perfect plan and I was too late. Learn from my mistake. Launch messy, embrace mistakes. Done is better than perfect. And remember that urge to be perfect? It's really fear. Perfectionism is fear in a tuxedo. It looks respectable, even admirable, but it's killing your success. So, punch fear in the face by putting out your work, flaws and all. Progress beats perfection every time.
turns.zh: 第二，你追求完美，这会拖慢你。这是我的诅咒。在学校里，你可能是拿 A 的学生，设定极高的标准。但在生活和商业中，这些高标准反而会阻碍你。你重写开头章节七次，却从未出版书。你无休止地调整产品，因为觉得还不够好不能发布。猜怎么着？完美是进步的敌人。成功的人先执行，再迭代。不成功的聪明人则不断打磨永远见不到光的草稿。一位创业者说得好：你无法改进不存在的东西。你无法改进从未发布的产品。平均水平的执行者往往打败完美主义者，因为他们愿意先拿出“足够好”的版本，然后再改进。我自己 4000 万美元的失误就源于完美主义。我等待并想要完美的计划，结果太迟了。从我的错误中学习。不完美地发布，拥抱错误。完成胜过完美。记住那种追求完美的冲动吗？那其实是恐惧。完美主义是穿着燕尾服的恐惧。它看起来体面甚至令人钦佩，但正在扼杀你的成功。所以，直面恐惧，将你的作品公之于众，带着瑕疵。进步每次都战胜完美。

ts.sec: Relying on talent instead of work

turns.en: Number three, you rely on talent instead of work. This one stings, but I've seen it so often. Things come easy for you. Right school, jobs, picking up new skills. You're used to being the best with minimal effort. Meanwhile, others had to grind to get good, and the result is you never develop the discipline and habits that success actually requires. Maybe you breezed through school without studying, so you never learn how to truly study or struggle. You prided yourself on pulling off last-minute miracles or acing presentations with no prep, and it worked until now. So, when you finally hit something hard, something that doesn't come instantly, you stall or quit because you don't have the tools or grit to push through. Psychology research backs this up. People who think intelligence is fixed tend to avoid challenges that might prove them wrong. But those who believe abilities grow with effort are the ones who persist when things get tough. So, natural talent might open the door, but discipline, resilience, and grind get you to the finish line. If you've coasted on talent, it's time to be humble and get to work. Being smart is not an excuse to be lazy. Embrace the beginner's mindset. Push yourself to do the uncomfortable drills, the boring repetitions, the late-night study sessions. Hard work beats talent when talent doesn't work hard every single time.
turns.zh: 第三，你依赖天赋而非努力。这一点很扎心，但我见过很多次。事情对你来说很容易：好学校、好工作、学新技能。你习惯了最小努力就能做到最好。与此同时，别人必须刻苦才能变优秀，结果是你从未培养出成功真正需要的自律和习惯。也许你轻松通过了学业，从不学习，所以从未学会真正学习或奋斗。你以临时抱佛脚或毫无准备就能做精彩演讲为傲，而且至今奏效。但当你最终遇到困难、无法一蹴而就的事情时，你会停滞或放弃，因为你没有突破所需的工具或毅力。心理学研究支持这一点：认为智力固定的人倾向于回避可能证明他们错误的挑战；而认为能力可以通过努力增长的人在困难时会坚持。所以，天赋可能打开大门，但纪律、韧性和苦干才能让你冲过终点线。如果你一直依赖天赋，现在是时候谦虚并开始努力了。聪明不是懒惰的借口。拥抱初学者心态。强迫自己做不舒适的练习、枯燥的重复、深夜学习。当天赋不努力时，努力每次都击败天赋。

turns.en: Number four, you get bored and lose focus. So, let's get real. Highly intelligent people get bored easily. Your brain craves novelty and big ideas. Once you figure something out, doing the actual work feels tedious. You love planning the project, but hate the day-to-day grind of executing it. And I get it. But here's the reality, most success is built in the boring middle. The book that you want to write, 5% is the exciting idea and 95% is sitting down day after day banging out words or editing. And that business you want to build, the concept is thrilling, but actually building it involves a thousand tedious tasks, paperwork, and emails, and routines. Not exactly fun or intellectually stimulating. The smartest people often struggle here. Isn't this work beneath me? No, this work makes you. Consistency is the secret weapon of the average. Those who succeed are willing to do the uninspiring stuff consistently without constantly questioning, is this worth my genius? If boredom is killing your momentum, fix it by reframing the boring stuff as a challenge. Can you show up and execute even when it's not exciting? That's your new game. Also, systematize your life. Build routines and accountability that keep you moving forward even when you're not feeling it. The ability to do boring things consistently is incredibly valuable. Master it and you'll leave the dabbling geniuses in the dust.
turns.zh: 第四，你容易无聊并失去专注。说实话，高智商的人很容易无聊。你的大脑渴望新奇和大想法。一旦你弄明白了，实际做起来就觉得乏味。你喜欢规划项目，但讨厌执行的日常琐碎。我理解。但现实是，大多数成功都是在枯燥的中间阶段建立的。你想写的书，5% 是激动人心的想法，95% 是日复一日敲字或编辑。你想创立的业务，概念令人兴奋，但真正构建它涉及上千个繁琐任务：文书、邮件和常规事务。这并不有趣或刺激智力。最聪明的人常常在这里挣扎。“这工作配不上我吗？”不，是这份工作塑造了你。一致性是普通人的秘密武器。成功的人愿意持续做无趣的事情，而不去不断质疑“这值得我的才华吗？”如果无聊正在扼杀你的动力，那就重新定义无聊的事情为挑战。你能在事情不令人兴奋时仍然出现并执行吗？这就是你的新游戏。此外，系统化你的生活。建立习惯和问责机制，即使你感觉不佳也能推动你前进。持续做无聊事情的能力非常有价值。掌握它，你就会把那些浅尝辄止的天才远远甩在后面。

turns.en: Number five, you live in theory, not reality. Smart people often fall in love with theories and big picture ideas. You might design elegant strategies in your head, craft perfect models of how things should work, but then here's how things do work in real life, which is usually much messier. If you're too attached to the ideal scenario, you can become disconnected from actual reality. So, for example, you might refuse to launch a product until you understand every aspect perfectly. Or you insist on a plan going exactly as imagined, and when it doesn't, you freeze. Meanwhile, less brilliant people are adapting on the fly and they're getting results. So, what's the fix? Embrace reality and adjust. Don't let your beautiful theory stop you from getting your hands dirty. Maybe your strategy should be tweaked. That's fine. Maybe your hypothesis was wrong. Learn and you pivot. Actionable data comes from the real world, not the daydreams. So, don't wait for conditions to match your mental model. Get out there, try stuff, and adjust to the feedback. Remember, your ability to learn and adapt beats your ability to pontificate. Stay grounded and stay flexible.
turns.zh: 第五，你活在理论中，而非现实里。聪明人常常迷恋理论和宏观图景。你可能会在脑海中设计优雅的策略，构建完美的模型说明事物应该如何运作，但现实运作方式通常要混乱得多。如果你过于执着于理想情境，就会与现实脱节。例如，你可能拒绝发布产品，直到你完美理解每个方面；或者你坚持计划完全按想象进行，当不符时你就僵住了。与此同时，不那么聪明的人实时调整并取得成果。那怎么解决？拥抱现实并调整。别让你的美好理论阻止你弄脏双手。也许你的策略需要微调，没关系。也许你的假设错了，那就学习并调整方向。可操作的数据来自现实世界，而非白日梦。所以，不要等待条件符合你的思维模型。走出去，尝试，并根据反馈调整。记住，你学习和适应的能力胜过你夸夸其谈的能力。保持脚踏实地，保持灵活。

turns.en: Number six, you undervalue emotional intelligence and help from others. Success is not a solo brain game. It's a team sport. If you're brilliant, but can't work with other people, you're going to hit a ceiling fast. Maybe you've told yourself, "Others just slow me down." Or, "No one can do it as well as I can." Right? Classic smart person trap. The truth is, someone with average IQ, but great people skills, will outrun a genius who alienates others. Businesses, careers, life, they all run on relationships. If you struggle to communicate, to collaborate, or to ask for help, that's a major blind spot. And I used to try everything alone, and not admit weakness. It nearly broke me. I was too embarrassed to tell anyone that I was struggling. And that loneliness almost made me quit. I learned that if you don't ask for help, you end up stuck and isolated, and far more likely to fail. So, don't let the pride or social awkwardness sabotage you. You don't have to be an extrovert or the life of a party. I'm not. Just develop the skills to connect and communicate. Listen more. Be curious about others. Find mentors and accept their advice. If you lack some of the soft skills, learn it. Being smart means you can grow here, too. Remember, being right isn't enough.
turns.zh: 第六，你低估了情商和他人的帮助。成功不是一个人的脑力游戏，而是一项团队运动。如果你很聪明但无法与他人合作，你会很快触顶。也许你告诉自己：“别人只会拖慢我。”或者“没人能做得和我一样好。”对吧？典型的聪明人陷阱。事实是，智商一般但人际关系出色的人，会超越疏远他人的天才。企业、职业、生活都建立在关系之上。如果你难以沟通、协作或求助，那是一个重大盲点。我以前什么都自己尝试，不承认弱点，这几乎压垮了我。我太尴尬，不敢告诉任何人我在挣扎。那种孤独让我几乎放弃。我学到：如果你不寻求帮助，你会陷入困境、孤立无援，更可能失败。所以，别让骄傲或社交障碍破坏你。你不必成为外向者或派对焦点——我就不是。只需培养连接和沟通的技巧。多听，对他人保持好奇。寻找导师并接受建议。如果缺少某些软技能，就去学习。聪明意味着你在这方面也能成长。记住，仅仅正确是不够的。

turns.en: You have to bring others along if you want to do something big. And if you have a big dream, you'll definitely need others. So, start valuing emotional intelligence as much as book intelligence. It's not soft. It's the glue that holds your success together. Okay, now let's bring this home. We've identified the traps: over analysis, perfectionism, coasting on talent, lack of follow through, living in theory, and flying solo. These are natural tendencies of a powerful mind. But if you leave them unchecked, they become big barriers. The great news is you can overcome each one. Self-awareness is step one. If you've nodded along or winced at any of these points, you're already learning where to improve. Step two is to work with your tendencies instead of against them. Build systems and habits to counteract your weak spots. For example, if you know that you overthink, set strict deadlines or accountability partners to force action even when you're in your head. If you're a perfectionist, set good enough goals, deliberately release version 1.0 of a project when it's 80% there, just to prove to yourself the world doesn't end if it's not perfect. If you get bored, gamify the process or tie boring tasks to a deeper mission that actually fires you up. Practice doing things before you feel fully ready for them. This starts to train you to gather real-world feedback. And if going it alone is not working for you, find a coach, a community, a partner who can push you and keep you accountable. And most of all, shift your identity. Don't see yourself as the smart one, see yourself as the bold one, the action taker, the lifelong learner, the resilient fighter. Yes, you're smart. So, use that brain to strategize ways to get out of your comfort zone instead of clever excuses to stay in it. My mom used to tell me, 'If you have the ability, you have the responsibility. If you can, then you must.' And that hit me hard and stays with me. Your intelligence is a gift, not just for acing tasks or impressing people, but for making an impact. If you're capable of more, you owe it to yourself and the world to do more. I know there's genius inside of you. Everybody has what I call Michael Jordan-level talent or genius at something. Don't let it go to waste because of fear, laziness, or ego. Break the patterns. Do the uncomfortable work. The world needs what you have, and you deserve to fulfill the measure of your potential.
turns.zh: 要做出大事，你必须带动别人。如果你有一个大梦想，你肯定需要他人。所以，开始像重视书本智慧一样重视情商。这不是软技能，而是维系你成功的粘合剂。好了，让我们总结一下。我们已经识别出了陷阱：过度分析、完美主义、依赖天赋、缺乏执行力、活在理论中、单打独斗。这些都是强大头脑的自然倾向。但如果放任不管，它们就会变成巨大的障碍。好消息是，你可以逐一克服它们。自我认知是第一步。如果你在听到这些点时点了头或皱了皱眉，你已经在了解需要改进的地方了。第二步是顺应你的倾向，而不是对抗它们。建立系统和习惯来抵消你的弱点。例如，如果你知道自己思虑过度，就设定严格的截止日期或问责伙伴，迫使自己采取行动，哪怕你还在头脑中纠结。如果你是个完美主义者，设定"足够好"的目标，在项目完成 80% 时故意发布 1.0 版本，只是为了向自己证明世界不会因为不完美而毁灭。如果你感到无聊，就把过程游戏化，或者将无聊的任务与能激发你热情的更深层使命联系起来。在感觉完全准备好之前就开始行动。这能训练你收集真实世界的反馈。如果单打独斗不适合你，就找一个教练、一个社群、一个能推动你并让你保持责任的伙伴。最重要的是，转变你的身份。不要把自己看作聪明的人，而是看作勇敢的人、行动者、终身学习者、坚韧的斗士。是的，你很聪明。所以，用你的大脑来策划如何走出舒适区，而不是找聪明的借口待在舒适区里。我妈妈曾经告诉我："有能力就有责任。如果你能做到，你就必须去做。"这句话深深触动了我，并且一直伴随着我。你的智慧是一份礼物，不仅是为了完成任务或给别人留下印象，更是为了产生影响。如果你有能力做得更多，你就有责任为自己和世界做得更多。我知道你内心有天才。每个人在他所擅长的事情上都有我称之为迈克尔·乔丹级别的天赋或天才。不要因为恐惧、懒惰或自负而浪费它。打破模式。做不舒服的工作。世界需要你所拥有的，你值得发挥你的全部潜力。

ts.sec: Ease of starting a business today

turns.en: If I lost everything tomorrow and had to start a brand new business this year with no audience and no savings, I wouldn't panic because starting a business has never been simpler or cheaper than it is right now. There's never been a time to be an inventor and a pioneer than right now because the world is on fire with new ideas and with AI and space opportunities. We're in the middle of multiple golden ages right now. This is the best time ever in the history of technology ever, period, to start a company. 99% of small businesses you can start with next to no capital. It's more about effort. Americans filed a record 5.67 million business applications in 2025, the most in history, according to the US Census Bureau. So, while everyone online keeps telling you the dream is dead and the economy is rigged, more people are quietly betting on themselves than at any point ever. The US is marking Small Business Week and new data finds more Americans are jumping on the small business bandwagon. Data is showing us that last year a record number of people applying to be small business owners. This isn't just about business, it's about taking back control of your time, your income, your life. And I'm going to walk you through the exact steps I'd follow in order to do it from scratch. Where you spend your time and your energy is one of the most important decisions you get to make in life. I am in control of everything that happens to me. Everything. Everything that will happen in my life, I will be the master of it. One of the most important things you have in your life is time. It's one of your greatest assets or it's your liability.
turns.zh: 如果我明天失去一切，今年必须从头开始一个全新的生意，没有受众，没有积蓄，我不会恐慌，因为创业从未像现在这样简单和便宜。现在正是成为发明家和先驱的最佳时机，因为世界充满了新想法，还有人工智能和太空机遇。我们正身处多个黄金时代之中。这是科技历史上最好的时代，句号，去创立一家公司。99% 的小型企业几乎不需要资本就能起步，更重要的是努力。根据美国人口普查局的数据，2025 年美国人提交了创纪录的 567 万个商业申请，史上最多。所以，当网上每个人都在告诉你梦想已死、经济被操控时，有更多的人在悄悄押注自己，比以往任何时候都多。美国正在庆祝小企业周，新数据显示更多美国人正加入小企业热潮。数据显示，去年申请成为小企业主的人数创下纪录。这不仅仅是关于生意，更是关于重新掌控你的时间、收入和人生。我将向你展示我从零开始的具体步骤。你把时间和精力花在哪里，是你一生中最重要的决定之一。我掌控发生在我身上的一切。一切。我生命中将要发生的一切，我都将是它的主人。你生命中最重要的一件事就是时间，它要么是你最大的资产，要么是你的负债。

turns.en: When I was 20 years old I had a little software company and I was making $300 a month. I was so broke and so ashamed of it that I lied to my own friends and pretended I was living the hustle lifestyle when the truth is I couldn't even afford $20 for a night out and beer. One night I was sitting there crying, ready to quit, completely convinced that I just wasn't smart enough to pull this off. And then something hit me that changed the whole direction of my life and my company. Somebody had already figured this out. I don't have to be a genius, I don't have to have the skills or information yet, and I can model someone who has already done it. So, I went and studied how Bill Gates built Microsoft. He had a software company, I had a software company. Everyone assumes Microsoft blew up because of some genius piece of code, but it didn't. It blew up because Gates made a deal with IBM, the number one computer maker in the entire world at the time. So that every single computer they shipped came with Microsoft software already loaded on it. But here's a part that almost nobody talks about: Microsoft was already a $7 million company before that famous IBM deal ever happened. And when I dug into how Gates got from zero to that first 7 million, the answer was the exact same word: partnerships. He didn't outwork everyone, although he worked very hard. He partnered with people who already had what he needed. So I went back to work the very next morning, copied that one single idea, stopped trying to do everything alone, and closed my first deal for $13,500. Bill Gates kept me in business and I've never once met the man. Right now, you're probably thinking it's easy for me to say all this because I have a big audience today. But if you took every single follower away from me tomorrow, I promise you I would not start by trying to go viral on YouTube. Building an audience from scratch takes three, five, or more years. And most people run out of motivation and money and quit long before it ever pays them anything. So forget about followers at the start. Forget about the perfect logo. Forget about waiting until you feel ready because ready is not the truth. And so here's exactly what I would do instead starting from absolute zero step by step. Get to $96,000 with just four clients. So the first thing I do is ignore almost everything you think a business needs. I would not build a website. I've personally helped launch multi-million dollar companies that didn't even have a website when they signed their first clients. So a website is not the thing standing between you and your money. It's just a comfortable thing to hide behind feeling like you have to get this thing done.
turns.zh: 当我 20 岁时，我有一家小软件公司，每月赚 300 美元。我穷困潦倒，羞愧难当，以至于对朋友撒谎，假装自己过着拼搏的生活方式，而实际上我连 20 美元都拿不出来去外面喝杯啤酒。有天晚上我坐在那里哭，准备放弃，完全相信自己不够聪明，做不成这件事。然后有件事冲击了我，改变了我整个人生和公司的方向。已经有人完成了这个。我不必是天才，我还不必拥有技能或信息，我可以模仿那些已经做到的人。于是我去研究了比尔·盖茨是如何建立微软的。他有一家软件公司，我也有一家软件公司。每个人都以为微软因为某个天才的代码而爆发，但事实并非如此。微软爆发是因为盖茨与 IBM（当时全球第一大电脑制造商）做了一笔交易，使得他们出货的每一台电脑都预装了微软软件。但几乎没有人谈到的一点是：微软在那笔著名的 IBM 交易之前就已经是一家价值 700 万美元的公司。当我深挖盖茨如何从零到 700 万时，答案正是同一个词：合作伙伴关系。他并没有比所有人都努力——尽管他非常努力——他与那些已经拥有他所需资源的人合作。于是第二天早上我回去工作，复制了那一个想法，不再试图独自完成一切，并达成了我的第一笔 13,500 美元的交易。比尔·盖茨让我留在了商界，而我从未见过他本人。现在，你可能觉得我说这些很容易，因为今天我有一个庞大的受众。但如果明天你拿走我所有的粉丝，我向你保证，我不会先试图在 YouTube 上走红。从零开始建立受众需要三到五年甚至更久，大多数人在获得任何回报之前就已经耗尽了动力和金钱而放弃。所以一开始忘掉粉丝，忘掉完美的 Logo，忘掉等到你觉得自己准备好了，因为"准备好了"不是真相。以下是我从零开始会做的具体步骤：用四个客户赚到 96,000 美元。第一步，忽略你认为生意需要的一切。我不会建网站。我亲自帮助推出的数百万美元公司在签下第一个客户时连网站都没有。所以网站不是你与钱之间的障碍。它只是一个让你躲起来感到舒适的东西，总觉得自己必须先完成这个才行。

turns.en: Instead, I'd lock onto one piece of dead simple math and let it run my entire life. I need to get four people paying me $2,000 a month. That is the whole goal. Not 400 customers, not some giant viral launch, not a warehouse full of inventory, just four people who get enough value for you that they will pay you $2,000 every single month. Four clients at $2,000 a month is $96,000 a year, which means you have a almost six-figure business built on just four relationships, and it gives you the survivable cash flow you need to build everything else on top of it.
turns.zh: 相反，我会盯住一个极其简单的数学目标，让它掌控我的整个生活。我需要找到四个人，每人每月付我 2000 美元。这就是全部目标。不是 400 个客户，不是某个大型病毒式发布，也不是装满库存的仓库，仅仅是四个人，他们从你这里获得足够价值，愿意每月付你 2000 美元。四个客户每月 2000 美元，一年就是 96,000 美元，这意味着你仅凭四个关系就建立了一个近乎六位数的业务，并且你有了可持续的现金流，可以在其上构建其他一切。

turns.en: So, the only question that matters on day one is simple. What can you do that's worth $2,000 a month to somebody else? And this year, that list is huge. You can set up AI systems and automations for companies that they're drowning in their busy work. You can run ads on their social media. You can consult in a skill that you already have. Pick the one thing that you're best at and can start delivering this week and price it at $2,000 a month or more so the math works fast and you're not grinding to make a hundred tiny little sales. You do not need a thousand customers. You need four yeses.
turns.zh: 所以，第一天唯一重要的问题很简单：你能做什么对别人来说每月值 2000 美元？今年，这个清单非常大。你可以为那些被繁忙工作淹没的公司搭建 AI 系统和自动化流程。你可以为他们的社交媒体运营广告。你可以用你已经掌握的技能做咨询。挑一件你最擅长且能在本周开始交付的事情，定价每月 2000 美元或更高，这样数学能快速成立，你就不必为了做成一百笔小额销售而辛苦劳作。你不需要一千个客户，你需要四个“是”。

turns.en: And when you stop thinking that you need to build some massive company and you realize you just need four people to say yes, the whole thing stops feeling impossible and starts feeling like something you could go and do this week.
turns.zh: 当你不再认为你需要建立一个庞大的公司，而是意识到你只需要四个人说“是”时，整件事就不再感觉不可能，而开始感觉像是你这周就能去做的事情。

turns.en: Mine the network you already have. Here's where almost everybody freezes. They think they have to go find total strangers and somehow convince them out of thin air to buy from you, right? You don't. To land those first four clients, I would start by auditing the resources and the people already sitting in my phone, in my contacts right now. I don't want you throwing a bunch of spaghetti at the wall, answering fake questions in your own head about whether you're qualified or whether you're ready. I want you to go out to the people you already know.
turns.zh: 挖掘你已经拥有的网络。这几乎是每个人都会僵住的地方。他们认为必须去找完全陌生的人，然后不知怎么凭空说服他们向你购买，对吧？你不需要。为了拿下最初的四个客户，我会从审视我手机里、通信录中已有的资源和联系人开始。我不希望你像往墙上扔一堆意大利面那样，在脑子里回答自己是否合格或是否准备好了这些虚假问题。我希望你去找你已经认识的人。

turns.en: If your brother and your sister run chiropractic clinics or your friend owns a med spa, you go straight to them first. You don't reinvent the wheel. You offer to run their ads or handle the service for them, even cheap or free at the start, so you can learn the industry from the inside and walk away with your very first real testimonials and case studies to share. Those early wins are absolutely everything because proof is the thing that lets you walk into the next conversation and charge full price with total confidence.
turns.zh: 如果你的兄弟姐妹经营脊椎按摩诊所，或者你的朋友拥有一家医疗水疗中心，你直接先去找他们。不要重新发明轮子。你主动提出为他们运营广告或处理服务，一开始甚至可以低价或免费，这样你就能从内部了解这个行业，并且带着你最初的真实推荐和案例研究离开。那些早期的胜利就是一切，因为证明是让你能够走进下一场对话并充满信心地收取全价的东西。

turns.en: Being leads to doing here. The moment you decide that you are the person who solves this problem, you stop researching and you start reaching out to the people who already know you, already like you, and already pick up the phone when you call them. So, you're not starting from zero connections right now, even if it feels that way. Your network, not your wallet, is your real startup capital. And the good news is, you already have one. You just never asked it for anything.
turns.zh: 在这里，“成为”引导“做”。当你决定你就是解决这个问题的人那一刻，你停止研究，开始联系那些已经认识你、喜欢你、并且你一打电话他们就接的人。所以，你并不是从零人脉开始，即使感觉如此。你的网络，而不是你的钱包，才是你真正的创业资本。好消息是，你已经有了一个网络，只是你从未向它要求过任何东西。

turns.en: Make your first offer impossible to turn down. So, when you reach out to those first three people, the worst thing you can do is show up sounding desperate or trying to sell some big, vague, expensive package. Instead, I would lead with a clear result and almost no risk for them at all. So, pick one specific, painful problem that you already know how to fix and offer to fix just that one thing. Tell them you'll do it at a low starter rate or even tie your pay to the result that you get them. So, the only way they lose is if you don't deliver.
turns.zh: 让你的第一个报价让人无法拒绝。所以，当你联系最初的三个人时，最糟糕的做法是表现得绝望，或者试图推销一个庞大、模糊、昂贵的方案。相反，我会用一个明确的结果和几乎没有风险的方式来开场。所以，挑选一个你已经知道如何解决的具体而痛苦的问题，主动提出只解决那一件事。告诉他们你会以一个较低的起步价来做，甚至把你的报酬与他们获得的结果挂钩。这样，他们唯一可能损失的情况就是你没有交付。

turns.en: That one move, it melts their fear away because now they aren't gambling on you. They're just saying yes to an outcome that they already want anyway. So, don't pitch them a long list of features and deliverables because features confuse people. And a confused person, they don't buy from you. So, pitch them the after. Paint a clear picture of exactly where their business will be once their problem is finally gone, and let them feel it for a second, right?
turns.zh: 这一步就能消除他们的恐惧，因为他们现在不是在赌你。他们只是对一个他们本来就想要的结果说“是”。所以，不要向他们推销一长串的功能和交付物，因为功能会让人困惑。而困惑的人不会向你购买。所以，推销“之后”。描绘一幅清晰的画面，一旦他们的问题终于消失，他们的业务会是什么样子，让他们感受一下，对吧？

turns.en: Then, the very second you get them a real result, you ask for two simple things. You ask for a short testimonial in their own words, and you ask them who else they know that has that exact same problem. That becomes a flywheel for you. That one happy client instantly becomes both your proof and your next referral source, and you use that momentum to raise your price a little bit and go land the next one. You're not trying to close a thousand deals or be everywhere at once. You are just trying to make your very first client so ridiculously happy that getting your second, third, and fourth starts to feel almost easy. So, get that first yes this week, over-deliver like your life depends on it, and from there you let the proof do the selling for you.
turns.zh: 然后，一旦你给他们带来了真正的结果，你就要求两件简单的事情：你要一个简短的、用他们自己的话写的推荐，并且你问他们还有谁有同样的确切问题。这就成了你的飞轮。那一个开心的客户立即成为你的证明和下一个推荐来源，你利用这个势头稍微提高价格，然后拿下下一个。你不是要完成一千笔交易，或者同时出现在每个地方。你只是设法让你的第一个客户如此不可思议地开心，以至于获得第二、第三、第四个客户开始感觉几乎是容易的。所以，这周就去拿到第一个“是”，像依靠它生存一样超额交付，然后让证明为你做销售。

turns.en: Build your money 50. So, once you get that first bit of cash flow coming in, you stop hunting one client at a time, and you start scaling through relationships instead of ads. I would build what I call my money 50 list. This is what we teach inside our Movement Makers program. Here's how it works. You pick five different categories of people, and then you go 10 people deep in each category. So, you end up with a written list of 50 names. These are people who, if they did know you, if they did like you, if they did trust you, could each be worth six figures or even seven figures to your business every single year.
turns.zh: 建立你的“金钱 50”列表。所以，一旦你有了第一笔现金流进来，你就停止一次追逐一个客户，而是开始通过关系而不是广告来规模化。我会建立我所说的“金钱 50”列表。这是我们在 Movement Makers 项目中教授的内容。它的运作方式是：你选择五个不同类别的人，然后在每个类别中深入十个人。这样，你最终得到一个包含 50 个名字的书面列表。这些人如果认识你、喜欢你、信任你，每个人每年可能为你的业务带来六位数甚至七位数的价值。
