turns.en: And here's the key that most people miss. These usually are not your current customers. They're referral partners. They might be CPAs or lawyers or property managers, agency owners, the people who already have a deep trusted relationship with the exact audience that you're trying to reach. One single CPA can send you 30 clients without you even spending a dollar on advertising because their clients already do whatever they recommend. So, write those 50 names down on one page, you put it where you see it every day, and you treat that list like like it's made of gold because getting in front of those 50 people is the entire game. You don't need a million customers, you need a handful of powerful relationships. The person with the best relationships wins every single time, and relationships are completely free to build if you're simply willing to give first before you ever ask for anything.
turns.zh: 这里是大多数人错过的关键：这些通常不是你当前的客户，而是推荐合作伙伴。他们可能是注册会计师、律师、物业经理、代理机构老板，这些人与你试图接触的精确受众已经建立了深厚的信任关系。仅仅一个注册会计师就可以在不花一分钱广告的情况下给你带来 30 个客户，因为他们的客户已经会按照他们的推荐去做。所以，把那 50 个名字写在一页纸上，放在你每天都能看到的地方，像对待金子一样对待那张清单，因为出现在那 50 个人面前就是整个游戏。你不需要一百万客户，你需要几个强有力的关系。拥有最佳关系的人每次都赢，而建立关系完全免费，只要你愿意在索取任何东西之前先给予。

turns.en: Start a biz dev show. Now, how do you actually get in front of your money 50 list when these are busy, important, successful people? Here's the mistake most people make. If you email them and ask to grab a coffee and pick their brain, they will ignore you every time because everybody on earth wants their time and attention. So, you flip the whole thing around. You start a simple interview show, what I call a biz dev show, and you invite those exact 50 people to come on as your guests. Almost nobody ever asked them for an interview before, so they say yes because everybody loves being treated like the expert. And here's the beautiful part.
turns.zh: 启动一个业务拓展节目。那么，当你的“金钱 50”列表上都是些忙碌、重要、成功的人时，你如何真正出现在他们面前呢？这是大多数人犯的错误。如果你发邮件约他们喝咖啡、讨教经验，他们每次都会忽略你，因为世界上每个人都想要他们的时间和注意力。所以，你要完全翻转这件事。你启动一个简单的采访节目，我称之为业务拓展节目，然后邀请那 50 个人作为你的嘉宾。几乎没有人曾邀请他们做过采访，所以他们会说“是”，因为每个人都喜欢被当作专家对待。而美妙的部分在这里：

turns.en: You don't need a fancy studio, you don't need expensive gear, you don't need a big audience because going viral is not the point and the view count doesn't matter at all here because they're telling their story and they don't get a lot of attention typically. The only metric you care about is the relationship. You spend a full hour, you make them look great, you tell their story, you're genuinely curious about their work and somewhere in the middle of the conversation you ask one strategic question connected to what you do just to quietly plant a seed in their mind. And then, the moment you stop recording, you make your move. You tell them that you'd love to be their second opinion or their go-to person in case any of their clients have an issue that obviously you know how to deal with. In 1 hour you just turn a complete stranger into a warm potential partner who wants to help you and it cost you exactly $0. There is no faster way on this planet to earn someone's trust than to put them in the spotlight and champion them before you ever ask for a single thing back.
turns.zh: 你不需要昂贵的录音室，不需要昂贵的设备，也不需要庞大的观众群——因为走红不是目的，播放量也完全不重要。他们只是在讲述自己的故事，而他们通常得不到太多关注。你唯一在意的指标是关系。你花整整一个小时，让他们光彩照人，讲述他们的故事，你对他们的工作真正充满好奇，然后在对话的中段，你问一个与你领域相关的战略性提问，悄悄在他们心里播下一颗种子。录制结束后，你立刻行动。你告诉他们，你愿意当他们的参谋或依赖对象，万一他们的客户遇到你擅长解决的问题，你可以接手。一小时内，你就把一个陌生人变成了一位温暖的潜在合作伙伴，且愿意帮助你，而成本恰恰是零。在这个星球上，没有比先把你捧上舞台、在索取任何回报之前就为你欢呼更快赢得信任的方法了。

turns.en: Trade your time for a piece of the upside. The next move is the one that truly changes everything and it's the one that I'd be the most aggressive about this year if I'm trying to build my business. When you're first setting out it's totally fine to charge a flat monthly fee, but the real wealth is never in trading just your hours for dollars. It's in owning a piece of what you help actually build. So, the second I had proof of what I could actually get for results for people, I would stop just being a hired hand. I would walk into an established business that's already making money and say, 'Hey, give me a percentage of the company and I'll come in and be your growth person and your sales engine. If you really want to scale your upside, you take X% of a business in exchange for driving their growth instead of just giving them a flat rate every month.' I did this exact same thing with a bunch of agencies I started. I taught them everything I knew about YouTube. I took a 25% split. They had the other 75% and today they built up and run seven-figure businesses. I didn't need money to make that deal. I needed a skill that got results and the guts to ask for a percentage instead of just a paycheck. Most people they're too scared to ask so they stay employees of their own business forever. If you can deliver real results for someone, then you have the responsibility, I think, to ask for some real upside. If you can, then you must.
turns.zh: 用时间换股权。下一步才是真正改变一切的关键——如果今年我要创业，这是我会最积极去推动的一步。刚起步时，收固定月费完全没问题，但真正的财富从来不在于用时间换工资，而在于拥有你帮助创造的成果的一部分。所以，一旦我有能力证明自己能为别人带来实际结果，我就不再做单纯的打工者。我会走进一家已经在赚钱的成熟企业，说：「嘿，给我公司的一部分股份，我来当你的增长负责人和销售引擎。如果你真想扩大收益，就分给我一定比例的公司股份，我来驱动增长，而不是每月收固定费用。」我在自己创办的好几家代理机构中都用了同样的方法。我把所有关于 YouTube 的知识教给他们，我拿 25% 的分成，他们拿另外 75%。如今，他们都建起了并运营着七位数的生意。我做成这笔交易不需要钱，我需要的是能带来结果的技能，以及要求分股权而不是只拿工资的勇气。大多数人因为不敢开口，所以永远是自己生意的员工。如果你能为别人带来真实结果，那你就有责任去要求真正的高收益。如果你能做到，那就必须去做。

turns.en: Let AI be the team you can't afford yet. The last thing I do, and honestly, the biggest reason there has never been a better time in human history to start a business than right now, is to lean on AI like it's an entire team working for you for free. When I started out, I couldn't afford a designer. I couldn't afford a writer, an assistant, or a developer, a site. I did a lot of it myself, badly, painfully, slowly, and it held me back for years. You don't have that excuse anymore. Do you need your offer written, your emails drafted, your brand designed, your research done, a simple tool built for a client? AI can do a strong first draft of every single one of these things in minutes. And your only job is to add your judgment and your taste on top of it. That's exactly why setting up AI systems for other businesses is one of the best $2,000 a month offers you can possibly sell right now, because every business owner on Earth knows they need this, and almost none of them have any idea how to actually do it. So, don't use AI to replace your thinking, use it to delete your excuses. Every single time you catch yourself saying, 'I can't afford to do that part.' Stop and ask whether AI can do that part for you. And in this year, the honest answer is almost always going to be yes. The person who wins today is not the one with the biggest budget or the fanciest university degree. It's the one who's actually willing to roll up their sleeves and use the tools that are already there in your pocket.
turns.zh: 让 AI 成为你雇不起的团队。我最后要说的，也是人类历史上现在比任何时期都更适合创业的最大原因，就是依靠 AI，它就像一支免费为你工作的完整团队。我刚开始时，请不起设计师、写手、助理、开发人员或网站团队。很多事情我都自己干，干得糟糕、痛苦、缓慢，这拖了我好几年。你不再有这个借口了。你需要写方案、起草邮件、设计品牌、做调研、为客户搭建简单工具吗？AI 可以在几分钟内为每一项提供扎实的初稿。你唯一要做的就是在此基础上加上你的判断和品味。正因为如此，为其他企业搭建 AI 系统是现在最能卖到每月 2000 美元的服务之一，因为每个企业主都知道他们需要这个，而几乎没人知道具体怎么做。所以，不要用 AI 取代你的思考，用它来消除你的借口。每当你发现自己说「我负担不起这部分」时，停下来问问 AI 能不能为你做这部分。今年，诚实的答案几乎总是「能」。今天赢的人不是预算最大或文凭最漂亮的，而是真正愿意撸起袖子、使用口袋里已经有的工具的人。

ts.sec: Your first move is the one that matters

turns.en: Your first move is the one that matters. So, that's the entire plan, and I want you to notice that not one single step required money, a degree, or permission from anybody. It just required you deciding to start and being willing to model the people who have already done it instead of trying to be a genius all on your own. You don't have to figure it all out today. You just have to take that first step before you feel ready. You do not need money to start a business that makes $10,000 a month.
turns.zh: 你的第一步才是关键。所以，这就是完整的计划，我希望你注意到，没有一步需要钱、学历或任何人的许可。你只需要决定开始，并愿意模仿那些已经做到的人，而不是独自当个天才。你不必今天就想通所有事情，你只需要在感觉自己准备好之前迈出第一步。你不需要钱来创办一个月入一万美元的生意。

ts.sec: The power of hustle and examples

turns.en: What I would say, these days you do not have to have money to make money, which is incredibly powerful.
turns.zh: 我想说的是，现在你不必用钱来赚钱，这一点极其强大。

turns.en: The biggest lie the system feeds you is that wealth requires capital. But today, your time and hustle are the only currency that actually matters.
turns.zh: 体制给你灌输的最大谎言是财富需要资本。但今天，你的时间和奋斗才是唯一真正重要的货币。

turns.en: For those who are older, who have no more passion, they're burnt out, they're exhausted, it is the highest form of currency because it's not about what you know. You don't need to know the secret formulas, you don't need to have secret connections. If you just get your behavior right and your thinking right, you can do well.
turns.zh: 对于年龄较大、没有激情、筋疲力尽的人来说，奋斗是最高的货币形式——因为它不在于你知道什么。你不需要知道秘密公式，不需要拥有秘密关系。只要你的行为正确、思维正确，你就能做得好。

turns.en: And if you keep waiting for a perfect moment or some rich investor to save you, you will stay trapped in the exact same financial struggle for the rest of your life. Let's look at John Paul DeJoria. He was completely broke and living in his car. He only had $700 to his name. He didn't let his empty bank account stop him from building his business.
turns.zh: 如果你一直等待完美时机或某个有钱的投资者来拯救你，你将一生都被困在同样的财务困境中。我们来看看约翰·保罗·德约里亚。他身无分文，住在车里，全部身家只有 700 美元。他没有让空荡荡的银行账户阻止他创业。

turns.en: So, my car was my home where I'm going to live. Got a blanket, a pillow in there. And then to eat, I figured out a way to eat off $2.50 a day.
turns.zh: 所以，我的车就是我的家，我在里面放了一条毯子和一个枕头。为了吃饭，我找到了每天只花 2.5 美元的方法。

turns.en: Paul Mitchell was $700. My mother threw in 350. My mom put in some money not even knowing that I thought she was throwing life away for a little bit.
turns.zh: Paul Mitchell 是 700 美元。我母亲投了 350 美元。她投了一些钱，甚至不知道我当时觉得她有点在浪费人生。

turns.en: He partnered with a friend and they started selling hair care products door-to-door. They knocked on doors every single day because they had no money for marketing.
turns.zh: 他找了一个合伙人，开始挨家挨户推销护发产品。他们每天都敲门，因为没有钱做营销。

turns.en: I filled my car full of our products and drove right up Ventura Boulevard in Studio City. It was full of salons. And knocked like encyclopedias, okay, door-to-door to door selling my product, right? I had challenges. One, no distributor, no advertising money. So, I went out and it took me a week to get 12 salons to buy my product.
turns.zh: 我把车装满产品，直接开到 Studio City 的 Ventura 大道，那里到处都是沙龙。我像推销百科全书一样挨家挨户地推销我的产品。我遇到了挑战：没有经销商，没有广告费。我花了一周时间才让 12 家沙龙购买我的产品。

turns.en: And today, John Paul Mitchell Systems makes over a billion dollars a year. He proved that you only need hustle to get out of poverty.
turns.zh: 如今，John Paul Mitchell Systems 年收入超过十亿美元。他证明了只需要奋斗就能摆脱贫困。

turns.en: Now, you're probably thinking that door-to-door sales is dead and you don't have a physical product to sell anyway. Don't let that be your excuse. Today, the internet is your neighborhood and your digital skills are your products. You have access to billions of people right here on your phone for free.
turns.zh: 现在，你可能觉得挨家挨户推销已经过时了，而且你也没有实体产品可卖。别让这成为你的借口。今天，互联网就是你的社区，你的数字技能就是你的产品。你通过手机就能免费接触到数十亿人。

turns.en: So, here are 10 specific businesses you can launch today with $0 to start making real money. Number one, AI operations consultant.
turns.zh: 那么，这里有 10 个你可以今天就用零资金启动、开始赚真金白银的具体生意。第一，AI 运营顾问。

turns.en: Small business owners are terrified of falling behind, but they have absolutely zero time to learn how artificial intelligence actually works. They see the news, but they do not know where to start. And this is where you step in. You can become an AI consultant using just your computer and free tools. Recent data shows that 64% of businesses expect AI to increase their productivity. You do not need a computer science degree to do this. You can use free platforms to write their marketing emails or automate their customer service replies. You test a few prompts, you track the hours it saves them, and you optimize their daily workflow. When you take the stress off an entrepreneur's shoulder and give them their time back using AI, you are providing massive value. So, reach out to 10 local business owners today. Tell them you will automate their inbox for free to prove your worth. When you show them how much time you save them, they will happily pay you for a monthly retainer.
turns.zh: 小企业主们非常害怕落后，但他们完全没有时间学习人工智能到底是如何工作的。他们看到了新闻，却不知道从何入手。而这就是你介入的地方。你只需用一台电脑和免费工具，就能成为一名 AI 顾问。最新数据显示，64% 的企业期望 AI 能提高他们的生产力。你不需要计算机科学学位就能做这件事。你可以用免费平台来撰写他们的营销邮件，或自动化他们的客服回复。你测试几个提示词，记录节省下来的时间，然后优化他们的日常工作流程。当你用 AI 减轻创业者的压力、帮他们找回时间时，你就在提供巨大的价值。所以，今天就联系 10 个本地企业主。告诉他们你将免费自动化他们的收件箱来证明你的价值。当你展示为他们节省了多少时间后，他们会很乐意按月支付你报酬。

turns.en: Number two, custom AI assistant builder. Every company wants their own version of ChatGPT trained on their specific data, but they have no idea how to build it. You can build custom AI assistants for businesses without writing a single line of code. Harvard Business Review explains that anyone can now build custom AI models using simple text instructions. You simply take a company's training manuals, upload them into a custom GPT builder, and give them a chatbot that can instantly answer any employee question. Don't let the lack of cash be an excuse. You can use your time to learn this free skill and then charge businesses thousands of dollars to implement it. It is a skill and you can get better at any skill if you put in the reps. Go to five local plumbing and or HVAC companies. Ask them what their most common customer question is. Build a free chatbot that answers that exact question and send it to them.
turns.zh: 第二，定制 AI 助手构建器。每家公司都希望拥有自己版本的 ChatGPT，并基于其特定数据进行训练，但他们不知道该怎么做。你可以为零代码为公司构建定制 AI 助手。《哈佛商业评论》指出，现在任何人都可以用简单的文本指令来构建定制 AI 模型。你只需拿公司的培训手册，上传到定制 GPT 构建器中，就能给它们一个能立即回答任何员工问题的聊天机器人。不要让缺钱成为借口。你可以用时间学习这门免费技能，然后向企业收取数千美元来实施它。这是一项技能，任何技能只要勤加练习都能进步。去找五家本地管道或暖通空调公司，问他们最常见的客户问题是什么。构建一个能准确回答该问题的免费聊天机器人，然后发给他们。

turns.en: Number three, high-ticket remote sales. If you want to make $10,000 a month quickly, you need to sell expensive things. You do not need to invent the expensive thing, you just need to sell it for someone else. High-ticket remote sales means that you take phone calls, Zoom calls for experts who are selling $5,000 plus coaching programs or software. Entrepreneur Magazine notes that remote sales requires zero upfront cost and offers massive earning potential. You don't need to build a website or run ads. The business owner already does the marketing. They just need someone to close the deal. So, you get on the phone or Zoom call, you ask the prospect about their problems, and you offer the solution. You get paid a 10% commission on everything that you sell. If you close one $5,000 deal a day, you make $500 a day. You have to endure the learning curve. You'll be terrible at your first 10 sales calls. Expect to suck in the beginning, but your 11th call might completely change your financial reality.
turns.zh: 第三，高客单价远程销售。如果你想快速月入一万美元，你需要卖昂贵的东西。你不需要发明昂贵的东西，你只需要替别人卖。高客单价远程销售意味着你替那些销售 5000 美元以上教练课程或软件的专家接电话、打 Zoom 电话。《企业家》杂志指出，远程销售零前期投入，且收入潜力巨大。你不需要建网站或投广告。企业主已经做了营销，他们只需要有人来成交。所以，你上电话或 Zoom，询问潜在客户的问题，然后提供解决方案。你从所有销售额中获得 10% 的佣金。如果你每天成交一笔 5000 美元的生意，你每天就赚 500 美元。你必须经历学习曲线。你的前 10 个销售电话会表现糟糕。一开始要接受自己很烂，但第 11 个电话可能会彻底改变你的财务状况。

turns.en: Number four, short-form video strategist. Every business knows they need to be on TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and Instagram Reels. The problem is that most business owners are stiff, boring, and have no idea how to hook a viewer. You can become a short-form video strategist. HubSpot data shows that short-form video can have a high return on investment. You do not just edit the videos, you tell the business owner exactly what to say. You write the hooks. You can use free AI tools to add captions and fast cuts. I hated my first 350 videos. I could not watch them back because I was so embarrassed, but I kept putting in the reps. You can use your phone to film a local real estate agent and give three tips for buying a house. Edit it for free. When that video gets them a new client, they will hire you to do it every single week.
turns.zh: 第四，短视频策略师。每家企业都知道自己需要在 TikTok、YouTube Shorts 和 Instagram Reels 上出现。问题是大多数企业主都很僵硬、无聊，不知道如何吸引观众。你可以成为一名短视频策略师。HubSpot 数据显示，短视频可以带来高投资回报率。你不仅编辑视频，还告诉企业主具体该说什么。你写钩子。你可以用免费 AI 工具添加字幕和快剪。我讨厌自己最初拍的 350 个视频，我甚至不敢回看，因为太尴尬了，但我坚持练习。你可以用手机拍摄本地房产中介，给出三个买房技巧。免费剪辑。当那个视频为他们带来一个新客户时，他们就会每周都雇你来制作。

turns.en: Number five, email list monetization. Most creators and businesses have a list of past customers sitting completely ignored in an email database. That is pure cash waiting to be collected. You can offer to manage and monetize their email list. Campaign Monitor reports that email marketing produces an average return of $36 for every $1 spent. So, you go to a business and you say you will write one weekly email to their list for free. You tell them you only get paid a percentage of the new sales that come directly from your emails. This becomes a no-brainer for the business owner because there's zero risk for them. You use AI to help you write engaging stories and practical offers and it costs you $0 to start.
turns.zh: 第五，邮件列表变现。大多数创作者和企业都有一个过去客户的列表，完全被忽略在邮件数据库中。那都是等着去收的现金。你可以提供管理和变现他们邮件列表的服务。Campaign Monitor 报告称，邮件营销每花费 1 美元平均能带来 36 美元的回报。所以，你去找一家企业，说你会每周免费为他们写一封邮件发给列表。你告诉他们，你只从你邮件直接带来的新销售额中抽取一定比例。这对企业主来说无需思考，因为他们零风险。你用 AI 来辅助撰写引人入胜的故事和实用的优惠，而且启动成本为零。

turns.en: Number six, B2B lead generation. Business-to-business companies survive on leads. If an agency sells a $10,000 service, they desperately need to talk to qualified buyers. You can build a business simply by finding those buyers and setting up the meetings. G2 reports that lead generation is the top priority for marketers, but over 60% struggle to find high-quality leads. You do not need to be an expert in their industry. You just need to be relentless on LinkedIn and email. You find the target audience, you send a highly personalized message, and you book the meeting on the agency's calendar. You charge a flat fee for every qualified meeting that shows up. Your purpose comes from your pain. If you know what it feels like to be broke, use that pain to motivate your hustle. Reach out to 50 marketing agencies today and offer to book their next three meetings for free.
turns.zh: 第六，B2B 线索生成。企业对企业（B2B）公司靠线索生存。如果一家机构出售价值一万美元的服务，他们急需与合格买家交谈。你可以通过找到那些买家并安排会议来建立一个业务。G2 报告称，线索生成是营销人员的首要任务，但超过 60% 的人难以找到高质量线索。你不需要成为他们行业的专家。你只需要在 LinkedIn 和邮件上坚持不懈。你找到目标受众，发送高度个性化的信息，然后在机构的日历上预约会议。你为每个出现的合格会议收取固定费用。你的动力来自你的痛苦。如果你知道身无分文是什么感觉，就用那种痛苦来激励你的奋斗。今天就联系 50 家营销机构，主动提出免费为他们预订接下来的三场会议。

turns.en: Number seven, no-code automation architect. Businesses lose thousands of hours every year doing boring, repetitive tasks. They copy data from emails into spreadsheets and then from spreadsheets into billing software. You can eliminate this manual work by becoming a no-code automation architect. Zapier highlights that no-code tools allow anyone to build complex software integrations without knowing how to program. You connect your different apps so they talk to each other automatically. You are giving people their time back. Wealthy people will gladly pay you to get their time back. And you can learn these platforms for free on YouTube. The best teachers in the world are on YouTube right now. So look at a local accounting firm, see what manual data entry they do, build an automation that does it instantly, and show them how it works.
turns.zh: 第七，无代码自动化架构师。企业每年浪费数千小时在无聊重复的任务上。他们把数据从邮件复制到电子表格，再从电子表格复制到计费软件。你可以通过成为无代码自动化架构师来消除这种手工劳动。Zapier 强调，无代码工具允许任何人在不懂编程的情况下构建复杂的软件集成。你连接不同的应用，让它们自动互相通信。你在帮人们找回时间。富有的人会很乐意付钱让你帮他们赢回时间。你可以在 YouTube 上免费学习这些平台。世界上最好的老师现在就在 YouTube 上。所以，找一家本地会计事务所，看看他们做了什么手动数据录入，构建一个能立即完成这项工作的自动化方案，并向他们展示效果。

turns.en: Number eight, YouTube click-through rate specialist. If a YouTube video has a bad title and a boring thumbnail, nobody will click on it. It does not matter how good the video is. Creators are desperate for higher click-through rates. You can build a highly profitable business by designing thumbnails and writing titles. YouTube officially states that 90% of the best-performing videos have custom thumbnails. You can use free software to design the graphics, you study the psychology of what makes people click, you find a YouTuber with 50,000 plus subscribers who gets terrible views, you redesign their last three thumbnails for free and send them over. When their views double, they will hire you to do every video going forward.
turns.zh: 第八，YouTube 点击率专家。如果一个 YouTube 视频标题差、缩略图无聊，没人会点进去，不管视频本身多好。创作者极度渴望更高的点击率。你可以通过设计缩略图和撰写标题来建立一个高利润业务。YouTube 官方指出，90% 表现最好的视频都有自定义缩略图。你可以用免费软件设计图形，研究让人点击的心理学，找一个拥有 5 万以上订阅者但观看量很差的 YouTuber，免费重新设计他最近三个缩略图并发送过去。当他的观看量翻倍后，他就会雇你为之后的每个视频做设计。

turns.en: So stop worrying about looking successful and start doing the unglamorous work that actually pays. And bonus tip for anybody who's really trying to take YouTube split testing seriously, I built a software that's called brandlytics.ai. We'll link it up in the description below. That's the tool that big YouTubers are using to be able to identify the videos that are underperforming and run the split test to improve their performance. Number nine, paid community manager. The biggest trend online right now is private paid communities. Creators are launching groups where members pay $99 a month to learn, but these creators do not have the time to actually run the community. Influencer Marketing Hub reports that the creator economy is now worth over a hundred billion dollars, driven heavily by direct community monetization. So you can step in as a community manager. You welcome new members, you host weekly video calls, you organize the content. You are the glue that holds the group together. Find a creator that you already follow and love. Message them and offer to moderate their communities for free for 2 weeks. When you increase their member retention, they will happily pay you a percentage of the monthly recurring revenue. And number 10, starting a YouTube channel. You have a computer in your pocket with a camera that connects you to the entire world. Starting a YouTube channel costs you $0. You just press record and you start sharing your story, your skills, your journey. Forbes highlights that building a digital audience is one of the most powerful low-cost business models available today. The key is your titles and your thumbnails and you have to hook the viewer instantly. So, commit to posting one video a week for an entire year. You might feel like you're too shy and nobody will care about what you have to say. I'm an introvert and I struggled deeply with putting myself out there, too. But, I realized that quality of thought right here is more important than quality of production. So, your lighting might be bad and your audio might be a little echoey, but if your message helps one person change their life, it's worth it. So, stop overthinking the perfect setup, take out your phone, look into the lens, and teach someone how to solve a problem that you have already solved for yourself. Your audience is waiting for you to step up and lead. So, hopefully now your excuses are officially gone. You have the tools, the strategies, and the power to completely rewrite your financial future right now. Do not let another day slip by wishing your life was different while you still are stuck standing still. Take the risk, do the work, and build the life you actually deserve.
turns.zh: 所以，别再担心看起来是否成功，开始做那些真正带来回报的不起眼工作吧。对于那些真正想认真做 YouTube 分众测试的人，我建了一个叫 brandlytics.ai 的软件，我们会在下方描述里放上链接。大 YouTuber 们正用这个工具来找出表现不佳的视频，并运行分众测试来提升效果。第九点，付费社群管理员。现在网上最大的趋势就是私密付费社群。创作者们正在推出每月 99 美元的付费学习群，但他们自己没时间管理。网红营销中心（Influencer Marketing Hub）报告说，创作者经济现在价值超过一千亿美元，很大程度上由直接的社群变现驱动。所以，你可以担任社群管理员。欢迎新成员、主持每周视频通话、整理内容——你是把大家凝聚在一起的黏合剂。找一个你已经关注并且喜欢的创作者，私信他们，免费为他们的社群做两周的版主。当你提升了他们的成员留存率时，他们很乐意向你支付每月经常性收入的一定比例。第十点，开一个 YouTube 频道。你口袋里就有一台带摄像头的电脑，它连接着整个世界。开 YouTube 频道零成本，你只需按下录制键，然后开始分享你的故事、技能和经历。《福布斯》指出，建立数字受众是当下最强大的低成本商业模式之一。关键在于你的标题和缩略图，你必须立即吸引住观众。所以，承诺一年内每周发布一个视频。你可能会觉得自己太害羞，没人会关心你说什么。我也是内向型人格，曾经也挣扎着走出去。但我意识到，想法的质量比制作质量更重要。所以，你的灯光可能很差，音频可能有点回声，但只要你的信息能帮助一个人改变生活，那就值得。别再纠结于完美的设备，拿出手机，看着镜头，教别人如何解决你已经解决过的问题。你的观众正在等你站出来引领他们。所以，希望现在你的借口已经正式消失。你现在就拥有工具、策略和力量，可以彻底改写你的财务未来。不要再让一天溜走，一边希望生活不同，一边却停在原地。冒险，行动，建立你真正应得的生活。

turns.en: You don't need multiple streams of income to get rich. Three wonderful businesses is more than you need in this life to do very well. And three of those will be better than 100 average businesses. Splitting your focus across five different side hustles guarantees that you fail at all of them. Diversification is a protection against ignorance. The resource you have to deal with is your time and how you spend time. So, I'm always trying to make sure that I'm only doing the things that are important. Well, focusing is saying yes, no. Focusing is about saying no. If you refuse to go all in on your one true genius, you'll stay stuck in the exact same painful place 10 months from now. Bill Gates and Warren Buffett are two of the richest men in history. One night, they were at a dinner party together. Someone asked them both to write down the single most important factor for their massive success on a piece of paper. They did not look at what the other person was writing, but when they turned their papers over, they had both written the exact same word, focus. So, Bill and I, right after we met, had a group of 20 write down on a sheet of paper one word that they thought accounted for their success. And Bill and I, who may only have twice, didn't know what the other one was writing down. We both wrote down the same word, which was focus. They did not build their wealth by doing 10 things at once. They picked one thing and poured every ounce of their energy into it. Now, you're probably thinking that focusing on just one thing is way too risky. You want a backup plan, but your backup plan is actually a trap. When you give yourself a plan B, you almost guarantee that plan A will fail because you don't lack time or resources, you lack the courage to bet on yourself completely.
turns.zh: 你不需要多种收入来源才能致富。三个好生意就足够你这辈子做得非常好了。而这其中的三个，会好过一百个普通生意。把注意力分散在五个不同的副业上，几乎注定你会全部失败。分散投资是抵御无知的手段。你需应对的资源是你的时间，以及你如何使用时间。所以，我总在确保自己只做重要的事。嗯，专注就是说是和不。专注在于说不。如果你不愿全身心投入你真正的天赋所在，那么十个月后你还会困在同样痛苦的位置。比尔·盖茨和沃伦·巴菲特是历史上最富有的两个人。有一天晚上，他们一起参加一个晚宴。有人请他们各自在纸上写下他们认为对巨大成功最重要的单一因素。他们没有看对方写的是什么，但当他们翻过纸时，两人都写出了同一个词：专注。所以，比尔和我——我们刚认识时，曾让大约二十个人在一张纸上写下他们认为自己成功的一个词。而比尔和我——我们可能只见过两次面——不知道对方在写什么。我们写下了同一个词：专注。他们不是靠同时做十件事积累财富的。他们挑了一件事，把每一分精力都投入进去。现在你也许在想，专注一件事风险太大了。你想要一个备用计划，但备用计划实际上是个陷阱。当你给自己准备了 B 计划时，你几乎注定了 A 计划会失败，因为你缺乏的不是时间或资源，而是完全赌一把的勇气。

turns.en: When you finally commit, everything changes. So, here are 10 money rules that will force you to focus and skyrocket your net worth. Charge higher prices to fewer people. You think you need thousands of customers paying a tiny amount to get rich. That's completely wrong. Most entrepreneurs are terrified of charging higher prices. You lower your hourly rates because you think it will attract a massive crowd. Instead, you attract people who don't value your time. It is much easier to find 10 customers who will pay you $1,000 than to find 1,000 customers who will pay you $10. If you want to build a half a million dollar business, you need clients who are worth $50,000 a year to you. You don't want to do all the grueling work for clients paying you pennies. You need to upgrade your offers immediately. Harvard Business Review shows that premium pricing actually increases perceived value. Customers respect your service more when they pay significantly more. So, if you sell a software product, don't just charge $20 a month and hope they figure it out. Charge $2,000 a month and personally help the clients win massive victories. You get vastly better results. Your clients get vastly better results. You build a highly profitable business that doesn't run you into the ground. This specific pricing strategy leads directly into how you fund your daily operations. Fund your business with clients, not investors. People think that raising capital from venture capitalists is the ultimate goal. Raising capital is a trap. If you get an investor to give you $50,000, they will take half your business. You might make $50,000 just by landing two high-ticket clients. When you raise money, you buy a boss. You lose your freedom and your control. The Wall Street Journal reported that three out of four venture-backed startups fail completely. Your clients should fund your growth. When you deliver massive value, they will pay you gladly. You use that exact money to build your website and hire your team. You keep all your equity. You stay the owner of your dream. You don't have to report to a board of directors who only care about fast returns. You get to build the business on your own terms. Keeping your equity matters, but you also have to protect your daily time. Stop over-delivering on low-ticket offers. You are spending way too much time on deals that pay you almost nothing.
turns.zh: 当你终于下定决心，一切都会改变。所以，这里有 10 条金钱法则，会迫使你专注，并让你的净资产飙升。向更少的人收取更高的价格。你以为需要成千上万的低价客户才能致富，大错特错。大多数企业家害怕提高价格。你降低时薪，以为会吸引大批客户，结果吸引来的却是并不珍惜你时间的人。找到 10 个愿意付你 1000 美元的客户，比找到 1000 个付你 10 美元的客户要容易得多。如果你想建立一个 50 万美元的生意，你需要每年值 5 万美元的客户。不要为了那些付你几毛钱的客户做所有苦差事。你得立刻升级你的报价。《哈佛商业评论》显示，高价其实能提升感知价值。客户付得越多，就越尊重你的服务。所以，如果你卖软件产品，不要只收 20 美元一个月然后指望他们自己摸索。收 2000 美元一个月，并亲自帮助客户取得巨大胜利。你的结果会好得多，客户的结果也好得多，你建立的是一家高利润且不会拖垮自己的企业。这个具体的定价策略直接通向你的日常运营资金来源。用客户的钱来资助你的生意，而不是靠投资者。人们以为从风投那里融资是终极目标，但融资是个陷阱。如果你拿到投资者给的 5 万美元，他们会拿走你一半的业务。你只需谈下两个高价客户就能赚 5 万美元。当你融资时，你买来了一个老板，你失去了自由和掌控权。《华尔街日报》报道，四分之三的风投支持的初创公司完全失败。你的客户应该为你的增长买单。当你提供巨大价值时，他们会很乐意付钱。你就用这些钱建网站、雇团队。你保留全部股权，你仍是梦想的主人。你不必向只关心快速回报的董事会汇报，你可以按自己的方式打造企业。保留股权很重要，但你也要保护自己的日常时间。别再在低客单价产品上过度交付了。你花了太多时间在几乎不赚钱的交易上。

turns.en: Now, you might over-deliver and spend 40 hours on a five-figure deal. You undercut yourself and charge 10,000 instead of 40,000. That burns you out and destroys your profit margins. You bend over backwards for people who demand everything and pay nothing. The Pareto principle proves that 80% of your results come from 20% of your effort. You need to stop doing the work that doesn't scale. Serve your premium clients deeply. Let the low-paying clients go. They complain the most and they pay the least. Free up your schedule so you can focus on high-level strategy. Your time is your most valuable asset. When you stop wasting hours on low-value tasks, you open up space for massive income leaps.
turns.zh: 你可能会过度交付，在五位数交易上花 40 个小时。你低估了自己，只收 10,000 而不是 40,000。这会让你筋疲力尽，摧毁你的利润率。你为那些要求一切却什么都不付的人鞠躬尽瘁。帕累托法则证明，80% 的结果来自 20% 的努力。你需要停止做那些无法规模化的工作。深度服务你的优质客户。让低付费客户离开。他们抱怨最多，付钱最少。腾出你的日程，专注于高层的战略。你的时间是你最宝贵的资产。当你停止在低价值任务上浪费时间时，你就为巨大的收入飞跃打开了空间。

ts.sec: Track your money like your health

turns.en: And once you control your time, you must control your tracking. Track your money like you track your health. You can't improve what you don't measure accurately. Most people treat their finances like it's a mystery. You avoid looking at your bank account because you're afraid of what you will see. You have to stop hiding from your own numbers. If your physical goal is to drop your weight to 185 lb and live completely pain-free, you track your sleep and your resting heart rate and your weight. You might wear your Aura ring like I do to monitor your daily readiness score. You treat your physical health like a serious data project. You need to demand real numbers. You need to do the same thing with your total net worth. Check your bank accounts daily. Track your daily spending. The American Psychological Association calls this the measurement effect. Simply tracking a specific behavior automatically changes that behavior for the better. When you track every single dollar, you instantly stop wasting your money on things that don't matter. You gain absolute clarity and total control over your future. Tracking gives you the hard data you need to build a real system that scales.
turns.zh: 一旦你掌控了时间，就必须掌控你的追踪。像追踪健康一样追踪你的金钱。你无法改善那些你未准确衡量的东西。大多数人把财务当作谜团。你避免看银行账户，因为害怕看到什么。你必须停止逃避自己的数字。如果你的身体目标是减到 185 磅并完全无痛生活，你会追踪睡眠、静息心率和体重。你可能会像我一样戴上 Aura 戒指来监控每日准备度评分。你把身体健康当作一个严肃的数据项目。你需要真实的数据。对自己的净资产也要做同样的事。每天查看银行账户。追踪每日开支。美国心理学会称之为“测量效应”。仅仅追踪一个特定行为就会自动使该行为变得更好。当你追踪每一美元时，你会立刻停止把钱浪费在无关紧要的事情上。你获得绝对的清晰度和对未来的完全控制。追踪给你所需的数据，来建立一个真正可扩展的系统。

ts.sec: Build a machine, not a job

turns.en: Build a machine, not just a job. Now, most entrepreneurs just buy themselves a terrible job, right? If you stop working, your income stops entirely. That is not a business. That is a cage. You need to build a machine around your work. So, look at your daily systems. You have to ask yourself, if your business can generate $20,000 a month if you don't show up to work. Harvard Business Review highlights that process-driven companies scale much faster and survive longer than founder-dependent companies. So, document your daily steps. Hire people to do the tedious tasks that you hate doing. Step out of the daily grind so you can focus on the bigger vision. Your job is to replace yourself as fast as possible.
turns.zh: 打造一台机器，而不仅仅是一份工作。现在，大多数企业家只是给自己买了一份糟糕的工作，对吧？如果你停止工作，你的收入就完全停止了。那不是生意，那是牢笼。你需要围绕你的工作建造一台机器。所以，审视你的日常系统。你必须问自己，如果不去上班，你的生意每个月还能产生 20,000 美元吗？《哈佛商业评论》指出，流程驱动的公司比依赖创始人的公司扩展得更快、生存得更久。所以，记录你的日常步骤。雇人来做你讨厌做的繁琐任务。走出日常的苦差事，这样你才能专注于更大的愿景。你的工作就是尽可能快地取代自己。

ts.sec: Start a video show to network with wealthy clients

turns.en: Start a business development show to get referrals. Cold calling is completely dead. You need a better way to network with wealthy clients. One of the things we teach inside of our Movement Makers program is to start a simple video show. Interview the top 50 people in your specific industry. Invite them on your show and tell your story. Nobody asked them for an interview. And when they say yes, that 30-minute conversation turns into a deep relationship. You don't have to be a professional broadcaster. You just have to be curious. LinkedIn data shows that 85% of all jobs and major deals are filled via networking. So, don't ask for a sale. Ask for the interview. Bring them massive value first. The referrals flow naturally because you build real trust over time.
turns.zh: 开办一个业务发展节目来获取推荐。冷拨电话已经完全过时了。你需要更好的方式与富裕客户建立联系。我们在 Movement Makers 项目中教授的一件事就是开设一个简单的视频节目。采访你所在行业的顶尖 50 人。邀请他们上你的节目，讲述你的故事。没人问过他们是否接受采访。当他们答应时，那 30 分钟的对话就会变成深厚的关系。你不必是专业播音员，你只需要保持好奇。领英数据显示，85% 的工作和重大交易都是通过人脉完成的。所以，不要请求销售，请求采访。先给他们带来巨大的价值。推荐自然而来，因为你随着时间的推移建立了真正的信任。

turns.en: But, building that trust requires you to listen more than you speak. Stop giving free advice until they ask. You want to help absolutely everyone. You see a problem and you immediately try to fix it. Giving advice before someone asks creates instant friction. They don't want what they didn't ask for. You push them away when you try to solve a problem they haven't admitted that they have. You need to ask them probing questions instead. Keep asking questions until they finally ask you what you would do in their situation. Psychology Today notes that unsolicited advice is almost always perceived as harsh criticism. So, wait patiently for the clear invitation. When they ask you for your help, they are fully ready to pay for your premium solution. You can only guide the people who are truly ready to be guided.
turns.zh: 但是，建立信任需要你多听少说。在他们开口之前，不要提供免费建议。你想帮助所有人。你看到问题就立刻试图解决。在别人开口之前给出建议会立刻产生摩擦。他们不想要他们没要求的东西。当你试图解决他们尚未承认的问题时，你会把他们推开。相反，你应该问他们探索性的问题。不断提问，直到他们最终问你在他们的情况下会怎么做。《今日心理学》指出，主动提出的建议几乎总是被视为严厉的批评。所以，耐心等待明确的邀请。当他们向你寻求帮助时，他们已经完全准备好为你的优质解决方案付费。你只能引导那些真正准备好被引导的人。

ts.sec: Focus on your first five clients

turns.en: This level of patience, though, requires you to narrow your focus completely. Focus on the first five clients, not the next 5,000. You're stressing about how to scale to millions of users. You don't even have your perfect five clients yet. Stop worrying about massive growth at the very beginning. If you have a high-level program like we have, Movement Makers, figure out how to make it incredibly fun and life-changing for just five people. You have to nail the foundation before you build the skyscraper. Kevin Kelly, the famous essay '1,000 True Fans'. It proves you don't need millions of followers to build massive wealth. If you change five lives completely, those people will bring you the next 50 clients. Focus small so you can eventually grow huge. Treat your early clients like royalty.
turns.zh: 不过，这种程度的耐心要求你完全缩小你的焦点。专注于前五个客户，而不是接下来的 5,000 个。你为如何扩展到数百万用户而焦虑，但你甚至还没有五个完美的客户。在开始时不要担心大规模增长。如果你有一个像我们这样的高级项目 Movement Makers，想办法让它对仅仅五个人来说变得极其有趣并改变人生。你必须打好地基，然后才能建造摩天大楼。Kevin Kelly 著名的文章《1,000 个铁杆粉丝》证明你不需要数百万粉丝来创造巨大财富。如果你完全改变了五个人的生活，那些人会给你带来接下来的 50 个客户。从小处着眼，这样你最终才能变得巨大。像对待皇室一样对待你的早期客户。

ts.sec: Keep money in top five, but never number one

turns.en: But this type of focus requires the right internal motivation. Keep money in your top five, but never number one. If money is your only goal, you will quit when the journey gets hard. Money is a powerful tool. It is the fuel for your car. You absolutely need it, but it can't be your destination. Your main mission has to be bigger than your bank account. You have to have a cause that you would work on even if you were not getting paid. The National Institutes of Health published studies showing that intrinsic motivation sustains long-term effort much better than external rewards like cash. Put money as your number two or three on your priority list. Let your true purpose be number one. You will actually make far more money this way because you won't burn out.
turns.zh: 但这种专注需要正确的内在动力。把金钱放在前五，但永远不要放在第一。如果金钱是你唯一的目标，当旅程变得艰难时你就会放弃。金钱是一个强大的工具，是你汽车的燃料。你绝对需要它，但它不能是你的目的地。你的主要使命必须比你的银行账户更大。你必须有一个即使没有报酬也愿意为之努力的事业。美国国立卫生研究院发表的研究表明，内在动机比现金等外部奖励更能维持长期努力。把金钱放在你优先清单的第二或第三位。让你的真正目标成为第一。这样你实际上会赚更多的钱，因为你不会精疲力竭。

ts.sec: Put your family's future before your ego

turns.en: And your deeper purpose usually ties directly back to the people you love. Put your family's future before your ego. You are making terrible financial decisions based on how you look to strangers on the internet. You need to stop caring about digital likes and start caring about your real legacy. Look closely at your family. Look closely at your husband or wife. They do not care about your daily view count. They care about the secure life you are building for them. You need to focus on what actually moves the needle for your household first. Pew Research Center states that family support is the primary driver of long-term life satisfaction and financial stability. So swallow your pride, do the boring work, send the emails, build the true wealth that changes your family tree forever. Your next move.
turns.zh: 而你更深层的目标通常直接与你爱的人相关。把家人的未来放在你的自我之前。你正根据自己在互联网陌生人眼中的形象做出糟糕的财务决策。你需要停止关心数字点赞，开始关心你真正的遗产。仔细看看你的家人，看看你的丈夫或妻子。他们不关心你每天的播放量，他们关心你为他们建立的安全生活。你需要首先专注于那些真正影响你家的事情。皮尤研究中心指出，家庭支持是长期生活满意度和财务稳定的主要驱动力。所以，收起你的骄傲，做无聊的工作，发送邮件，建立能永远改变你家谱的真正财富。你的下一步。

turns.en: So you have the exact rules laid out in front of you right now. The only thing missing is your absolute commitment to take action. So stop waiting for the perfect moment and start building your real wealth today. Most of the richest people in the world started with nothing, which means that your empty bank account is not the main thing that's holding you back. Woz and I started Apple in my parents' garage when I was 20.
turns.zh: 所以，现在你面前已经有了确切的规则。唯一缺少的是你对采取行动的绝对承诺。所以，不要再等待完美时机，从今天开始建立你真正的财富。世界上最富有的人大多白手起家，这意味着你空空的银行账户并不是阻碍你的主要原因。沃兹和我 20 岁时在我父母的车库里创办了苹果。

turns.en: People like me, I was born in a very poor family. I never got a great education. I failed all the examinations. For what reason? I don't know. But later I realized I don't have money, I don't have technology, I don't have a lot of good backgrounds who have a rich uncle or something. No. The only thing I competed with my people than the young people is let's compete for 10 years later. Look at the Forbes 400, the richest people in America, and you'll find that a record 70% of them built their fortune from scratch with no inheritance, no head start, just a person who decided to begin. The list is mostly a list of self-made billionaires. 70% of the Forbes 400 made their fortune. So, the fact that you're starting from zero today decides only one thing, which is whether the person you become 10 years from now thanks you for starting or wishes that you had. One of the things that I've learned in my business is that the mistakes are where all the learning is. And actually, the mistakes and the imperfect stuff, that's where the gold is, everybody. Look, when I'm 80 years old, I want to have minimized the number of regrets that I have. I don't want to be 80 years old in a quiet moment of reflection thinking back over my life and cataloging a bunch of major regrets.
turns.zh: 像我这样的人，出生在一个非常贫穷的家庭。我没受过良好的教育，所有的考试都失败了。为什么？我不知道。但后来我意识到，我没有钱，没有技术，也没有好的背景，比如有个富有的叔叔之类的。没有。我和同龄人竞争的唯一的资本就是——让我们竞争10年后的未来。看看福布斯400富豪榜，美国最富有的人，你会发现创纪录的70%的人是白手起家的，没有继承遗产，没有先发优势，只是一个决定开始的人。这份榜单基本上都是白手起家的亿万富翁。福布斯400富豪榜上有70%的人是自己创造财富的。所以，你今天从零开始只决定了一件事：10年后的那个你，是会感谢你今天的开始，还是会希望你当时开始了。我在生意中学到的一件事是，错误才是所有学习的来源。实际上，错误和不完美的地方才是金矿，各位。你看，当我80岁时，我想尽量减少遗憾的数量。我不想在80岁时，在安静的反思时刻回顾一生，列出一堆重大的遗憾。

turns.en: Let me tell you about a man who got rejected by everybody. His name is Jack Ma. He grew up poor in China and he failed his university entrance exam twice. I failed a key primary school test for two times. And I failed like three times for the middle school. For three years I tried to fail in the university. When he finished school, he applied for 30 different jobs and got rejected by all 30 of them. KFC opened up in his town. 24 people applied and 23 of them got hired. He was the only one they turned down, the only one. I failed so many times. People probably know that I've applied jobs for so many jobs. Over 30 jobs, all rejected. Not even got a chance. 24 of us were interviewed for a KFC job. 23 accepted. I was the only guy rejected. He finally landed work as a English teacher making about $12 a month. Then in 1995, he traveled to America and saw the internet for the very first time, and something clicked in him. He went home with an idea nobody believed in. And in 1999, he gathered 17 of his friends into a small apartment, and they started a little company called Alibaba. People told him he was crazy, that nobody in China would ever shop online. He kept going anyway. He kept getting the door slammed in his face, and he kept on knocking on new ones. And in 2014, Alibaba went public and raised about $25 billion. It was the biggest stock offering the world had ever seen at that point. And Jack Ma became one of the richest people on the planet. From being rejected by KFC to one of the top five wealthiest people in the world, he didn't have the money, he didn't even know how to code, he didn't come from a big powerful family or some fancy school. By every measure the world uses to decide who was going to make it, Jack Ma was supposed to fail. He was supposed to stay an English teacher making $12 a month for the rest of his life. And everyone around him agreed. So, the only thing that he had that you don't is that he refused to stop.
turns.zh: 让我给你讲一个被所有人拒绝的人的故事。他叫马云。他在中国贫困长大，大学入学考试两次失败。我小学关键考试两次不及格，中考也考了三次才考上。大学我考了三年。毕业之后，他申请了30份工作，全部被拒。肯德基在他镇上开店，24人应聘，23人被录用，他是唯一被拒绝的那个，唯一一个。我失败过很多次。人们可能知道我申请了很多工作，超过30份，全部被拒，连机会都没有。我们24个人面试肯德基，23个被录用，只有我被拒。最后他当了一名英语老师，月薪大约12美元。1995年，他去美国第一次看到了互联网，心里突然有了灵感。他带着一个没人相信的想法回了家。1999年，他召集了17个朋友，在一间小公寓里创办了一家小公司，叫阿里巴巴。人们说他疯了，说在中国没人会在网上购物。但他坚持下去了。一次次被拒之门外，他一次次敲开新的门。2014年，阿里巴巴上市，融资约250亿美元，是当时世界上最大的IPO。马云成为全球最富有的人之一。从被肯德基拒绝到全球前五大富豪，他没有钱，甚至不会编程，没有显赫的家庭或名校背景。用世界上衡量成功的所有标准来看，马云本应失败。他本应一辈子当个月薪12美元的英语老师，他周围的人都这么认为。所以，他拥有而你没有的唯一东西就是——他拒绝停止。

turns.en: Okay, so here's what you might be thinking. That's Jack Ma, that's China, it's a billion person market, right? Right place, right time, and you don't have any of that. You've got bills, a job you're tired of, you got no money saved, nobody in your corner, right? I've been broke, I've been stuck, I've been exactly where you are when I was 19. I turned down a six-figure dream job to join a tiny startup for $300 a month. I worked out of my partner's dining room. I ate McDonald's french fries and bean salad because it's the cheapest food that I could find. I was so embarrassed that I lied to my friends and said I was just hustling when I was really just broke. And one night I called my partner and I quit and I cried my eyes out. And the next morning I knocked on his door and just went back to work. I had no money. I had no clue. What I figured out though is that you don't need to be a genius to win. You just need to start. And then you need to refuse to stop. And you are sitting on more tools today than I ever had. So let me show you exactly how you can get rich when you're starting from nothing. Step number one. Start with the skill you already have. I think your purpose comes from your pain. The thing that you struggled through the most, the problem that you've already solved for yourself, that's the seed of how you make money. So you don't need a brand new idea that nobody's ever heard of. You need a real problem that real people will pay to fix. And the best place to find that is in what you already know. So look at your own life and ask, 'What do people already come to me for? What did I have to figure out the hard way? What would I paid someone to teach me a year ago?' That's your starting point. So when I was broke, I didn't have capital, I didn't have any connections. What I had was the ability to study what worked and apply it. So you have that skill right now today, too. That's somebody out there will pay for. So maybe you're really good with words and writing. Maybe you can edit video or you can sell or you can organize chaos or you can teach something that you take for granted. That skill that you take for granted is the key. It feels easy to use so you assume it's easy for everyone and it isn't. The stuff that comes naturally to you is exactly the same stuff that someone else is struggling with right now and would gladly pay to have it solved. So write down three things that people already trust you with. The friend who always asks you to look at their resume, the cousin who needs you to fix their phone, the coworker who copies how you handle clients. That is not just random things, that is the market, that's people telling you where your value already is. So stop waiting to feel qualified, right? I believe the being leads to the doing. The moment you decide that you're someone who helps people with this skill, the actions start to follow and the confidence shows up after the action, not before. You build belief by starting, not by waiting until you feel ready because ready is not actually real. You already have the skills I can pay you your first dollars and your job is to stop hiding it and start moving towards it. Step number two, build your money 50 list. So, this is something we teach inside of our Movement Maker's program. This is the fastest way I know to make real cash from zero. Here's what you do. You don't need a giant audience, you need 50 of the right people. So, open up Google Maps or LinkedIn, find 50 people who could either become a high-value client or send you high-value clients.
turns.zh: 好了，你可能在想：那是马云，那是中国，一个十亿人口的市场，对吧？天时地利，而你什么都没有。你有账单，有厌倦的工作，没有存款，没有支持你的人，对吧？我曾经破产，曾经困顿，19岁时和你一模一样。我拒绝了一份六位数的梦想工作，加入了一个月薪300美元的小型创业公司。我在合伙人的餐厅里办公，吃麦当劳薯条和豆沙拉，因为那是我能找到的最便宜的食物。我太尴尬了，对朋友撒谎说我只是在忙，其实我真的很穷。一天晚上，我打电话给合伙人说要辞职，哭得稀里哗啦。第二天早上，我又敲开他的门，回去工作了。我没钱，没头绪。但我发现，你不需要是天才才能赢。你只需要开始，然后拒绝停止。而你现在拥有的工具比我当时多得多。所以让我告诉你，如何从零开始变富。第一步：从你已经拥有的技能开始。我认为你的目标来自你的痛苦。你最挣扎的事，你已经为自己解决的问题，那就是你赚钱的种子。你不需要一个没人听说过的新点子。你需要一个真实的问题，人们会愿意付钱解决。而找到它的最好地方就是你已经知道的东西。所以审视你的生活，问自己：人们已经因为什么来找我？我艰难学会了什么？一年前我愿意花钱请人教我什么？那就是你的起点。当我破产时，我没有资本，没有人脉。我拥有的就是研究什么有效并加以应用的能力。你现在也拥有这个技能。有人愿意为此付钱。也许你很擅长文字和写作，也许你会剪辑视频、销售、整理混乱，或者教别人你觉得理所当然的东西。你觉得理所当然的技能就是关键。你觉得用起来轻松，就认为对每个人都轻松，但其实不是。你天生就会的东西，正是别人现在挣扎并愿意付钱解决的问题。所以写下三件人们已经信任你做的事：总是让你看简历的朋友，需要你修手机的表亲，模仿你处理客户方式的同事。这不是随机的事，这是市场，是人们在告诉你你的价值在哪里。所以别再等自己觉得合格了，好吗？我相信“身份”会引导行动。当你决定自己是一个用这项技能帮助别人的人时，行动就会随之而来，自信出现在行动之后，而不是之前。你通过开始来建立信念，而不是等到感觉准备好了，因为“准备好了”并不真实。你已经拥有技能，可以让我付给你第一笔钱，你的任务是停止隐藏它，开始朝它迈进。第二步：建立你的“50人清单”。这是我们在“运动创造者”项目中教授的内容，是我知道的从零赚到真钱最快的方法。做法如下：你不需要庞大的观众，你只需要50个对的人。打开谷歌地图或领英，找到50个人，他们要么能成为高价值客户，要么能给你带来高价值客户。

turns.en: That's what happens when you stop drowning in just busy work and you pour your time into the thing that actually pays you. Your time is your seed money. So we want to plant it where it can grow, not just where it keeps you busy. Step number seven: guard your belief and your circle. This is the one that decides whether you make it because starting with nothing is as much a head game as it is a money game. Remember that every single person around Jack Ma told him he was crazy. If he had believed them, then there's no Alibaba. The world will hand you a hundred reasons to quit before you ever see your first real win. And a lot of those reasons will come from people who love you but have never done what you're trying to do. So you have to protect your belief. Feed your mind every day with people who have already walked the road through their books, their videos, their words, so the voice in your head telling you to keep going. That voice becomes louder than the voices around you telling you to stop. And watch who you spend time with because slowly you become the average of the five closest people to you. Like Jim Rohn says, find the ones who are building something, who light you up instead of draining you, who help move you towards things. When you start with nothing, your belief in yourself is the very first asset that you're actually building, before the money, before the clients, before any of it. So you need to guard it, you need to protect it, because everything else you're going to build gets built on top of that.
turns.zh: 当你不再深陷于琐碎的工作，而是把时间投入到真正能带来回报的事情上时，奇迹就会发生。你的时间就是你的种子资金。所以，我们要把它种在能生长的地方，而不是仅仅让它忙个不停。第七步：守护你的信念和你的圈子。这一步决定了你是否能成功，因为白手起家既是心理游戏，也是金钱游戏。记住，马云身边的每个人都曾说他疯了。如果他相信了他们，那就没有阿里巴巴了。在你看到第一个真正的胜利之前，世界会给你一百个理由放弃。其中很多理由来自那些爱你但从未做过你正在尝试之事的人。所以，你必须保护你的信念。每天用那些已经走过这条路的人的思想喂养你的大脑——通过他们的书、他们的视频、他们的话语——这样你内心的声音会告诉你继续前进。这个声音会变得比周围让你停止的声音更响亮。注意你和谁在一起，因为慢慢地你会成为与你最亲密的五个人的平均值。正如 Jim Rohn 所说，找到那些正在建设的人，那些点燃你而不是耗尽你的人，那些帮助你向目标前进的人。当你白手起家时，你对自己的信念是你真正建立的第一项资产，比金钱、比客户、比任何东西都早。所以你需要守护它，保护它，因为你将要建造的一切都建立在它之上。

ts.sec: Starting from Nothing Is a Blessing

turns.en: So here's what I want you to walk away with. Starting from nothing is not a curse. It's awesome. It's a blank slate. You've got no bad habits to unlearn, no reputation to protect, nothing to lose, and everything to build. Jack Ma had less than you have right now, and he changed the world. I had $300 a month and bean salad every day, and I built a life that I love.
turns.zh: 所以，我希望你带走的是：白手起家不是诅咒。它太棒了。它是一张白纸。你没有坏习惯需要改掉，没有名誉需要保护，没有什么可失去的，却有一切可以建设。马云拥有的比你现在的还少，他却改变了世界。我每个月只有 300 美元，天天吃豆沙拉，但我建立了我热爱的生活。

ts.sec: Action Steps and the Right Time to Start

turns.en: Every single thing I just gave you, starting with your skill, building the money 50 list, selling high value, starting before you're ready, modeling what is working, protecting your time, and guarding your belief, every one of those things is something that you can begin today with $0. The only thing standing between you and your first win is the decision to start swinging. You have a skill, you have the internet, you have AI, and you have this one moment to decide. You know when the best time to start was? Years ago. You know the second best time? Right now. How about right now? If you can do this, and you can, then you must.
turns.zh: 我刚才给你的每一件事——从你的技能开始、建立赚钱 50 人名单、销售高价值产品、在准备好之前开始、模仿有效的方法、保护你的时间、守护你的信念——每一件你都可以在今天用 0 美元开始。你和第一次胜利之间唯一的障碍就是开始挥杆的决定。你有一项技能，你有互联网，你有 AI，你有这决定的瞬间。你知道最好的开始时间是什么时候吗？几年以前。你知道第二好的时间吗？就是现在。现在怎么样？如果你能做到，而且你能，那么你必须去做。

ts.sec: The Flawed System and Personal Choices

turns.en: Security in a corporate job doesn't exist anymore. The safe job is about to be unsafe. So far this year, companies have cut more than 800,000 jobs. That's the highest number we have seen since the pandemic. West Michigan company plans to cut hundreds of jobs. Tonight, Grand Rapids based Acrisure is telling us that artificial intelligence is replacing actual employees. Over 80% of students feel they learn nothing about entrepreneurship in school, even though most want to start their own businesses. The only non-gamble in life is going on offense. And you've been taught that going on offense is the gamble, because the school system was literally created to create factory workers. Our school systems teach us nothing about money. Nothing. It's pathetic. So at 25 I recommitted to my education, but this time I started studying not things that were in books, but people that had actually created wealth. Sticking to a traditional career path limits your impact, keeps you miserable, and stops you from sharing your unique genius with the world. My sense is that even for the kids that get into the elite colleges at this point, it's like you've passed some Mandarin examination in China, but you're just so exhausted. You're never going to do anything more with the rest of your life. You're burned out at 18. You take a calculated risk to start a company realizing you may forego a couple of years of studying coming out of your job, and whatever else. That's a great risk to take. And if you don't take that risk, I think you have a very high chance that you end up regretting that. Where you spend your time and your energy is one of the most important decisions you get to make in life.
turns.zh: 企业工作的安全感已不复存在。安稳的工作即将变得不稳定。今年到目前为止，公司已经裁员超过 80 万，这是自疫情以来我们看到的最高的数字。西密歇根一家公司计划裁减数百个岗位。今晚，位于大急流城的 Acrisure 告诉我们，人工智能正在取代真正的员工。超过 80% 的学生觉得他们在学校里没有学到任何关于创业的知识，尽管大多数学生想创办自己的企业。生活中唯一不是赌博的是主动出击。而你被教导说主动出击是赌博，因为学校系统根本就是为培养工厂工人而创建的。我们的学校系统什么都不教我们关于钱的知识。什么都不教。可悲。所以 25 岁时我重新投身教育，但这一次我开始学习的不是书本里的东西，而是那些真正创造了财富的人。坚持传统的职业道路会限制你的影响力，让你痛苦，并阻止你与世界分享你独特的天赋。我的感觉是，即使是那些进入精英大学的孩子，就像你通过了中国的某种普通话考试，但你太累了。你在余生中再也做不了什么了。你 18 岁就精疲力竭了。你承担一个经过计算的风险去创办一家公司，意识到你可能会放弃从工作中出来学习的一两年时间，以及其他东西。这是一个值得冒的巨大风险。如果你不冒这个风险，我认为你最终后悔的可能性非常大。你把时间和精力花在哪里，是你一生中最重要的决定之一。

ts.sec: You Don't Need Money to Make Money

turns.en: When I was 19, I had the hardest choice to make. I was in university and I had a job offer for a safe six-figure investment banking job. It was a job everybody wanted, but I also had a chance to own 30% of a biotech startup making only $300 a month. And I picked the startup. I chose the struggle, eat beans for lunch because the thought of sitting in a cubicle doing work I hated scared me more than being broke. I knew I had to take control of my own income. Think about Colonel Sanders at 65 years old. He had a tiny $105 social security check. He didn't go looking for a greeter job at a local store. He took his chicken recipe, hit the road, and slept in his car. He faced 1,009 rejections before finally someone said yes to his franchise idea. He proved that you can create massive wealth at any age just by owning your own ideas instead of working for someone else. Brian Chesky and Joe Gebbia couldn't pay their rent in San Francisco. They didn't rush out to get safe normal jobs. Instead, they put three air mattresses on their floor and charged people to sleep there during a local design conference. That simple idea turned into Airbnb. They created a $100 million company because they looked for a creative way to solve a problem instead of looking for a safe corporate salary. And right now you might be thinking that you need thousands of dollars in the bank to start making your own money. You think you need rich parents or some giant loan to succeed. And that's not true. Colonel Sanders was broke at 65. Airbnb started with three cheap air mattresses. You don't need money to make money. You just need a problem to solve and the courage to take a step. I'm going to show you exactly how to start generating your own income from scratch right now. Solve your own biggest problem. To make money without a job, you've got to realize where value actually comes from. You get paid for bringing value to other people. The absolute easiest way to bring value is to look directly at your own life. Your purpose comes from your pain. Whatever you struggle with the most is exactly what you want to help other people overcome. So think about your past. If you had a hard time getting fit and you figured out a system that works. That system is your new business. If you struggled with anxiety and found a way to manage it. That method, that's your business. You don't need a fancy business degree to make this happen. You just need to be one step ahead of the person that you're trying to help. Over 62% of billionaires are totally self-made.
turns.zh: 我 19 岁时，面临最艰难的选择。我还在上大学，有一份稳定的六位数投行工作邀请，这是人人都想要的工作，但我也有机会拥有一家生物技术初创公司 30% 的股份，每月只赚 300 美元。我选择了初创公司。我选择了奋斗，午餐吃豆子，因为坐在格子间做我讨厌的工作的想法比身无分文更让我害怕。我知道我必须掌控自己的收入。想想 65 岁的桑德斯上校。他只有一张 105 美元的社会保障支票。他没有去当地的商店找一份迎宾员的工作。他带着他的鸡肉配方上路，睡在车里。他面对了 1009 次拒绝，最终有人对他的特许经营想法说了“是”。他证明了，你可以通过拥有自己的想法而不是为他人工作，在任何年龄创造巨大的财富。Brian Chesky 和 Joe Gebbia 在旧金山付不起房租。他们没有急于找安稳的普通工作。相反，他们把三个充气床垫放在地板上，在当地一个设计会议期间收费让人们睡在那里。这个简单的想法变成了 Airbnb。他们创造了一家价值 1 亿美元的公司，因为他们寻找创造性的方式解决问题，而不是寻找安稳的公司薪水。现在你可能认为你需要银行里有几千美元才能开始赚钱。你认为你需要富有的父母或一笔巨额贷款才能成功。那不是真的。桑德斯上校 65 岁时破产了。Airbnb 从三个便宜的充气床垫开始。你不需要钱来赚钱。你只需要一个待解决的问题和迈出一步的勇气。我现在就向你展示如何从零开始创造自己的收入。解决你自己最大的问题。要没有工作也能赚钱，你必须认识到价值实际上来自哪里。你因为给他人带来价值而获得报酬。带来价值的最简单方法就是直接审视自己的生活。你的使命来自你的痛苦。你挣扎最多的正是你想帮助他人克服的。所以想想你的过去。如果你很难健身并找到了一个有效的系统，那个系统就是你的新生意。如果你与焦虑作斗争并找到了管理它的方法，那个方法就是你的生意。你不需要一个花哨的商业学位来实现它。你只需要比你试图帮助的人领先一步。超过 62% 的亿万富翁完全是白手起家。

turns.en: Meaning they've created their wealth by solving real problems, not by inheriting cash. People pay you to solve their problems because they desperately want to skip the pain that you have already went through. You're selling speed and convenience. If you can help someone skip five years of painful trial and error, they pay you for that shortcut. So don't think you need to invent the next big tech platform to be successful. Look at the local business in your town. They need help with their marketing, their accounting, their daily operations. They've got massive problems right now. You can step in and help fix those problems. When you focus entirely on serving others and solving their actual pain points, you stop acting like an employee begging for a simple paycheck and you start acting like a true entrepreneur commanding a premium price. You stop handing out weak resumes and start handing out powerful solutions for problems. This simple shift in your mindset changes everything. You go from hoping that a boss picks you to knowing that the market desperately needs you. So, you've got to stop looking for a company to hire you and start looking for a person to help. The money will always follow the value you provide. So, if you fix a $100 problem, you make a little bit of money. If you fix a $1,000 problem, you make a lot more money. It's simple. Your job right now is to identify the most expensive problem you know how to solve and then go find the exact people who are crying out for that exact solution.
turns.zh: 也就是说，他们是通过解决实际问题来积累财富的，而不是靠继承现金。人们付钱给你，是因为他们迫切想跳过你曾经经历过的痛苦。你卖的是速度和便利。如果你能帮某人跳过五年的痛苦试错，他们就会为这个捷径买单。所以，别以为非要发明下一个大型科技平台才能成功。看看你所在城镇的本地生意——他们在营销、会计、日常运营上都需要帮助。他们现在就有巨大的问题。你可以介入并帮助解决这些问题。当你完全专注于服务他人、解决他们的真实痛点时，你就不再像个乞讨薪水的员工，而是像一个真正的企业家，能收取溢价。你不再递出薄弱的简历，而是递出强大的问题解决方案。这个简单的思维转变会改变一切。你从指望老板挑中你，变成知道市场急需你。所以，你必须停止寻找雇佣你的公司，开始寻找需要你帮助的人。金钱永远会追随你提供的价值。如果你解决了一个 100 美元的问题，你就赚一点钱；如果你解决了一个 1000 美元的问题，你就能赚更多钱。就这么简单。你现在的任务就是识别出你知道如何解决的最昂贵的问题，然后找到那些迫切需要那个解决方案的人。

turns.en: But, finding a problem is only the first step because your surroundings might be secretly destroying your chances of success. Change your environment to change your mind. Your current environment is perfectly designed to keep you exactly where you are right now. So, if your friends all have traditional jobs, they'll constantly tell you to get a safe job. They aren't trying to hurt you, they just don't understand your big vision. Research shows that you're up to 61% more likely to adopt the exact habits and mindsets of the people closest to you. So, if you want to make your own money, you must change your daily environment. You've got to completely shut out the negativity. Limit your access to people who doubt you and fill that empty space with extreme positivity and the specific messages you actually want to hear. So, if you can't find supportive friends in your own town yet, go find them online. Read powerful books, listen to great podcasts, watch amazing YouTube videos from the exact people who are already doing what you want to do. I started my YouTube channel because I wanted to surround myself with some of the greatest minds in history. I wanted Steve Jobs and Warren Buffett in my ear every single morning. I wanted their intense ambition to rub off on me. You've got to be incredibly intentional with your daily morning routine. Don't wake up and immediately scroll through toxic social media or that pressing news. Start your day with content that makes you believe in yourself. When you consume greatness daily, it starts to feel completely normal. Soon the idea of settling for a boring cubicle will feel totally insane to you. You'll begin to think bigger, act faster, and expect so much more of yourself. You can literally rewire your entire brain for massive success just by changing what you look at and who you listen to every single day. So treat it like a garden, right? Your mind is a garden. If you plant negative seeds, you'll grow a massive negative life. If you plant seeds of belief, you'll grow a massive awesome empire. You've got to ruthlessly protect your focus. So stop giving your attention to things that make you feel small and start obsessing over the ideas that make you feel powerful. The moment you change your inputs, the outputs will transform forever.
turns.zh: 但是，找到问题只是第一步，因为你的周围环境可能正在暗中破坏你的成功机会。改变环境，从而改变思维。你当前的环境完美地设计成让你保持在原地。如果你的朋友都有传统工作，他们会不断告诉你要找份安稳的工作。他们不是想伤害你，只是不懂你的宏大愿景。研究表明，你采取身边最亲近的人的习惯和思维模式的可能性高达 61%。所以，如果你想自己赚钱，就必须改变你的日常环境。你必须彻底屏蔽消极因素。限制你接触那些怀疑你的人，用极度的积极性和你真正想听到的特定信息来填补那个空间。如果你在镇里找不到支持你的朋友，那就上网找。读有力量的书，听好的播客，看那些已经做到你想做的事的人的精彩 YouTube 视频。我创办自己的 YouTube 频道，是因为我想让自己被历史上一些最伟大的头脑包围。我希望每天早晨都能听到史蒂夫·乔布斯和沃伦·巴菲特的声音。我希望他们强烈的雄心能影响我。你必须对你的每日晨间例行公事极其有意识。不要一醒来就刷有毒的社交媒体或那些紧迫的新闻。用让你相信自己内容开始新的一天。当你每天吸收伟大时，它会开始变得完全正常。很快，安于一个无聊隔间的想法会让你觉得完全疯狂。你会开始想得更远，行动更快，对自己期望更高。你真的可以每天仅仅通过改变你看什么和听什么来重新连接你的整个大脑，以实现巨大成功。所以像对待花园一样对待它，对吧？你的思想就是一座花园。如果你种下消极的种子，你会长出一个巨大的消极人生。如果你种下信念的种子，你会长出一个巨大的精彩帝国。你必须无情地保护你的注意力。所以停止把注意力放在让你感觉渺小的事情上，开始痴迷于让你感到强大的想法。当你改变输入的那一刻，输出将永远改变。

turns.en: But once you fix your surroundings, you need a system to actually get you moving, which brings us to the simple 2% trick. Use the 2% rule to build massive momentum. The biggest thing you're missing right now is just momentum. You're sitting on a truly great idea, but you haven't taken any real action. You're constantly overthinking it. You want everything to be 100% perfect before you finally launch. You want the perfect logo, the perfect website, the perfect business plan. Stop doing that. Perfectionism is just you being afraid. Studies reveal that perfectionism actually decreases your productivity and increases severe mental burnout. You don't need a perfect plan. You just need to execute the first 2%. If your goal is to write a book, a best-selling book, the first 2% is writing just one single page. If your goal is to start a massive YouTube channel, awesome. The first 2% is pulling out your phone and recording your first really messy video. Don't worry about step 100, just focus completely on step number one. Take the absolute smallest, easiest action right now. Once you take that first step, your brain gets a quick win. And that quick win builds confidence and that confidence creates momentum. So when I wrote my book about momentum, I didn't plan it out for long months. I just started typing furiously. The physical action itself creates the energy you need to keep going. So, waiting around for the perfect moment, what does it do? It guarantees that you'll wait forever. Action cures fear every single time. When you're moving forward, you simply don't have the time to sit there and doubt yourself. So, don't let your greatest ideas die silently here in your head. Put them out into the real world. Start messy. Start small, but you've absolutely got to start when? Today. It doesn't matter if your first attempt looks crazy, ridiculous. The only thing that matters is that you aren't just standing still anymore. You're finally in the game. Every massive company started as some tiny, flawed little experiment. You are no different. So, push through the hesitation, click publish, make the call, and watch how quickly your life begins to change.
turns.zh: 但是，一旦你改善了周围环境，你需要一个系统让你真正行动起来，这就引出了简单的 2% 技巧。用 2% 法则来建立巨大的动力。你现在最缺少的就是动力。你有一个真正伟大的想法，但你没有采取任何实际行动。你一直在过度思考。你想在最终推出之前让一切都 100% 完美。你想要完美的标志、完美的网站、完美的商业计划。别那样做了。完美主义只是你在害怕。研究表明，完美主义实际上会降低你的生产力并增加严重的精神倦怠。你不需要一个完美的计划。你只需要执行最初的 2%。如果你的目标是写一本书，一本畅销书，那么最初的 2% 就是写一页纸。如果你的目标是创办一个庞大的 YouTube 频道，太好了。最初的 2% 就是拿出手机，录制你的第一个非常草率的视频。别担心第 100 步，只专注于第一步。现在就采取最小、最简单的行动。一旦你迈出第一步，你的大脑就会获得一个快速的胜利。而这个快速胜利会建立信心，信心又创造动力。所以当我写那本关于动力的书时，我没有计划好几个月。我只是开始疯狂打字。身体行动本身就会创造出你继续前进所需的能量。所以，等待完美时刻会怎样？它会保证你永远等待下去。行动每次都能治愈恐惧。当你向前迈进时，你根本没有时间坐在那里怀疑自己。所以，别让你最伟大的想法默默死在你脑子里。把它们放到现实世界里。从混乱开始。从小处开始，但你绝对必须开始，什么时候？今天。你的第一次尝试看起来是否疯狂、荒谬，都没关系。唯一重要的是你不只是停留在原地。你终于入场了。每个大公司最初都是一个小小的、有缺陷的实验。你也不例外。所以，突破犹豫，点击发布，打那个电话，然后看着你的生活有多快开始改变。

ts.sec: Expect to Be Terrible at First

turns.en: Now that you're moving though, you've got to prepare yourself for the hardest phase of all. And this is where almost everyone quits. Expect to be terrible at first. So, now you've got to accept a really harsh reality. Your first attempt at anything new is going to be absolutely terrible. Your first product will have tons of flaws. Your first video will be incredibly embarrassing. Your first major sales call will feel completely awkward, and that is completely normal. Everyone starts out at the bottom. You just don't see the messy, hidden starts. Data shows that it takes roughly 10,000 hours of deliberate practice to truly master any complex skill. You just can't skip the struggle. When I first started on YouTube, I was completely terrified. I was shy, quiet, introverted. I did not like being on camera.
turns.zh: 不过，既然你已经开始行动了，你必须为最难的阶段做好准备。而这正是几乎所有人放弃的地方。预计自己一开始会很糟糕。所以，现在你必须接受一个非常残酷的现实。你对任何新事物的第一次尝试都绝对会很糟糕。你的第一个产品会有大量缺陷。你的第一个视频会非常尴尬。你的第一次重要销售电话会感觉完全别扭，而这完全正常。每个人都是从底层开始的。只是你没看到那些混乱、隐藏的起步。数据显示，真正掌握任何复杂技能大约需要一万小时的刻意练习。你无法跳过挣扎。当我刚开始做 YouTube 时，我完全吓坏了。我害羞、安静、内向。我不喜欢上镜。

turns.en: It took me 350 videos before I wasn't completely embarrassed to watch myself back, and 700 public videos before I actually felt inspired by one piece of content that I made. And I made absolutely hundreds of terrible videos. You can go back and watch them, but I kept going anyway. Most people just quit because they tried five times and they expected to be world class immediately. They let their ego stop you from making actual progress. So, the fact that you're willing to try and be terrible becomes an actual secret advantage. So, embrace the highly awkward phase, look at your early failures as data and that's going to be part of your story as you climb. Every single time you fail, you learn exactly what not to do the next time. It'll be an inspiration to others. If you can handle looking foolish for a little while, you'll eventually become completely unstoppable. The only real failure in life is quitting before you get good. So, you've got to give yourself permission to be a total beginner. Stop comparing your chapter one to somebody else's chapter 20, right? Your journey is your journey and that is okay. So, put in the boring reps, do the unglamorous work. The mastery that you want is waiting on the other side of a thousand terrible attempts.
turns.zh: 我拍了 350 个视频后才不再完全尴尬地回看自己，700 个公开视频后才真正为自己创作的某个内容感到振奋。我制作了绝对好几百个糟糕的视频，你可以回去看它们，但我还是继续前进。大多数人只是放弃了，因为他们试了五次就期望立刻成为世界级。他们让自尊心阻止了自己取得真正的进步。所以，你愿意尝试并接受糟糕，这反而成了一种秘密优势。拥抱那个高度尴尬的阶段，把你早期的失败视为数据，那将是你攀登过程中故事的一部分。每一次失败，你都确切地学到了下次不该做什么。这会成为他人的灵感。如果你能暂时忍受显得愚蠢，你最终会变得完全不可阻挡。人生中唯一的真正失败是在你变好之前放弃。所以，你必须允许自己成为一个彻底的初学者。别再拿你的第一章和别人第二十章比较，对吧？你的旅程就是你的旅程，那没问题。所以，投入枯燥的重复，做那些不光彩的工作。你想要的精湛技艺就在一千次糟糕尝试的另一边等待着你。

turns.en: And once you survive that awkward phase, you can speed up your results by borrowing the exact blueprints of people who've already won. Model the massive success of others. You don't need to figure out all of this on your own. That was one of the biggest mistakes I made early on. You don't have to reinvent the wheel to make a massive fortune. The smartest entrepreneurs study the exact people who've already won and simply model their success. So, if you want to build a $100,000 consulting business, find someone who already did exactly that. Study their public website, look at their specific pricing, see exactly how they talk to their premium clients. Then, thoughtfully apply those same proven principles to your own unique style. According to the Small Business Administration, businesses that receive direct mentoring and strictly model proven strategies are two times more likely to survive their first five difficult years. When my first business was struggling, I felt completely lost. I had no real idea how to turn things around. Then, I decided to intensely study uh a highly successful software company, Microsoft, cuz I had a software company. I looked at how they operated, I looked at how they got their first clients, not how they make an extra million now. I didn't steal or copy them, but I learned directly from Bill Gates' powerful framework. And that single focus decision saved my entire company. Success always leaves clues. There's a road map out there for you to do whatever you want and achieve whatever you want. You just have to be humble and curious enough to actively go and follow it. So, read the biographies of great leaders. Watch the long-form interviews of the performers that you look up to and respect. Find the hidden patterns in their daily behaviors and then creatively adapt them to your situation. Why would you spend 10 years making deeply painful mistakes when you can learn from someone else's expensive experience in just 10 days or 10 hours? So, be an aggressive student of greatness and your path to financial independence will be so much faster. You don't lack the ability. You just lack the right model. So, find your ideal model, study them relentlessly, build your own blueprint for your special flavor.
turns.zh: 一旦你挺过了那个尴尬阶段，你就可以通过借鉴那些已经获胜之人的精确蓝图来加速你的成果。模仿他人的巨大成功。你不需要独自解决所有问题。这是我早期犯的最大错误之一。你不必为了赚大钱而重新发明轮子。最聪明的企业家研究那些已经获胜的人，并直接模仿他们的成功。所以，如果你想建立一项 10 万美元的咨询业务，去找一个已经做到的人。研究他们的公开网站，查看他们的具体定价，看看他们如何与高端客户交谈。然后，深思熟虑地将那些经过验证的原则应用到你自己独特的风格中。根据小企业管理局的数据，接受直接指导并严格模仿经证实的策略的企业在最初五年内生存下来的可能性是其他企业的两倍。当我的第一个企业陷入困境时，我感到完全迷失。我不知道如何扭转局面。然后，我决定深入研究一家非常成功的软件公司——微软，因为我当时也有一家软件公司。我观察他们如何运营，如何获得第一批客户，而不是他们现在如何多赚一百万。我没有窃取或复制他们，而是直接从比尔·盖茨的强大框架中学习。那个专注的决定拯救了我的整个公司。成功总会留下线索。那里有一张路线图，让你做你想做的事，实现你想要的任何成就。你只需要足够谦逊和好奇，主动去追随它。所以，阅读伟大领袖的传记。观看你敬佩和尊重的表演者的长篇访谈。在他们日常行为中找到隐藏的模式，然后创造性地将它们适应到你的情境中。为什么要花十年时间犯下深痛的错误，而你可以在短短十天或十小时内从别人昂贵的经验中学习？所以，成为伟大的积极学生，你通往财务独立的道路会快得多。你不是缺乏能力，你只是缺乏正确的模型。所以，找到你的理想模型，不懈地研究他们，为你自己的特色构建你的蓝图。

turns.en: And then when you've got the right model, you need the right people. And there's a specific way to get the most powerful CEOs to take your call. Build real relationships instead of fake followers. So, most people think that making money online means you definitely need millions of random followers, right? You think that you need to go incredibly viral to succeed. And that's a massive and actually dangerous distraction. You don't need a million casual subscribers to make a million dollars. You just need deep, highly meaningful relationships. Don't worry about vanity metrics. They will constantly waste your time. Instead, focus on direct business development through high-value connections. One of my favorite strategies that we teach inside our Movement Makers program is a business development show. It's a dedicated interview show. Don't constantly cold call potential clients. Warmly invite them onto your show to share their story. People love talking about themselves. When you feature them prominently, they feel valued and you build a relationship. Statistics clearly show that 84% of B2B sales start exactly with a warm referral or a strong existing relationship. When you interview someone, you spend real focused time with them. You build authentic trust with them. That genuine trust turns into lucrative partnerships, massive referrals, highly paying clients. It literally doesn't matter if your new channel only has 200 total subscribers. We're going after people who have high demand, but low media demand. You're coming in as media right now. And you can get top industry leaders who built multi-million dollar networks. So, don't worry about the random clicks and start aggressively chasing real conversations. Add massive value to the exact people that you desperately want to work with. Feature their deep expertise. Ask them incredibly great questions. Do your research before you have them on. Give them a beautiful platform to share their story. When you actively become a super connector and a supporter, the big money naturally follows you everywhere you go. Your network is truly your actual net worth. So, start building it deliberately and strategically today. Stop worrying about the algorithm instead of obsessing over the actual human beings you want to serve.
turns.zh: 然后当你有了正确的模型，你需要正确的人。有一种特定的方法可以让最有影响力的 CEO 接听你的电话。建立真实的关系，而不是虚假的粉丝。所以，大多数人认为在网上赚钱意味着你肯定需要数百万的随机粉丝，对吧？你认为你需要极度走红才能成功。这是一个巨大且实际上危险的干扰。你不需要一百万个随意订阅者来赚一百万美元。你只需要深刻、高度有意义的关系。不要担心虚荣指标，它们会不断浪费你的时间。相反，通过高价值连接专注于直接业务发展。我们在 Movement Makers 项目中教授的一个我最喜欢的策略是业务发展节目。这是一个专门的访谈节目。不要一直冷拨电话给潜在客户。热情地邀请他们上你的节目分享他们的故事。人们喜欢谈论自己。当你突出展示他们时，他们感到被重视，你就建立了关系。统计数据清楚地显示，84% 的 B2B 销售正是从温暖的推荐或牢固的现有关系开始的。当你采访某人时，你与他们共度了真正专注的时间。你与他们建立了真实的信任。那种真诚的信任转化为有利可图的合作伙伴关系、大量的推荐、高薪客户。你的新频道只有 200 个订阅者根本无关紧要。我们瞄准的是高需求但低媒体需求的人。你现在是以媒体的身份进入。你可以接触到那些建立了数百万美元网络的一流行业领袖。所以，不要担心随机的点击，开始积极追寻真实的对话。为你迫切想要合作的人增加巨大价值。展示他们的深厚专业知识。问他们极其精彩的问题。在他们上节目之前做好研究。给他们一个美丽的平台来分享他们的故事。当你积极成为超级连接者和支持者时，大钱自然会在你去的任何地方跟随你。你的人脉就是你的实际净资产。所以，从今天开始有意识、有策略地建立它。不要再担心算法，而是痴迷于你想服务的真实人类。

turns.en: And building that network takes extreme focus, which means you've got to completely change how you manage your 24 hours. Make every single day truly count. Your limited time is your absolute most precious asset. If you want to permanently escape the endless job cycle and build your own incredible life, you've got to maximize your specific daily actions. So, you wake up every morning with a clear intention. Make today truly count. Before you hit your head your tired head on the pillow tonight, do one specific thing that moves you significantly closer to your dream. Make one beautiful piece of art. Send one highly important email. Record one incredibly helpful video. Create something today that you desperately want your future grandkids to see. Research strongly indicates that completing just one highly meaningful task a day significantly boost your overall life satisfaction and guarantees long-term success. To make real time for that meaningful work, you've got to ruthlessly manage your busy schedule. You must eliminate, automate, or delegate absolutely everything else. If a specific task doesn't directly serve your core mission, stop doing it.
turns.zh: 建立那个网络需要极度的专注，这意味着你必须完全改变你管理 24 小时的方式。让每一天都真正有意义。你有限的时间是你绝对最宝贵的资产。如果你想永久摆脱无尽的工作循环，建立自己非凡的生活，你必须最大化你每天的具体行动。所以，你每天早上带着清晰的意图醒来。让今天真正算数。今晚在你疲惫的头撞到枕头之前，做一件能显著让你更接近梦想的具体事情。制作一件美丽的艺术品。发送一封极其重要的电子邮件。录制一个非常有帮助的视频。今天创造一些你未来孙辈渴望看到的东西。研究强烈表明，每天只完成一项高度有意义的任务能显著提升你的整体生活满意度并保证长期成功。为了为那些有意义的工作腾出真正的时间，你必须无情地管理你的繁忙日程。你必须消除、自动化或委派其他所有事情。如果某个特定任务不直接服务于你的核心使命，就停止做它。

turns.en: If a basic computer program or AI can do it, awesome, automate it immediately. If someone else can do something significantly cheaper, hire them right away. Don't waste your unique genius on boring busy work. Focus only on the high-level tasks that actually move the big needle forward. When you finally take control of your daily time, you instantly take total control of your personal income. You stop hopelessly trading hours for a flat, boring salary and start aggressively trading massive value for huge financial returns. You already have absolutely everything it takes to build a beautiful life of total freedom. You just have to firmly decide that you're ready to step up and claim it. And this brings us to the absolute most important truth of all, and it's something that I hope that you remember every single morning when you wake up. Your belief is your ultimate superpower. You are entirely capable of building a massive life on your own terms. So, trust your vision. Take the messy action, and never let fear make your decisions for you. Ready to discover the skills that could skyrocket your success this year? These aren't academic theories, they're practical, in-demand abilities that you can learn without a formal degree. Each skill taps into emerging market needs, offers entrepreneurial leverage, and has scalable impact. Let's dive in and imagine the possibilities each one opens up for your business and income.
turns.zh: 如果一个基础计算机程序或 AI 能做的事情，太棒了，立刻自动化。如果别人能以低得多的成本做某事，马上雇佣他们。不要把独特的才华浪费在无聊的琐事上。只专注于那些真正能推动大局的高阶任务。当你最终掌控了自己的日常时间，你就立刻掌控了个人收入。你不再绝望地用时间换取固定的、乏味的薪水，而是开始积极地用巨大的价值换取丰厚的财务回报。你已经拥有创造完全自由的美好生活所需的一切。你只需要坚定地决定，准备好挺身而出，去争取它。这就引出了最重要的事实，我希望你每天早上醒来时都记住它：你的信念是你的终极超能力。你完全有能力按照自己的方式建立丰盛的人生。所以，相信你的愿景。采取混乱的行动，永远不要让恐惧替你决策。准备好发现能让你今年成功飙升的技能了吗？这些不是学术理论，而是实用的、需求旺盛的能力，无需正式学位就能学会。每项技能都切入新兴市场需求，提供创业杠杆，并具有可扩展的影响。让我们深入探讨，想象每一项技能为你的生意和收入带来的可能性。

turns.en: Skill number one, AI integration and automation, turning intelligence into income. Okay, so what is it? Here we're going to leverage AI and automation tools to streamline operations, create smarter products, or even launch AI-driven services. It's using machines to do the heavy thinking or doing for you from chatbots that handle customer inquiries to AI systems that optimize your marketing or inventory in real time. Here's why it matters this year. The AI revolution isn't coming, it's right here now, and it's rewriting the rules of business. By 2024, 70% of organizations reported using AI in some capacity, up from just 55% the year before. Companies are pouring investments in the AI at record levels, over $109 billion in the US in 2024 with nearly 34 billion globally into generative AI. And they desperately need people who can make it work. The catch? There's a huge talent gap. 94% of business leaders say they face AI-related skill shortages on their teams with one in three reporting massive gaps in critical AI roles. What does that mean? Demand is way bigger than supply, and that means opportunities for you. Entrepreneurs who are AI-savvy can step in and command premium prices for their solutions. This isn't just for tech companies, either. From healthcare to finance, AI is being woven into daily operations. Even the FDA has approved hundreds of AI-enabled medical devices, and self-driving cars are logging thousands of rides right now. The world is racing to adopt AI, and those who can ride that wave stand to reap huge rewards. So, how can entrepreneurs profit? Think of AI as a force multiplier for your business. An entrepreneur with AI skills can automate super boring processes, freeing up time to scale faster. You can make smarter products with better features. You can offer AI consulting and integration services to companies who are willing to pay for help. Uh so, for example, a small e-commerce founder might use AI to personalize a shopping experience for each customer automatically, leading to happier customers and higher sales. Or maybe you're launching a micro SaaS tool that uses AI, like a AI scheduling assistant or content generator. Even a one-person business can serve thousands of customers when AI is doing most of the work. The evidence is everywhere. Companies using AI report higher productivity and lower costs, and many have seen AI-driven projects boost their bottom line.
