turns.zh: 如果你不彻底忽略那 20 个目标，它们就会毁掉你成功的机会。它们会偷走你的时间，耗尽你的精力，你将永远无法完成真正重要的五件事。你现在可能就在这么做——把精力摊得太薄，以至于没有一件事得到你的全部注意力。你对自己的人生有宏大的愿景，却因为拒绝专注而毫无结果。所以你必须明白，好是卓越的敌人。你可能有 20 个好主意，但追求这些好主意恰恰阻止了你执行那五个伟大的主意。因此你必须砍掉干扰，愿意忽略那些你确实在乎的事情，只为了赢取你最在乎的东西。你的大脑会告诉你你在错过什么，它会给你十分聪明的理由，让你觉得必须保持所有选项开放，但结果只是让你原地踏步。你必须学会说“不”。如果你不无情地缩减目标，你永远只能平庸，永远无法发挥全部潜力；你会看着别人从你身边超越，因为他们有自律去专注。所以你必须停止把你的专注力当作理所当然，当作廉价的商品；它是你拥有的最有价值的资产。如果你想知道具体怎么做，你需要建立你的“不惜一切代价避免清单”。

turns.en: Building your avoid at all costs list. Okay, so how do you actually do this? You have to write down your list today. Write down every single project that you're working on. Write down every goal that you have for the next 5 years. Look at that list. It's probably huge. Now, force yourself to pick just five. This is going to hurt. You'll want to pick 10. You're going to try to negotiate with yourself. Don't do it. Warren Buffett says don't do it. Pick exactly five. Take the rest of your list and put it in a drawer. You aren't allowed to look at it or touch it until you succeed at the top five. You have to protect your attention like it's your most valuable asset. The wealthiest people in the world are extremely aggressive about what they ignore. If you want to make millions of dollars, you must ignore almost everything. You have to cancel projects. You have to say no to people. Every time you say yes to a distraction, you're delaying your ultimate success. Your sixth most important goal is your biggest enemy. You like it just enough to spend time on it, but it won't ever give you the massive success of the top five. When I joined my first software company at 19 years old, I was struggling. I didn't know what to do. I had to focus entirely on modeling success. I studied how Bill Gates started Microsoft. I applied his exact strategy to my business. It landed me my first deal for 13 and a half thousand dollars. It only worked because I ignored everything else. I focused on one specific model and put all my energy into it. You have to do the same thing. Find your top priority. Commit to it completely. People will invite you out. They'll pitch you new business ideas. They're going to allow you to join their exciting new startup, right? You have to tell them no. It's going to feel uncomfortable. People might even get mad at you. Let them be mad. You can't let other people dictate where your time goes. If you don't take control of your schedule, somebody else will happily take it from you. You're built to serve a specific purpose, and you can't do that if you're constantly distracted. So, you have to stay laser focused on your top five.
turns.zh: 建立你的“不惜一切代价避免清单”。具体怎么做？你今天就必须写下你的清单：写下你正在做的每一个项目，写下你未来五年的每一个目标。看看那份清单——很可能很大。现在，强迫自己只选五个。这会很痛苦，你会想选十个，你会试图和自己讨价还价。别这么做。沃伦·巴菲特说别这么做。就选五个。把清单剩下的部分放进抽屉，在你成功完成前五项目标之前，你不准看它或碰它。你必须像保护最有价值的资产一样保护你的注意力。世界上最富有的人在忽略什么上极其激进。如果你想赚几百万美元，你必须忽略几乎所有事情。你必须取消项目，必须对别人说“不”。每次你对一个干扰说“是”，你就在推迟你最终的成功。你的第六重要的目标是你最大的敌人——你足够喜欢它以至于会花时间在上面，但它永远不会给你带来前五个目标那样的巨大成功。我 19 岁加入第一家软件公司时，处境艰难，不知道该做什么。我不得不完全专注于模仿成功。我研究了比尔·盖茨如何创立微软，将他的确切策略应用到我的业务中，这为我带来了第一笔 13,500 美元的交易。它能成功只因为我忽略了其他一切，专注在一个具体的模型上，投入了我所有的精力。你也必须做同样的事：找到你的最高优先级，完全承诺它。人们会邀请你出去，向你推销新的商业点子，让你加入他们激动人心的新创业公司。你必须对他们说“不”。这会让你不舒服，人们甚至可能生你的气。让他们生气吧。你不能让别人决定你的时间去向。如果你不控制自己的日程，别人会很乐意把它从你手中夺走。你生来就是为了一个特定的使命，如果总是分心，你就无法完成它。所以你必须激光般聚焦在你的前五个目标上。

turns.en: But focus alone won't make you rich. You need to know exactly how to compound your value, which brings us directly to Warren Buffett's second daily habit. The 500-page knowledge habit. Once you have your focus, you need to execute. Warren Buffett spends up to 80% of his day reading. When a student asked him how to prepare for an investing career, Buffett held up a stack of paper. He said to read 500 pages like this every day. He said knowledge builds up like compound interest. Everyone can do it, but he guaranteed very few actually will. Now, you might think you don't have time to read 500 pages. That's not the point. The point is that you must aggressively consume knowledge about your specific focus. Most people consume garbage. You wake up, you immediately scroll through negative news, you look at social media and compare yourself to people who are faking their success. You load your brain with all sorts of distractions. You have to change your environment. If you want to be great, you have to put greatness into your mind every single day. So, start your morning by listening to someone who inspires you. Put on a video of a successful entrepreneur. Listen to the greats. When you surround yourself with massive thinkers, your own problems start to look small. You begin to believe that you can overcome your current struggles. You borrow the belief from them. If you aren't learning every day, you're falling behind. Your competitors, they're studying, they're getting ready, they're getting better. You have to make learning a non-negotiable part of your daily routine, and ideally first thing in the morning. So, I go for a walk every morning. I call it my belief walk. It's my dedicated time to clear my head and find my focus. And while I walk, I listen to videos and interviews of successful entrepreneurs. I want the greatest minds in history speaking into my ear. I want their belief to transfer into me. You can do the same. Find the authors, the speakers, the leaders who've already accomplished your goals. Consume their content relentlessly, right? Let their knowledge compound inside of you. It's the highest return on investment you will get.
turns.zh: 但仅仅专注不会让你致富。你需要确切知道如何让价值复利增长，这直接把我们带到沃伦·巴菲特的第二个日常习惯——500 页知识习惯。一旦你有了焦点，你就需要执行。沃伦·巴菲特每天花高达 80% 的时间阅读。当一个学生问他如何为投资生涯做准备时，巴菲特举起一叠纸，说每天读 500 页这样的内容。他说知识像复利一样积累。每个人都能做到，但他保证几乎没人会真正去做。你可能会想自己没时间读 500 页，但重点不是这个。重点是你必须积极摄取关于你特定焦点的知识。大多数人消费垃圾：醒来就立即刷负面新闻，看社交媒体和那些假装成功的人比较，给自己的大脑塞满各种干扰。你必须改变你的环境。如果你想变得卓越，就必须每天把卓越输入你的大脑。所以，早上从听一个激励你的人开始，放一个成功企业家的视频，聆听伟人的声音。当你身边围绕的都是大思想家时，你自己的问题就开始显得渺小；你开始相信你能克服当前的困难——你从他们那里借来了信念。如果你不每天学习，你就在落后。你的竞争对手在学习、在准备、在进步。你必须让学习成为你日常中不可协商的一部分，最好在早上第一件事就做。我每天早上散步，称之为我的“信念漫步”。这是我专门用来理清思绪、找到焦点的时间。散步时，我听成功企业家的视频和访谈。我希望历史上最伟大的头脑在我耳边说话，希望他们的信念传递给我。你也可以这样做：找到那些已经实现了你目标的作者、演讲者、领导者，无情地消费他们的内容，让他们的知识在你体内复利。这是你能获得的最高投资回报。

turns.en: But consuming information is only half the battle. If you don't know how to translate that knowledge into real-world action, you're just wasting your time, which is exactly what we're going to fix right now. Turning knowledge into action. Reading and learning are completely useless if you don't take action. Watching this video is useless if you don't take action. You can read 100 books a year. If you don't change your behavior, you just wasted your time. You're just trying to feel productive without actually doing the work. So you need to implement what you learn, and when? Immediately. You have to start taking risks. Your fear of failure is the number one thing holding you back. You want everything to be perfect before you launch. I get it. You want the perfect website, the perfect camera, the perfect plan. Perfectionism is really just fear. It's a mask for fear. You have to expect to suck at the beginning. When I started my YouTube channel, I was terrible. You can go back and watch the videos. I hated my first 250 videos. I couldn't even watch them because I was so embarrassed by myself, and it took me 700 videos before I actually felt a little bit proud of my work, but I kept posting. I kept learning.
turns.zh: 但消费信息只是战斗的一半。如果你不知道如何把知识转化为现实行动，你只是在浪费时间——这正是我们现在要解决的问题。把知识转化为行动。阅读和学习，如果不采取行动就完全没用；看这个视频如果不采取行动也没用。你一年能读 100 本书，但如果行为不改变，你只是浪费了时间，只是在试图让自己感觉高效而没有真正做事。所以你需要立刻实践你学到的东西。你必须开始冒险。对失败的恐惧是阻碍你的头号因素。你希望在推出之前一切完美——我理解，你想要完美的网站、完美的相机、完美的计划。完美主义其实只是恐惧，是恐惧的伪装。你必须预期自己一开始会很糟。当我开始做 YouTube 频道时，我很糟糕。你可以回去看那些视频。我讨厌自己的前 250 个视频，甚至因为太尴尬而无法看它们，直到第 700 个视频我才真正为自己的作品感到一点自豪，但我一直在发布，一直在学习。

turns.en: I took the knowledge I had and I put it into action, and you can get there faster. You can do the same. Make the messy video. Send the awkward email. Launch the ugly product. Just get it out there. The market will tell you what works. You will learn far more from 10 days of taking action than you will from 10 months of just reading books. Every time you test a new idea, you're gathering new data. You're figuring out what works and what doesn't. So stop overthinking your next move. Stop waiting for the perfect moment. The perfect moment doesn't exist. You just have to start where you are with what you have. Action builds confidence. When you combine massive knowledge with massive action, you become incredibly dangerous to your competition.
turns.zh: 我把已有的知识转化为行动，你也可以更快地达到目标。你可以做到同样的事。拍出粗糙的视频，发送尴尬的邮件，推出不完美的产品。只管把它们发布出去。市场会告诉你什么有效。从 10 天的行动中学到的东西，远胜于 10 个月的埋头读书。每次测试一个新想法，你都在收集新数据，搞清楚什么可行、什么不可行。所以别再过度思考下一步，别再等待完美时机——完美时机根本不存在。你只需从当前所在的位置、用现有的资源开始行动。行动能建立自信。当大量知识与大量行动结合时，你会成为竞争对手眼中极其危险的存在。

ts.sec: The Third Habit: Scheduled Thinking Time

turns.en: To make sure you're taking the right actions, you have to master the third habit of the ultra-rich. It's a habit that almost every entrepreneur completely ignores: scheduled thinking time. The third habit is the most difficult for entrepreneurs to master. It's the habit of sitting in a quiet room and simply thinking. Warren Buffett doesn't just read; he schedules large blocks of time to just think. Bill Gates used to schedule every minute of his day, then he saw Buffett's calendar and realized it was mostly blank. You think being busy means being productive. You fill your calendar with meetings, calls, and emails. You pride yourself on working 15 hours a day, but you're running on a treadmill a lot of times—moving fast but going nowhere. If you don't schedule time to think, you'll never solve your biggest problems. You'll just keep reacting to fires. You have to pull yourself out of the daily grind. You need time to step back and look at the whole board, the bigger picture. I call it CEO time. You have to ask yourself the hard questions: Are you actually moving closer to your ultimate goal? Are you spending your time on those top five priorities we identified earlier, or are you slipping back into your old habits? You have to protect your thinking time. Treat it like the most important meeting of your week. Turn off your phone, close your laptop, sit with a blank piece of paper and a pen, let your mind wander. The best ideas come when you give your brain the space to breathe. Most people are terrified of silence. You constantly need a podcast, a song, a video playing in the background. You're afraid to be alone with your own thoughts, but your thoughts are where the million-dollar ideas live. You have to practice being bored. You have to force yourself to sit and strategize. This isn't wasted time; it's the most profitable time of your entire week.
turns.zh: 为了确保你采取正确的行动，你必须掌握超级富豪的第三个习惯——这是几乎每个企业家都会完全忽略的习惯：安排好的思考时间。第三个习惯对企业家来说最难掌握，就是坐在安静的房间里单纯地思考。沃伦·巴菲特不只是阅读，他会安排大块时间纯粹用于思考。比尔·盖茨曾经把每一分钟都安排得满满当当，后来他看到巴菲特的日历，发现上面大部分是空白的。你以为忙碌就等于高效。你用会议、电话和邮件填满日历，自豪于每天工作 15 小时，但很多时候你就像在跑步机上奔跑——速度很快却寸步未移。如果不安排思考时间，你永远解决不了最大的问题，只会不断被动救火。你必须把自己从日常琐事中抽离出来，需要退后一步，审视整盘棋局和更大的图景。我称之为“CEO 时间”。你必须问自己那些艰难的问题：你真的在向最终目标靠近吗？你把时间花在之前确定的五大优先事项上了吗，还是又滑回了旧习惯？你必须保护自己的思考时间，把它当作一周中最重要的会议。关掉手机，合上笔记本电脑，拿一张白纸和一支笔坐下，让思绪自由飘荡。最好的想法往往在你给大脑呼吸空间时出现。大多数人害怕沉默。你总需要播客、歌曲或视频在背景中播放，害怕独自面对自己的思绪——但百万美元的点子恰恰就藏在你的思绪里。你必须练习忍受无聊，强迫自己坐下来制定策略。这并非浪费时间，而是你一整周里最具价值的时间。

ts.sec: Design Your Environment for Deep Focus

turns.en: To make this actually work, you have to ruthlessly engineer your physical and mental space, which is what we're going to cover next: designing your daily environment. To make thinking time work, you have to ruthlessly control your environment. Your environment right now is perfectly designed to keep you exactly where you are. If you want to change your life, you have to change what surrounds you. You have to limit access to negativity. You have to shut down the voices that tell you your ideas are crazy. Sometimes those voices are your friends and family. Sometimes the loudest negative voice is in your own head. You have to fight back by engineering your surroundings. When you sit down to think, you can't be in a place full of distractions. You need a dedicated space, a place where your brain knows it's time to work. So find your version of that. Maybe it's a quiet corner in your house. Maybe it's a park bench. It doesn't matter where it is. It only matters that you guard it fiercely. If you let other people interrupt your thinking time, you're telling them their priorities are more important than your future. So stop doing that. You have to value your own mind enough to give it the silence it needs. When I'm creating something new, that's when I feel the most free. You need to give yourself permission to explore your ideas without judgment. Don't worry if the idea sounds stupid at first. Let it develop. Write it down. Look at the different angles. You'll have moments of self-doubt. You'll wonder if you're sitting there wasting your time. You'll want to go back to checking emails because it feels easier—you get that dopamine hit. Don't give in to that urge. Push through the discomfort of deep thinking. When you create an environment that supports deep focus, your productivity will absolutely skyrocket. You'll start seeing opportunities that were totally blind to you before. You'll finally have the clarity you need to push forward.
turns.zh: 为了让思考时间真正奏效，你必须毫不留情地设计你的物理和心理空间——这就是我们接下来要讲的内容：设计你的日常环境。为了让思考时间发挥作用，你必须严格控制你的环境。你当前的环境被精心设计成让你维持现状。如果你想改变人生，就必须改变你周围的一切。你必须限制消极信息的接触，关闭那些告诉你想法很疯狂的声音。有时那些声音来自朋友和家人，有时最响亮的负面声音就在你自己的脑海里。你必须通过设计环境来反击。当你坐下来思考时，不能身处一个充满干扰的地方。你需要一个专属空间，一个让你的大脑知道“该工作了”的地方。所以找到属于你的那个版本——可能是家里安静的角落，也可能是公园的长椅。地点不重要，重要的是你坚决守护它。如果你容许别人打断你的思考时间，就等于在告诉他们，他们的优先级比你自己的未来更重要。所以别再这样做了。你必须足够重视自己的心智，给它所需的宁静。每当我创造新东西的时候，那是我感觉最自由的时刻。你需要允许自己在没有评判的情况下探索想法。不要担心最初的想法听起来很蠢。让它发展，写下来，从不同角度审视。你会有自我怀疑的时刻，会怀疑自己坐在那里浪费时间，会想回到检查邮件这种更容易的事情——因为你能获得多巴胺的刺激。但不要屈服于那种冲动。挺过深度思考的不适感。当你创造一个支持深度专注的环境时，你的生产力绝对会飙升。你会开始看到之前完全视而不见的机会，最终获得向前推进所需的清晰度。

turns.en: But there's one final piece of the puzzle that ties all of this together: building unstoppable momentum. Okay, you now know the three habits. You need to ruthlessly focus on your top five goals. You need to aggressively consume knowledge about those goals. You need to schedule quiet time to think and strategize. Knowing this is not enough. The only thing you're missing right now is momentum. You don't need a massive breakthrough. You don't need a viral moment. You just need to take one small step today, and then another small step tomorrow. Momentum is created by doing the boring repetitive tasks every single day, even when you don't feel like it. You're going to wake up tomorrow and you won't want to execute. You'll feel tired, you might feel overwhelmed. That's the exact moment that defines your entire life. Are you going to give in to comfort, or are you going to push through and do the work? You have to believe that the work you're doing today will eventually pay off. The results will not show up immediately. You'll put in massive effort and see zero results for a long time. That's the test. That's the filter that removes the weak. You have to keep pushing until the momentum takes over, and when it does you'll become unstoppable. You'll look back at your life and realize that mastering these three daily habits changed absolutely everything. Lack of belief is the biggest problem in the world today. That's what I think. You have to believe in your own potential before anyone else will. You have to trust that if you put in the daily reps, the compound interest of your effort will eventually explode. So stop waiting for someone to come and rescue you. Stop waiting for permission from anybody else. Give yourself the green light right now. Protect your focus, expand your knowledge, and guard your thinking time. Everything you want is on the other side of that consistency. Your next step. Your dreams aren't impossible. They're just waiting for you to actually commit to them. You have everything you need right now to start making a massive impact. So trust your vision and take the very next step today.
turns.zh: 但拼图中还有最后一块将所有一切串联起来：建立不可阻挡的势能。好了，你现在知道了这三个习惯：你需要毫不留情地专注于你的五大目标；你需要积极地吸收关于这些目标的知识；你需要安排安静的时间来思考和制定策略。但仅仅知道还不够。你现在唯一缺失的就是势能。你不需要巨大的突破，不需要病毒式传播的时刻。你只需要今天迈出一小步，明天再迈出一小步。势能是通过每天做那些无聊的重复性任务积累起来的，即使你不想做。明天你醒来时可能不想执行，会感到疲惫，甚至不知所措。但那正是定义你整个人生的关键时刻。你是向舒适妥协，还是咬牙坚持把工作完成？你必须相信今天所做的工作终将得到回报。结果不会立刻显现。你会付出巨大努力却在很长一段时间内看不到任何成果。这是考验，是淘汰弱者的过滤器。你必须持续推进，直到势能接管一切——一旦势能形成，你将变得不可阻挡。当你回首人生时，会意识到掌握这三个日常习惯彻底改变了一切。缺乏信念是当今世界最大的问题——我是这么认为的。你必须先相信自己潜力，别人才会相信。你必须相信，只要你坚持每日的重复练习，你努力的复利效应终将爆发。所以别再等待别人来拯救你，别再等待任何人的许可。现在就给自己亮绿灯。保护你的专注力，扩充你的知识，守护你的思考时间。你所渴望的一切都在那份坚持的另一端。你的下一步。你的梦想并非不可能实现，它们只是在等待你真正地投入其中。你现在就拥有开始产生巨大影响所需的一切。所以，相信你的愿景，今天就迈出下一步。

turns.en: Does school teach you about money? The answer is nothing. They know nothing about money and they teach our kids. The highest earners in the world ignore traditional career paths and focus on stacking a handful of high impact skills. If you keep following the old rules of climbing the corporate ladder, you will stay stuck struggling to pay your bills while watching other people live your dream life. Salary is a drug they give you when they want you to forget about your dreams. Let's look at Warren Buffett. He is one of the richest investors alive. But if you walk into his office, you will not see his university degrees on the wall. The only thing he hangs up is a certificate for a public speaking course that he took. I actually have the diploma in the office, and I don't have my diploma from college, I don't have my diploma from graduate school, but I've got my Dale Carnegie diploma there because it changed my life. He realized that learning the skill of communication would instantly double his value. He ignored traditional rules and focused on a skill that actually prints money. By far the best investment you can make is in yourself. If they just learn to communicate better, both in writing and in person, they increase their value at least 50%. Now, you might be thinking, 'Okay, that's easy for Warren Buffett, but I'm just too busy trying to survive to learn something new.' The actual truth is you do not need to quit your job or spend years back in a classroom. You just need to focus your limited time on the exact abilities that the market actually pays for. And so today I'm going to show you the seven high-return skills you can start learning today that will completely transform your earning power.
turns.zh: 学校会教你关于钱的知识吗？答案是一点都没有。他们对钱一无所知，却教育着我们的孩子。世界上收入最高的人忽略传统的职业道路，专注于叠加一些高影响力的技能。如果你继续遵循爬职业阶梯的旧规则，你会一直困在努力支付账单的挣扎中，同时看着别人过着你梦想的生活。薪水是他们给你的一剂毒品，想让你忘记自己的梦想。让我们看看沃伦·巴菲特。他是在世最富有的投资者之一。但如果你走进他的办公室，你不会看到他的大学文凭挂在墙上。他唯一挂出来的是一张他参加过的公开演讲课程的证书。我办公室里确实有那张文凭，我没有我的大学文凭，没有研究生文凭，但我有我的戴尔·卡内基文凭，因为它改变了我的人生。他意识到学习沟通技能会立刻让他的价值翻倍。他忽略了传统规则，专注于一项真正能印钱的技能。到目前为止，你所能做的最好的投资就是投资自己。如果他们学会更好地沟通，无论是书面还是当面，他们的价值至少增加 50%。现在，你可能会想：“好吧，这对沃伦·巴菲特来说很容易，但我太忙于生存了，没时间学新东西。”事实是，你不需要辞职，也不需要回到教室好几年。你只需要把有限的时间集中在市场真正付钱的那些能力上。所以今天我要向你展示七种高回报技能，你可以从今天开始学习，它们将彻底改变你的赚钱能力。

turns.en: Master artificial intelligence and prompt engineering. So you might think that artificial intelligence is going to steal your job, but the truth is a person who knows how to use artificial intelligence is going to take your job. It's projected that 75% of global businesses will use AI in their daily operations. If you ignore this trend, you'll be completely left behind. A massive report shows that artificial intelligence can add 4.4 trillion dollars to the global economy. So you need to claim your piece of that pie. The most important high-return skill right now is prompt engineering. This just means knowing exactly how to talk to artificial intelligence to get the best results. You cannot just type in a lazy question and expect magic. You have to use a specific four-part framework. First, define the role, so tell the program to act like an expert copywriter or brilliant lawyer. Second, provide the data. Give it examples of what you want. Third, make the specific ask. Do not be vague. And fourth, request the exact format, like a bulleted list or a table. When you master this communication skill, you can do 10 hours of work in just 1 hour. You instantly become 10 times more valuable to any client or employer. Do not wait for the perfect moment to learn this. Action cures fear. Just open a free program today and start testing it. Build your momentum right now. But artificial intelligence is just a tool. To truly multiply your income, you need to know how to sell the value you just created, which leads perfectly into the second skill.
turns.zh: 掌握人工智能和提示工程。你可能认为人工智能会抢走你的工作，但事实是，一个知道如何使用人工智能的人会抢走你的工作。预计 75% 的全球企业将在日常运营中使用 AI。如果你忽视这一趋势，你将被完全抛在后面。一份大规模报告显示，人工智能可以为全球经济增加 4.4 万亿美元。所以你需要分得一杯羹。当下最重要的高回报技能是提示工程。这仅仅意味着知道如何与人工智能对话以获得最佳结果。你不能只是输入一个懒散的问题然后期待奇迹。你必须使用一个特定的四部分框架。首先，定义角色，告诉程序扮演专家文案或杰出律师。第二，提供数据。给它你想要的例子。第三，提出具体的要求。不要模糊。第四，请求确切的格式，比如项目符号列表或表格。当你掌握了这种沟通技能，你可以在 1 小时内完成 10 小时的工作。你立即变得对任何客户或雇主都有 10 倍的价值。不要等待完美的时机来学习这个。行动可以治愈恐惧。今天就打开一个免费程序，开始测试。现在就建立你的势头。但人工智能只是一个工具。要真正倍增你的收入，你需要知道如何销售你刚刚创造的价值，这完美地引出了第二个技能。

turns.en: Close high-ticket sales. Selling cheap products will keep you exhausted and broke. If you sell a $20 item, you need thousands of customers just to pay your rent. But if you master the skill of high-ticket sales, you only need a handful of clients to completely change your financial life. High-ticket offers are not about tricking people into paying more for the same service. They are about solving problems that are so painful, urgent, or expensive that premium pricing becomes totally obvious to the buyer. So, you have to change your entire mindset around selling. Most people feel slimy when they ask for money. But you were built to serve. If you have a product or a service that can genuinely fix someone's problem, you have a moral obligation to offer it to them. If you do not offer it to them, you are hurting them. You are being selfish. Selling is just serving at the highest possible level. You also need to understand that sales is a learned skill, not a genetic gift. Companies that spend money on sales training are 57% more effective than companies that ignore it. You can learn the scripts. You can learn how to handle objections. Do not take the yes away from the customer before you even ask for the sale. So, pick up the phone, make your premium offer, and let them decide. Selling 101 is incredibly powerful, but what if you want to reach millions of people at the exact same time? That is where the third skill comes in.
turns.zh: 完成高额销售。销售廉价产品会让你筋疲力尽且破产。如果你卖一件 20 美元的商品，你需要成千上万的客户才能付得起房租。但如果你掌握了高额销售的技能，你只需要几个客户就能彻底改变你的财务状况。高额报价不是要骗人为同样的服务支付更多。而是要解决那些痛苦、紧迫或昂贵的问题，以至于溢价对买家来说完全显而易见。所以，你必须改变你关于销售的整个心态。大多数人在要钱时感觉不光彩。但你生来就是为了服务。如果你有产品或服务能真正解决某人的问题，你有道德义务提供给他们。如果你不提供给他们，你就是在伤害他们。你是在自私。销售就是在最高水平上服务。你还需要理解销售是一种学来的技能，不是天赋。在销售培训上花钱的公司比忽略它的公司有效 57%。你可以学习话术。你可以学习如何处理反对意见。在你要出售之前，不要把客户的“是”拿走。所以，拿起电话，做出你的优质报价，让他们决定。销售 101 非常强大，但如果你想同时触达数百万人呢？这就是第三个技能的用武之地。

turns.en: Public speaking and video communication. You have to get on camera. It does not matter if you are shy or introverted. I was. Video communication is the single fastest way to build deep trust with a massive audience. When people can see your face, they can hear your voice, they connect with your story on a highly emotional level. You do not need a fancy studio or an expensive microphone. You just need your smartphone and the courage to share your truth. When I started making videos, I was completely terrified. I was an introverted guy who just wanted to hide. It took me 350 videos before I was not completely embarrassed to watch my own content back, and it took me 700 public videos until I actually started to think I was getting good. I expected to suck at the beginning and I did. But I just kept going. I focused entirely on the one person I could help instead of worrying about the millions of people who were not watching me yet. So if you want to stand out in your industry, start making videos about your foundation story. Tell people why you started your business. Tell them about your struggles. Tell them what to believe. Do not wait for validation from the internet. Just put in the reps and build your back catalog. The market always rewards the people who show up consistently and speak with passion.
turns.zh: 公开演讲和视频沟通。你必须上镜头。无论你害羞还是内向都没关系。我曾经也是。视频沟通是与大量观众建立深度信任的最快方式。当人们能看到你的脸，听到你的声音，他们会在情感层面上与你的故事产生联系。你不需要 fancy 的工作室或昂贵的麦克风。你只需要你的智能手机和分享真相的勇气。当我开始制作视频时，我完全吓坏了。我是个内向的人，只想躲起来。我做了 350 个视频才不再完全尴尬地回看自己的内容，又做了 700 个公开视频才开始觉得自己变好了。我预料到一开始会很烂，事实也确实如此。但我就是继续坚持。我完全专注于我能帮助的那一个人，而不是担心那几百万还没看我的人。所以如果你想在你的行业里脱颖而出，开始制作关于你创始故事的视频。告诉人们你为什么开始你的生意。告诉他们你的挣扎。告诉他们该相信什么。不要等待网络的认可。只管投入次数，建立你的内容库。市场总是奖励那些持续出现并充满激情地发言的人。

turns.en: The art of skill stacking. So schools taught you that you need to pick one major and do one specific job for the rest of your life, right? That is terrible advice for making real money. Our economy does not reward specialists who only know one narrow thing. The highest earners in the world use a strategy called skill stacking. You do not need to be the absolute best in the world at one skill. You just need to be in the top 20% for three or four different skills and then combine them. So instead of just being a normal graphic designer, you become a designer who also understands user psychology and direct response copywriting. That specific combination makes you incredibly rare. Research from the World Economic Forum proves that cross-functional skills are the most heavily demanded abilities in the entire global job market. So, look at your own life.
turns.zh: 技能叠加的艺术。学校教你要选择一个专业，然后一辈子做一份特定的工作，对吗？这对赚大钱来说是糟糕的建议。我们的经济不会奖励那些只知道一件狭窄事情的专业人士。世界上收入最高的人使用一种叫做技能叠加的策略。你不需要在一个技能上是世界顶尖。你只需要在三四项不同技能上达到前 20%，然后把它们结合起来。所以，与其只做一个普通平面设计师，你成为一个也理解用户心理学和直接响应文案的设计师。这种特定的组合让你非常稀缺。世界经济论坛的研究证明，跨职能技能是整个全球就业市场上需求最高的能力。所以，看看你自己的生活中。

turns.en: Take your boring corporate experience, add a little bit of marketing knowledge, and mix in your weird weekend hobby. Suddenly, you have a totally unique profile that nobody else can compete with. You stop being a commodity, and you start being a category of one. When you are the only person who can do what you do, you get to dictate your own price. But, what happens when you have these rare skills and people still refuse to pay you what you're worth? You have to master the next skill to force the market to respect your value.
turns.zh: 把你无聊的企业经验，加一点营销知识，再混入你古怪的周末爱好。突然间，你拥有了一个完全独特的个人画像，无人能及。你不再是一件商品，而成为一个独一无二的类别。当你是唯一能做你所做之事的人时，你就可以自己定价。但是，当你拥有这些稀有技能，而人们仍然拒绝支付你应得的报酬时，该怎么办？你必须掌握下一项技能，迫使市场尊重你的价值。

turns.en: Data-driven negotiations. Most people walk into a salary review or a client pitch completely driven by their emotions. They complain about how hard they work. They talk about how long that they've been at their company. They say that they need more money because their rent went up. That strategy will keep you broke forever. Businesses do not care about your personal financial stress. They only care about the value that you bring to their bottom line. So, if you want to double your income, you have to separate your self-worth from the negotiation process. You can use hard data. An analysis of 500 different salary negotiations revealed that using emotional arguments only work 8% of the time. But, when people presented a business case backed by actual market data, the success jumped to 67%. You have to do your research. Find out exactly what your specific skill stack is worth in the open market right now. Present those numbers confidently. Show the client exactly how much money your work is going to make them. When you frame your request as a smart business investment instead of a personal favor, the money will flow to you.
turns.zh: 数据驱动的谈判。大多数人走进薪资评估或客户提案时，完全被情绪驱动。他们抱怨自己工作多辛苦，谈论自己在公司待了多久，说房租涨了所以需要更多钱。这种策略会让你永远穷下去。企业不在乎你的个人财务压力，它们只在乎你为它们的底线带来的价值。所以，如果你想收入翻倍，就必须将自我价值与谈判过程分开。你可以使用硬数据。一项对 500 次薪资谈判的分析显示，使用情感论据只有 8% 的成功率。但当人们提出基于实际市场数据的商业案例时，成功率跃升至 67%。你必须做好研究，确切知道你的特定技能组合在当前公开市场上的价值。自信地展示这些数字，向客户展示你的工作将为他们赚多少钱。当你把自己的要求框定为一项明智的商业投资，而不是个人恩惠时，钱就会流向你。

turns.en: Negotiation gets you paid the right amount, but to build massive wealth that lasts decades, you need to understand the underlying pulse of your entire industry. And that brings us to skill number six. Data analysis and market research. You cannot build a million-dollar business based just off of your gut feelings alone. You have to know your actual numbers. Most people are terrified of looking at their analytics because they are afraid of seeing the ugly truth. They would rather live in denial. But, if you do not know exactly where your leads are coming from or exactly where your customers are dropping off, you are just flying blind. Data science and analysis roles offer massive salaries because the ability to read data allows companies to maximize their purchasing power and predict future trends. You do not need a fancy degree to do this. You just need to log into your dashboard and face reality. Right? When I'm trying to grow a YouTube channel, I do not just guess what people want to watch. I look at the exact click-through rates on every single thumbnail. I study the audience retention curve for the first 60 seconds of the video. You have to do the exact same thing for your business. Track your conversion rates. Track your email open rates. Double down immediately on the things that are working and ruthlessly cut out the things that are failing. Let the data show you a clearer path forward.
turns.zh: 谈判能让你获得应得的报酬，但要建立持续数十年的巨大财富，你需要理解整个行业的基本脉动。这就引出了第六项技能：数据分析和市场研究。你不能仅凭直觉就建立一个百万美元的企业。你必须了解你的实际数据。大多数人害怕查看自己的分析报告，因为他们害怕看到丑陋的真相，宁愿活在否认中。但是，如果你不知道你的潜在客户从哪里来，也不知道你的客户在哪里流失，你就是在盲目飞行。数据科学和分析职位提供高额薪资，因为读取数据的能力使公司能够最大化购买力并预测未来趋势。做这些并不需要花哨的学位，你只需要登录你的仪表盘，面对现实。对吧？当我想发展一个 YouTube 频道时，我不会仅仅猜测人们想看什么。我会查看每个缩略图的确切点击率，研究视频前 60 秒的观众留存曲线。你必须对你的企业做同样的事情。跟踪你的转化率，跟踪你的邮件打开率。立即加倍投入有效的事情，无情地砍掉失败的事情。让数据为你展示更清晰的前进道路。

turns.en: Now, you can have the best data, the best sales pitch, and the best technical skills, but you will still hit a massive income ceiling if you try to do everything yourself. This final skill is the ultimate wealth multiplier. Leadership and team building. You are the biggest bottleneck in your own life right now. You are trying to control every single tiny detail of your work because you are a perfectionist. You think nobody else can do the job as well as you can. That belief is keeping you stuck playing a very small game. The fastest way to scale your income to the moon is to stop asking how you can do a task and start asking who can do this task for you. When you transition into true leadership, your job is no longer doing the daily grind. Your job is to empower other people to do the work. Self-confidence and the ability to delegate are the absolute foundations of success for any high-level executive or business owner. You must learn the framework of eliminate, automate, delegate. First, eliminate the useless tasks that you do every day that do not actually move the needle. Second, automate everything you can using software and AI, and finally delegate the rest of the work to talented people who actually love the things that you hate doing. You have to let go of your ego, let your team make mistakes so they can learn and grow, build a culture where your people feel like the work they do actually matters. When you focus on serving your team and lifting them up, they will build your empire with you.
turns.zh: 现在，你可能拥有最好的数据、最好的销售话术和最好的技术技能，但如果你试图事事亲力亲为，你仍然会遇到巨大的收入天花板。这最后一项技能是终极财富倍增器：领导力和团队建设。你现在是自己人生中最大的瓶颈。因为你是完美主义者，试图控制工作的每一个微小细节，认为没有人能比你做得更好。这种信念让你困在一个很小的游戏里。将收入最大化到月球般高度的最快方法是，不再问自己如何完成任务，而是开始问谁可以为你完成这项任务。当你过渡到真正的领导角色时，你的工作不再是日常的苦差事，而是赋能他人去完成工作。自信和委派能力是任何高级管理者或企业主成功的绝对基础。你必须学会「消除、自动化、委派」的框架。首先，消除你每天做的那些不会带来实质性改变的无用任务。其次，尽可能用软件和 AI 自动化一切，最后将剩余工作委派给那些真正热爱你所讨厌的事情的有才华的人。你必须放下自我，让团队犯错以便他们学习和成长，建立一种文化，让你的员工觉得他们所做的工作确实重要。当你专注于服务你的团队并提升他们时，他们会与你一起建立你的帝国。

turns.en: You now have the exact seven skills you need to completely double your income this year. But all of these strategies are completely useless if you do not fix the one massive problem happening inside your head right now. Your true potential. The only thing truly holding you back from doubling your income is your own self-doubt. You have to decide today that your biggest goals are actually possible for you. Stop listening to the people who tell you to play it safe and stay small. Step into your greatness and do the work that you were put on this earth to do. And congratulations, you're one video closer to who you're meant to be. Believe. If you want to learn how to become mentally tough, financially free, and consistent every day, check the video right there next to me. I think you'll love it. Continue to believe, and I'll see you there.
turns.zh: 现在你拥有了今年收入翻倍所需的确切七项技能。但是，如果你不解决此刻你头脑中的那个巨大问题，所有这些策略都完全无用。你的真正潜力。阻止你收入翻倍的唯一真正原因是你自己的自我怀疑。你必须今天做出决定：你最大的目标对你来说实际上是可能的。不要再听那些让你安于现状、保持渺小的人的话。走进你的伟大，做你来到这个世界上应该做的工作。恭喜你，你又离那个你应该成为的人近了一步。相信吧。如果你想学习如何变得心理坚强、财务自由且每天保持自律，请点击我旁边的那个视频。我想你会喜欢的。继续相信，我们那里见。

consensus.en: AI is the biggest technical opportunity of our lifetime, enabling one person to achieve what once required teams.
consensus.zh: AI 是我们一生中最大的技术机遇，使单个人能完成过去需要团队才能做到的事。

consensus.en: Starting before feeling ready and shipping imperfect work beats waiting for perfection.
consensus.zh: 在感觉准备好之前就开始，并交付不完美的作品，胜过等待完美。

consensus.en: Focus on solving one painful expensive problem for a few high-paying clients rather than many low-paying ones.
consensus.zh: 专注于为少数高价客户解决一个痛苦且昂贵的问题，而非服务大量低价客户。

consensus.en: Model the success of others who have already achieved what you want, instead of reinventing the wheel.
consensus.zh: 模仿那些已经实现你目标的人的成功路径，而不是重新发明轮子。

consensus.en: Build relationships by giving first—interview potential partners and add value before asking for anything.
consensus.zh: 通过先给予来建立关系——先采访潜在合作伙伴并创造价值，再提出请求。

consensus.en: Protect your time by eliminating, automating, and delegating tasks that don't directly generate income.
consensus.zh: 通过消除、自动化和委派不直接产生收入的任务来保护你的时间。

contrarian.en: High intelligence often holds people back due to overthinking, perfectionism, and reliance on talent over work.
contrarian.zh: 高智商常因过度思考、完美主义和依赖天赋而非努力而阻碍人们。

contrarian.en: Diversification is a protection against ignorance—focus on one thing to win big.
contrarian.zh: 多元化是对无知的保护——专注于一件事才能取得巨大成功。

contrarian.en: The safe corporate job no longer exists; going on offense and starting your own business is the real low-risk move.
contrarian.zh: 安全的公司工作已不复存在；主动出击、自己创业才是真正的低风险选择。

contrarian.en: Perfectionism is fear in disguise; you should launch at 80% complete and iterate based on real feedback.
contrarian.zh: 完美主义是伪装起来的恐惧；你应在完成80%时推出产品，并根据真实反馈迭代。

contrarian.en: Raising venture capital is a trap—fund your business with high-paying clients instead of giving away equity.
contrarian.zh: 筹集风险资本是一个陷阱——你应该用高价客户来资助业务，而不是出让股权。

contrarian.en: Giving unsolicited advice creates friction; wait until people ask for your help before offering solutions.
contrarian.zh: 主动提供建议会制造摩擦；等到人们向你求助时再提供解决方案。
